1:1.t: Under Egypt he meant the world, and under things made with hands its idolatry, and under the shaking its subversion and dissolution. And the Lord, the Word, he represented as upon a light cloud, referring to that most pure tabernacle, in which setting up His throne, our Lord Jesus Christ came into the world to shake error.

No one, when he will have seen the Prophets to be written in verses, would think them to be bound in meter among the Hebrews, and to have anything in common with the Psalms or the works of Solomon. But what is customary to be used in Demosthenes and Cicero, as they are written in words with divisions, who certainly wrote prose and not in verses, we also, providing ease of reading, have divided a new translation with a new kind of writing. And first, knowing of Isaiah what is presented in his speech, certainly as a man noble and of urbane elegance he does not have anything of rusticity mixed into (his) speech. For this reason it happens that in comparison with others the translation was not able to preserve the flower of his speech. And then adding this, that it is being spoken not only by a prophet, but by an evangelist. For thus all the mysteries of Christ and the Church are pursued to clarity, so that you would not think them to be prophesied of the future, but they covered the history of things past. […]

Having at last, after a long time, completed the twenty books of explanations on the twelve Prophets, and the Commentaries on Daniel, you compel me, Eustochium, virgin of Christ, to pass on to Isaiah, and to render to you what I promised your holy mother Paula while she was living. I remember, indeed, that I promised it also to your brother Pammachius, a most learned man; and though you are his equal in affection, you surpass him by being present. And so I pay to you, and through you to him, what I owe, obeying the commands of Christ, who says: Search the Scriptures (John 5:39); and, Seek, and you shall find (Matt 7:7). Let me not hear, along with the Jews: You err, not knowing the Scriptures, nor the power of God (Matt 22:29). For if, according to the apostle Paul (1 Cor 1:24), Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God, and he who does not know the Scriptures does not know the power of God and his wisdom, then ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ. […]

The vision of Isaiah, the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah. For Judah, in which two tribes are signified, the Seventy and Theodotion put Judea, which denotes the whole land of the twelve tribes. And for what we have translated from the Hebrew, concerning Judah and Jerusalem, they translated, against Judea and Jerusalem. Symmachus, more plainly as is his custom, has about Judah and Jerusalem, so that he would have the title point to neither prosperous nor adverse things, but to those things which the prophetic word foretold about Judah and Jerusalem in either direction. Isaiah therefore speaks principally of two tribes, Judah and Benjamin, apart from the ten which were in Samaria and were called Ephraim and Israel, and which Pul king of the Assyrians had already begun to lay waste under Uzziah king of Judah and Jerusalem. […]

1:2.t: The one who is [begotten] from another by nature is a true child, just as Isaac was to Abraham, and Joseph was to Jacob, and as the radiance is to the sun. But those who are called children only from virtue and grace are called so not by nature but because of what they have received by grace. They still are not of the same nature as the one who gave them [the gift]. They are the ones who received the Spirit by participation, about whom it is said, "I produced and exalted children, but they rebelled against me." Of course, they were never really children by nature, and because of this and the fact that they reverted [to their former ways], the Spirit was taken away and they were disinherited. But when they again repent, God will receive them again and give them light. He will again call them children who at the beginning had been given grace.

And if they had examined with their understanding the things which were written, they would not have carefully fulfilled the prophecies which were against themselves, so as for their city to be now desolate, grace taken from them, and they themselves without the law, being no longer called children, but strangers. For thus in the Psalms was it before declared, saying, ‘The strange children have acted falsely by Me.’ And by Isaiah the prophet; ‘I have begotten and brought up children, and they have rejected Me.’

Hear, O heaven, and give ear, O earth: for the Lord has spoken. Above, it was shown by the title who the prophet was, whose son, what he saw against Judah and Jerusalem, or concerning Judah and Jerusalem, and at what time; now he summons heaven and earth to listen. By heaven he signifies the supernal and angelic powers; by earth the race of mortals, μετωνυμικῶς, naming the things contained by the things that contain them. Or else because the Lord, through Moses, had called heaven and earth as witnesses when he gave his law to the people of Israel, and had said: Attend, O heaven, and I will speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth (Deut 32:1), after the transgression of the people he calls the same again to witness, so that all the elements may know that God has been justly roused to anger in vengeance for his commandments. For heaven the Hebrew SAMAIM (שמים) sounds heavens, in the plural number, especially since he said hear, that is, SEMU (שמעו), which is expressed in the plural number, not the singular. […]

And so that we may know that hearing is more sacred than that which sounds in the ears, let us learn it from Isaiah, who says: Hear, O heaven, and perceive with your ears, O earth. Those who are old men and heavenly hear spiritually; those who dwell on the earth and are called earthly perceive with their ears. And this must be noted in all the Scriptures where these two words are placed together. We read this also in the case of Lamech, the sinner, who spoke to his wives Adah and Zillah: Hear my words, wives of Lamech, perceive my words with your ears, for I have killed a man to my wounding, and a young man to my bruising; he knew that what he was saying was obscure, and therefore he called his wives not only to the simple sound of the words, but also to the hidden understanding of what was said.

THE God of all, blaming the haughtiness of the Jews, and their constant tendency to run into disobedience, thus spoke by the voice of Isaiah; "Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth; for the Lord has spoken. I have begotten, and brought up sons; and they have rejected Me." For they rejected God the Father, by setting in manifold ways the Son at nothing, Who, though sprung from Him by nature, yet afterwards was made like unto us for our sakes: and yet He called them unto the grace that is by faith, and would have fulfilled the promise given unto their fathers. For of this the sacred Paul bears witness, where he writes, "For I say that Christ was a minister of the circumcision, to fulfil the promises of the fathers: and that the Gentiles might glorify God for mercy." The Only-begotten Word of God therefore was made man, that He might fulfil the promise of the blessing granted unto them.
1:2.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

1:3.t: For how shall we not regard it fearful, if one who knows God shall not recognize the Lord? While the ox and the donkey, stupid and foolish animals, will know one who feeds them, Israel is found to be more irrational than these? And having, by Jeremiah, complained against the people on many grounds, God adds, "They have forsaken me, says the Lord."

That was the manger of which the prophet prophesied, saying: "the ox knew its owner, and the ass the manger of its lord". The ox is a clean animal, the ass an unclean animal. "The ass knew the manger of its lord". It was not the people of Israel who knew the manger of their lord, but an unclean animal from among the Gentiles: "but Israel", he says, "has not known me, and my people has not understood me". Understanding this manger, let us strive to know the Lord and to become worthy of the knowledge of him, and to take up not only the nativity and resurrection of his flesh, but also the renowned coming of his second majesty: to whom is glory and dominion unto the ages of ages. Amen.
1:3.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 13

1:3.t: But a benefactor ranks higher than those who are loved by natural impulse. And this trait, attachment to those who have given some good, is characteristic not only of men but also of nearly all animals. “The ox knoweth his master, and the ass his lord’s crib.” God forbid that the next words should be said of us: “but Israel doth not know me, and my people did not understand.” As for the dog and many similar animals, I need not say what great goodwill they show towards those that feed them. But if we naturally choose goodwill and affection towards our benefactors, and endure every labour in order to recompense them for what they have already done; what words can worthily describe the gifts of God, which are so many as to be innumerable, and so excellent that one alone is sufficient to make us render all thanks to the Giver?

How was God known in Jewry? Was it because in Jewry it was known what His essence is? “The ox,” it is said, “knoweth his owner.” According to your argument the ox knows his lord’s essence. “And the ass his master’s crib.” So the ass knows the essence of the crib, but “Israel doth not know me.” So, according to you, Israel is found fault with for not knowing what the essence of God is. “Pour out thy wrath upon the heathen that have not known thee,” that is, who have not comprehended thy essence. But, I repeat, knowledge is manifold—it involves perception of our Creator, recognition of His wonderful works, observance of His commandments and intimate communion with Him. All this they thrust on one side and force knowledge into one single meaning, the contemplation of God’s essence.

Now then I pray you accept His Conception, and leap before Him; if not like John from the womb, yet like David, because of the resting of the Ark. Revere the enrolment on account of which thou wast written in heaven, and adore the Birth by which thou wast loosed from the chains of thy birth, and honour little Bethlehem, which hath led thee back to Paradise; and worship the manger through which thou, being without sense, wast fed by the Word. Know as Isaiah bids thee, thine Owner, like the ox, and like the ass thy Master's crib; if thou be one of those who are pure and lawful food, and who chew the cud of the word and are fit for sacrifice. Or if thou art one of those who are as yet unclean and uneatable and unfit for sacrifice, and of the gentile portion, run with the Star, and bear thy Gifts with the Magi, gold and frankincense and myrrh, as to a King, and to God, and to One Who is dead for thee.

What is more evident than that it is said of the passion of the Lord: "The ox knows his owner and the donkey his master's crib." Let us, then, know the Lord's crib where we are nourished, fed and refreshed.

[The righteous person] does not say, "My portion consists of herds of oxen, donkeys or sheep," except, perhaps, he counts himself among those herds which know their owner and wishes to consort with that donkey which does not shun the crib of Christ … [For this person] that sheep is his portion which was led to the slaughter and the "Lamb which was dumb before his shearer and did not open his mouth." In [Christ's] humiliation, judgment has been exalted.

You hear the wailing of an infant, you do not hear the lowing of the ox recognizing its Lord; the ox in fact has known its owner, and the she-ass the manger of her lord, or rather I should say praesaepium [manger], as he who made the translation wrote; for to me there is no difference in the word where there is none in the sense. For if the orator of those who pursue the trappings of speech denies that the fortunes of Greece depend on whether he used this word or that, but thinks that the matter is what must be looked to; if their very philosophers, who spend whole days in disputation, made less use of Latin and accepted words in order to use terms of their own; how much more ought we to disregard words and look to mysteries, in which plainness of speech prevails, because the miracles of the divine works, adorned by no words, have shone with the light of their own truth? Indeed, that rational she-ass was fed by the holy mangers not with the gloss of dainties but with the sap of natural nourishment. […]

He calleth the action "glory," not only for Himself the Crucified, but also for the Father; since this was the case, for not the Son only, but the Father also was glorified. For before the Crucifixion, not even the Jews knew Him; "Israel," it saith, "hath not known Me" (Isa. i. 3); but after the Crucifixion, all the world ran to Him.
1:3.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF JOHN 80

1:3.t: The ox knows his owner, and the ass his master's crib. Israel has not known, my people has not understood. For which the Seventy alone translated: But Israel has not known me, and the people has not understood me; so that, according to the others and the Hebrew, Israel did not know his owner, and the people did not understand the crib of its master. And the sense is clear: I adopted them as sons, and made them a peculiar people, my portion and the cord of my inheritance, and called them firstborn; but they did not do even what brute animals do, so as to be won over by kindnesses and to recognize their shepherd and nourisher. Nor did he compare them to dogs, which are the most sagacious kind of animal and guard their masters' houses for a little food, but to the ox and the ass, of duller sense: of which the one, drawing carts, turns the hardest clods of earth with the ploughshare, the other carries burdens and lightens men's labor in walking; […]

He who fills the world found no room in an inn. Placed in a manger, he became our food. Let the two animals, symbolic of two races, approach the manger, for "the ox knows his owner, and the donkey his master's crib." Do not be ashamed to be God's beast of burden. Carrying Christ, you will not go astray; with him burdening you, you make your way through devious paths. May the Lord rest upon us; may he direct us where he wishes; may we be his beast of burden and thus may we come to Jerusalem. Though he presses upon us, we are not crushed but lifted up; when he leads us, we shall not go astray. Through the Lord may we come to the child so that we may rejoice forever with the child who was born today.

The Leader and Shepherd of shepherds is announced to shepherds, and the food of the faithful lies in the manger of dumb beasts.… For that reason he sat upon the colt of a donkey when he entered Jerusalem amid the praises of the multitude surging around him. Let us understand; let us draw near to the manger; let us eat of this food; let us bear the Lord, our Guide and Leader, so that under his direction we may come to the heavenly Jerusalem.
The ox from the Jews, the donkey from the Gentiles; both came to the one manger and found the fodder of the Word.

Finally, whoever wishes fuller proof that mere words are nothing without actions should consider how countless peoples, by failing in good works, have lost the names given them. The twelve tribes of the Hebrews, when they were of old chosen by God, received two holy names, for they were called the people of God, and Israel. We read: "Hear, O my people, and I will speak; O Israel, and I will testify against thee." Once the Jews bore both these titles, now they have neither. They who long since left off the worship of God cannot be called God's people, nor can they who denied his Son be given a name that means "Seeing God." So it is written: "But Israel does not know, my people doth not consider."
1:3.s: On the Government of God, Book 4, Chapter 1

1:3.t: By the ox he designates the people of the Jews, who were accustomed to carry the yoke of the law and to ruminate upon its words; by the donkey he represents the people of the nations, who remained always unclean with the stains of idolatry. From both peoples a great many turned to the grace of the gospel and recognized the owner by whom they were created. [They] were seeking by means of his heavenly nourishing fare to grow toward perpetual salvation.

Hence again in Isaiah: "An ox knows its owner, and an ass, its master's manger; but Israel does not know, My people has not understood." The ox represents the order of the apostles, wherefore Paul calls himself "a Hebrew of Hebrews": for they were oxen furrowing the earth. The ass was the gentile people.

1:4.t: But when you hear the utterances of the prophets spoken as it were personally, you must not suppose that they are spoken by the inspired themselves, but by the Divine Word who moves them. For sometimes He declares things that are to come to pass, in the manner of one who foretells the future; sometimes He speaks as from the person of God the Lord and Father of all; sometimes as from the person of Christ; sometimes as from the person of the people answering the Lord or His Father, just as you can see even in your own writers, one man being the writer of the whole, but introducing the persons who converse. And this the Jews who possessed the books of the prophets did not understand, and therefore did not recognise Christ even when He came, but even hate us who say that He has come, and who prove that, as was predicted, He was crucified by them. […]

Correction is a public rebuke of sin. [God] uses it in a manner that is particularly necessary for our instruction because of the weak faith of so many. For example, he says through Isaiah, "You have forsaken the Lord, you have provoked the holy one of Israel."

Excoriation is the most vigorous expression of disapproval. God employed excoriation as a remedy when he said through Isaiah, "Ah, sinful nation, a people full of sins, an evil seed, lawless children."

For whom do Arians spare, who have spared not even their own souls? Or how can they give up their infamous actions while they persist in denying Christ our Lord the only Son of God? This is the root of their wickedness; on this foundation of sand they build up the perversity of their ways, as we find it written in the thirteenth Psalm, ‘The fool said in his heart there is no God;’ and presently follows, ‘Corrupt are they and become abominable in their works.’ Hence the Jews who denied the Son of God, deserved to be called ‘a sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evil doers, children without law.’ Why ‘without law?’—because you have deserted the Lord. And so the most blessed Paul, when he had begun not only to believe in the Son of God, but also to preach His deity, wrote, ‘I know nothing against myself.’

Hence it is that he added: And we were by nature sons of wrath, even as the rest. For when an evil will is put under nature, it becomes a nature of wrath, that is, one that must be subjected to punishment, changed not in substance but by an evil will. For what it follows is reckoned to the nature; hence he says in Isaiah: A most wicked seed (Isa. 1:4). And why it is a most wicked seed he added: For you have forsaken the Lord, he says, and have provoked the Holy One of Israel to anger; so that the nature which deserts God is called a most wicked seed. For to degenerate is to withdraw from the Author: and when it offers a bad example to the rest, it is a bad seed; for it produces the worst fruits. But if it returns to the Author, the nature will be good, according to the Apostle, who, changed when he acknowledged his Creator, is called the vessel of election (Acts 9:15).

Woe to the sinful nation, to a people heavy with iniquity, to a wicked seed, to criminal sons: they have forsaken the Lord, they have blasphemed the Holy One of Israel, they are estranged backward. What I have put last, they are estranged backward, the Seventy Translators do not have; and for they have blasphemed there is written in them, they have provoked to anger; and for a wicked seed, a most evil seed. Following which the others translated the Hebrew MEREIM (מרעים) as of the most evil, so that the fault would lie not so much in the seed (lest the nature of good and evil be thought to be different) as in the malice of those who forsook the Lord by their own will.

At the beginning of the volume is the title, recording the person, the subject and the time; in the second verse he makes the hearers attentive; in the third he relates what the Lord has spoken; in the fourth, as if in an outburst, he rebukes the sinful nation and the people full of, or heavy with, iniquity. […]

1:5.t: For whenever I hear Isaiah threaten the people of Sodom and rulers of Gomorrah, and say Why will ye be smitten any more, adding sin to sin? I am almost filled with horror, and melted to tears. It is impossible, he says, to find any blow to add to those which are past, because of your newly added sins; so completely have you run through the whole, and exhausted every form of chastisement, ever calling upon yourselves some new one by your wickedness. There is not a wound, nor bruise, nor putrefying sore; the plague affects the whole body and is incurable: for it is impossible to apply a plaster, or ointment or bandages. I pass over the rest of the threatenings, that I may not press upon you more heavily than your present plague.

Upon what shall I strike you, you who add transgression still further? By this testimony we learn that the Lord strikes those who offend for this purpose, that he may correct them once struck, and that it may be not so much a punishment as an amendment. And the sense is: I do not find what medicine I can apply to your wounds; all your limbs are full of wounds; I find no part of the body that has not already been struck. Or certainly in this way: I find no blows with which to break your hardness. For the greater the torments are, the more impiety and iniquity grow, or, as Theodotion translated, turning aside, so that you withdraw and turn aside from the Lord. Like that saying of Jeremiah: In vain have I struck your sons; you have not received discipline (Jer 2:30). Hence he speaks in anger through Hosea: I will not punish your daughters when they commit fornication, nor your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery (Hos 4:14). […]

1:6.t: But that there are certain wounds of the soul, Isaiah teaches, saying: "From the feet even to the head there is no wound nor bruise nor inflamed sore," speaking these things without doubt concerning the sins of the people, that there are some to whom a poultice of medicine can still be applied. But that others are sinners to such a degree that not even a cure can be applied to them, the same prophet designates in this manner: "There is," he says, "no poultice to apply, neither oil nor bandages."

Let your exhortations be full of meaning.… Speech is a bandage that ties up the wounds of souls, and if anyone rejects this, he shows his despair of his own salvation. Likewise, with those who are vexed by a serious sore, use the oil of speech that you may soften their hardness of heart; apply a poultice; put on a bandage of salutary advice, so that you may never allow those who are astray or who are wavering regarding the faith or the observance of discipline to perish through the loss of courage and a breakdown of activity.

From the sole of the foot to the crown of the head there is no soundness in it: wound and bruise and swelling sore. He keeps up the figure he has begun: from the feet up to the crown, that is, from the lowest to the highest, from the last to the first, they are pierced through in the whole body. Wound, he says, and bruise and swelling sore: for bodies are either livid from beatings, or swollen with blows, or gaping with wounds. We ask to what time these things should be fitted. After the Babylonian captivity, under Zerubbabel and Ezra and Nehemiah, Israel returned to Judea and recovered its ancient state. Under various princes and kings also the temple was built more magnificently, so much so that they even earned the friendship of foreign nations, of the Lacedaemonians and the Athenians and the Romans. […]

It is not bound up, nor treated with medicine, nor soothed with oil. For which the Seventy translated: It is not possible to apply a plaster, nor oil, nor bandages. To this day the wound and bruise and swelling sore of the people of Israel is not bound up with bandages, nor treated with medicine. Which Aquila translated μότωσιν, namely the lint which is laid on wounds to dry up the matter and draw out the pus. Nor soothed with oil: that their hardness might be softened by tears of repentance. For the bandages, with which the wounds of Israel are by no means bound up, the Seventy translated plaster. Israel therefore lies pierced through and cut to pieces, because he killed the physician who had come to heal the house of Israel. Hence in Jeremiah too the Angels speak τροπικῶς in the person of Babylon: We have cared for Babylon, and she is not healed (Jer 51:9), that is, the city of confusion and of vices. […]

1:7.t: And concerning its desolation, and that no one should be permitted to inhabit it, there was the following prophecy by Isaiah: "Their land is desolate, their enemies consume it before them, and none of them shall dwell therein." And that it is guarded by you lest any one dwell in it, and that death is decreed against a Jew apprehended entering it, you know very well.

Christ has ceased to be in them, speech has abandoned them, and that has been fulfilled which is written in Isaiah: "the daughter of Zion shall be left like a booth in a vineyard, and like a lodge in a cucumber-field, like a city that is stormed". These being abandoned, salvation has been transferred to the nations, that those others might be stirred up to jealousy. Beholding, therefore, the dispensation and the hidden purpose of God, how Israel has been cast off unto our salvation, we ought to take care lest perhaps those others have been cast out for our sake, and we be worthy of greater punishment — we for whose sake others also have been abandoned, and we have done nothing worthy of God's adoption and of his mercy, who adopted us and reckoned us among his own sons in Christ Jesus: to whom is glory and dominion unto the ages of ages. Amen.
1:7.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 5

1:7.t:
[Passage quoted Isa. i. 7-9.]

This great and wonderful prophet at the opening of his own book here tells us that the whole scheme of his prophecy includes a vision and a revelation against Judaea and Jerusalem, then he attacks the whole race of the Jews, first saying:

" 3. The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's manger, but Israel doth not know, my people doth not understand."

And then he laments the whole race, and adds :

"4. Woe, race of sinners, a people full of iniquity, an evil seed, unrighteous children."

Having brought these charges against them in the beginning of his book, and shewn beforehand the reasons for the later predictions that he is to bring against them, he goes on to say, "Your land is desolate," though it was not desolate at the time when he prophesied : "Your cities are burnt with fire." Nor had this yet taken place, and strangers had not devoured their land. And yet he says, "Your land, strangers devour it before your eyes," and that which follows. […]
1:7.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 2, Chapter 3

1:7.t: Isaiah lived almost [two] thousand years ago and saw Zion in a hut. The city was still standing, beautiful with public squares and clothed in honor; yet he says, "Zion shall be plowed like a field," foretelling what has been fulfilled in our day. Observe the exactness of the prophecy; for he said, "Daughter Zion will be left like a hut in a vineyard, like a shed in a melon patch." Now the place is full of melon patches.

Your land is desolate, your cities are burned with fire; strangers devour your country in your sight, and it shall be made desolate as in a devastation by enemies. These things were partly fulfilled under the Babylonians, when the temple was burned and Jerusalem overthrown, when the Samaritans took possession of the region of the ten tribes, and the land of promise was reduced to such desolation that it was laid waste by lions. But what was to come under the Roman captivity is described more fully and more perfectly: when the Roman army laid waste all Judea, and the cities were burned, and strangers at the present time devour their country, and the desolation of the Jews will continue until the end of the world. […]

1:8.t: The daughter of Zion shall be left like a shelter in a vineyard, and like a hut in a cucumber field. That all Israel is called a vineyard the same Prophet testifies in what follows, saying: For the vineyard of the Lord Sabaoth is the house of Israel, and the man of Judah his young and beloved planting (below, Isa 5:7); and in the Psalm: You have brought a vine out of Egypt; you have cast out the nations and planted it (Ps 79 [80]:9). As long as this vineyard bore the richest fruit, it had God as its keeper, of whom it is written: He who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep (Ps 120 [121]:4). But after all who passed along the way had stripped it of its grapes, and the boar out of the wood had laid it waste, the Lord left his temple and, rising up in anger, said: Arise, let us go hence; and: Your house shall be left to you desolate (Matt 23:38). And through Jeremiah: I have left my house, I have abandoned my inheritance. My inheritance has become to me like a lion in the forest; […]

1:8.s: On Hebrew Names, On Isaiah the Prophet

1:9.t: And besides, they beguile themselves and you, supposing that the everlasting kingdom will be assuredly given to those of the dispersion who are of Abraham after the flesh, although they be sinners, and faithless, and disobedient towards God, which the Scriptures have proved is not the case. For if so, Isaiah would never have said this: "And unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we would have been like Sodom and Gomorrah." And Ezekiel: "Even if Noah, and Jacob, and Daniel were to pray for sons or daughters, their request should not be granted." But neither shall the father perish for the son, nor the son for the father; but every one for his own sin, and each shall be saved for his own righteousness.

For all the Gentiles were "desolate" of the true God, serving the works of their hands; but the Jews and Samaritans, having the word of God delivered to them by the prophets, and always expecting the Christ, did not recognise Him when He came, except some few, of whom the Spirit of prophecy by Isaiah had predicted that they should be saved. He spoke as from their person: "Except the Lord had left us a seed, we should have been as Sodom and Gomorrah."

For I have proved, on the contrary, that it was prophesied that all the Gentiles would benefit by the coming of Christ, while the multitudes of the Jews would lose the promises given to their forefathers through their unbelief in Christ, few of them believing in our Lord and Saviour, and therefore attaining the promised spiritual redemption through Him.

About which the wonderful Apostle teaches something when he says :

"27. Isaiah also crieth concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand ot the sea, the remnant shall be saved : 28. For finishing the word and cutting it short in righteousness, because a word cut short will the Lord do upon the earth. 29. And as Isaiah said before, If the Lord of Sabaoth had not left to us a seed, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like to Gomorrah."

To which he adds after other things:

"1. Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. 2. […]
1:9.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 2, Chapter 3

1:9.t: "And as Esaias said before, Except the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been as Sodoma, and had been made like unto Gomorrha." Here again he shows another thing, that not even those few were saved from their own resources. For they too would have perished, and met with Sodom's fate, that is, they would have had to undergo utter destruction (for they (of Sodom) were also destroyed root and branch, and left not even the slightest remnant of themselves,) and they too, he means, would have been like these, unless God had used much kindness to them, and had saved them by faith. And this happened also in the case of the visible captivity, the majority having been taken away captive and perished, and some few only being saved.

Unless the Lord of hosts had left us a seed, we would have been as Sodom, and we would have been like Gomorrah. Paul the apostle discusses this passage more fully to the Romans, writing: I say then, has God cast away his people? God forbid: for I too am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God has not cast away his people whom he foreknew (Rom 11:1, 2). And a little later: So then at this present time also a remnant has been saved according to the election of grace (ibid., 5). From this it is shown that the foregoing threats which the prophetic word uttered against Jerusalem and Judah are not to be referred to the time of the Babylonian captivity, but to the last, the Roman one, when in the Apostles the remnant of the people of the Jews was saved, and on one day three thousand believed and on another five thousand, and the Gospel was sown in the whole world. […]

1:10.t:
And to shew that the prophecy can only refer to the time of our Saviour's coming, the words that follow the text—"unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah," naming the whole people of the Jews as the people of Gomorrah, and their rulers as the princes of Sodom—imply a rejection of the Mosaic worship, and introduce in the prediction about them the characteristics of the covenant announced to all men by our Saviour, I mean regeneration by water, and the word and law completely new. For it says :

"Hear the word of the Lord, ye rulers of Sodom, give heed to the law of God, ye people of Gomorrah, What is the multitude of your sacrifices to me?" .

and that which follows. Thus it takes away what belongs to the Mosaic law, and introduces in its place another mode of the forgiveness of sins, through the washing of salvation and the life preached in accordance with it, saying :

"Wash you, be ye clean ; […]
1:10.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 2, Chapter 3

1:10.t: Hear the word of the Lord, you princes of Sodom; give ear to the law of our God, you people of Gomorrah. Once the remnant of the people of Israel had been saved through the Apostles, the prophetic word turns to the Scribes and Pharisees and the people shouting: Crucify, crucify such a man (John 19:6), and calls them princes of Sodom and people of Gomorrah, according to what we read in what follows: They have proclaimed and displayed their iniquity like Sodom. Woe to their soul, for they have devised a most evil counsel against themselves, saying: Let us bind the righteous man, for he is unprofitable to us (below, Isa 3). Therefore they are called princes of Sodom and people of Gomorrah for this reason, that they devised a most evil counsel and bound the righteous one, and said, We have no king but Caesar (John 19:15). And again: We know that God spoke to Moses; but as for this man, we do not know who he is (John 9:29). […]

1:11.t:
Even the heathen fancy they keep festival, and the Jews hypo-critically feign to do so. But the feast of the heathen He reproves, as the bread of mourners, and He turns His face from that of the Jews, as being outcasts, saying, ‘Your new moons and your sabbaths My soul hateth.’

For actions not done lawfully and piously, are not of advantage, though they may be reputed to be so, but they rather argue hypocrisy in those who venture upon them. Therefore, although such persons feign to offer sacrifices, yet they hear from the Father, ‘Your whole burnt-offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices do not please Me; and although ye bring fine flour, it is vanity, incense also is an abomination unto Me.’ For God does not need anything; and, since nothing is unclean to Him, He is full in regard to them, as He testifies, by Isaiah, saying, ‘I am full.’

HOW HAS THE LORD IN LEVITICUS COMMANDED THAT SACRIFICES AND LIBATIONS BE OFFERED, WHICH ELSEWHERE HE REJECTS? FOR IT IS CLEAR IN LEVITICUS THAT THE LORD COMMANDED THE FATHERS TO OFFER LIBATIONS OR SACRIFICES OR BURNT OFFERINGS: YET HE SAYS THEREFORE THROUGH THE PROPHET JEREMIAH: THEREFORE SAYS THE LORD, GATHER YOUR BURNT OFFERINGS WITH YOUR SACRIFICES, AND EAT FLESH; FOR I DID NOT SPEAK TO YOUR FATHERS, NOR DID I COMMAND THEM, IN THE DAY THAT I BROUGHT THEM OUT OF THE LAND OF EGYPT (Jer. 7:21–22) ABOUT BURNT OFFERINGS AND SACRIFICES. — If you look closely, there is really no question to be raised on this matter; nor should you think the Lord lied or changed, as if he commanded and later denied. For of this kind of sacrifices and drink offerings or burnt offerings, nothing is found that he commanded, regarding those of which he now testifies that he spoke. Notice that there are two kinds of sacrifices: one which was commanded to be offered for each specific kind, and another which was called voluntary. […]
1:11.s: QUESTIONS ON THE OLD AND NEW TESTAMENTS, QUESTION 103: WHY GOD COMMANDS SACRIFICES YET ELSEWHERE REJECTS THEM

1:11.t: By saying that he does not delight in the sacrifices of the people, God is saying this: I abound in my own [sacrifice], I do not seek yours, I do not desire whole burnt offerings of rams and the fat of lambs and the blood of bulls and of goats. And do not come so into my sight.

To what purpose is the multitude of your victims to me, says the Lord? I am full. Burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fatlings, and the blood of calves and of lambs and of goats I did not want. For what is I did not want, the Seventy translated I do not want, the present tense for the past. But according to the Hebrew, God shows that he never wanted the victims of the Jews; which we read also in Psalm 49 (50): I will not take calves from your house, nor goats from your flocks: for all the wild beasts of the forests are mine, the cattle on the mountains and the oxen. I know all the birds of the sky, and the beauty of the field is with me. If I am hungry, I will not tell you: for the world is mine and the fullness thereof. Shall I eat the flesh of bulls, or shall I drink the blood of goats (Ps 49 [50]ff.)? And having rejected the ceremonies of the old Law, he passes on to the purity of the Gospel, and shows what he desires in their place: Offer to God the sacrifice of praise, and pay your vows to the Most High. […]

Then came the time of the prophets who showed them clearly that they could not be saved through the Law. Hence, in Isaiah: "Your new moons and festivals I detest. — I have had enough of whole-burnt rams and fat of fatlings; in the blood of calves, lambs and goats I find no pleasure." And they killed them, and their followers too, and they received false prophets, thus revealing their malice.

1:12.t: And what does this mean my brethren? For it is right for us to investigate the saying of the prophet, and especially on account of heretics who have turned their mind against the law. By Moses then, God gave commandment respecting sacrifices, and all the book called Leviticus is entirely taken up with the arrangement of these matters, so that He might accept the offerer. So through the Prophets, He blames him who despised these things, as disobedient to the commandment saying, ‘I have not required these at your hands. Neither did I speak to your fathers respecting sacrifices, nor command them concerning whole burnt-offerings.’ Now it is the opinion of some, that the Scriptures do not agree together, or that God, Who gave the commandment, is false. But there is no disagreement whatever, far from it, neither can the Father, Who is truth, lie; ‘for it is impossible that God should lie,’ as Paul affirms. […]

For who has required these things at your hands? Let the Ebionites hear, who think that the Law, abolished after the passion of Christ, is to be kept. Let the companions of the Ebionites hear, who decree that these things are to be observed only by the Jews and by those of the stock of the Israelite race. Victims, then, and the immolation of sacrifices were not required by God as a principal thing, but so that they should not be made to idols, and so that from carnal victims, as through a type and image, we might pass over to spiritual sacrifices. And by saying that he did not require victims, he shows that the Law is spiritual, and that all that the Jews do carnally is fulfilled by us spiritually.

You shall no more tread my court. Observe that after the Babylonian devastation the Temple was built again by Zerubbabel, and that sacrifices were offered in the Temple through a long series of years (Ezra 5). Therefore he points to the last destruction of the Temple under Vespasian and Titus, which is to last until the consummation of the world.

1:13.t: Further, He says to them, "Your new moons and your Sabbath I cannot endure." Ye perceive how He speaks: Your present Sabbaths are not acceptable to Me, but that is which I have made, [namely this,] when, giving rest to all things, I shall make a beginning of the eighth day, that is, a beginning of another world. Wherefore, also, we keep the eighth day with joyfulness, the day also on which Jesus rose again from the dead.
1:13.s: The Epistle of Barnabas, Chapter XV

1:13.t: Tell me, you who gather to church only on feast days: are the other days not festal? Are they not days of the Lord? It belongs to the Jews to observe certain rare days as solemn feasts; and therefore God says to them that "your new moons and sabbaths and the great day I do not endure. Your fasting and holidays and feast days my soul hates." God therefore hates those who think that the feast day of the Lord is on one day only.

And let the parasceve become a rigorous fast, lest we should appear to observe any Sabbath with the Jews, which Christ Himself, the Lord of the Sabbath, says by His prophets that "His soul hateth," which Sabbath He in His body abolished.
1:13.s: On the Creation of the World

1:13.t: For He that said unto backsliding Israel, "If ye offer a wheaten cake, it is vain: your incense is an abomination unto me;" not accepting their New Moons and Sabbaths and Great Day, seeing that He, being full, stands not in need of anything that is human and little, so that He should take pleasure in those who offer to Him unworthily; for He abominates the sacrifice of transgressors, even though it be a calf, as that of a dog, and their frankincense like a blasphemy; and excluding from the Temple and shaking off as defilement the hire of a harlot; whilst He gives honour to that sacrifice alone which pure hands bring unto the Most Pure, and a high and sanctified spirit. What wonder, then, if He did not accept honour from that man, offered in bad manner and from a bad motive,—He that seeth not as man seeth, nor looketh at the outward appearance, but at the hidden man, and the inward workshop of virtue or of wickedness!

Your new moons, and sabbaths, and other festivals I will not bear: your assemblies are wicked. Every gathering that does not offer spiritual sacrifices, nor hears what is sung in Psalm 50 (51), A sacrifice to God is a troubled spirit; a contrite and humbled heart God does not despise, is abominable to God. And therefore he adds and says: Your calends and your solemnities, so as to call them not his own festivals but those of the people who abuse them wickedly. And as for what the Seventy translated, fasting and idleness, we can say that that fast is accepted by God which has no idleness from good works. My soul hates. Ἀνθρωποπάθως: not that God has a soul, but he speaks in terms of our feelings.

1:14.t: Fear and patience, then, are helpers of our faith; and long-suffering and continence are things which fight on our side. While these remain pure in what respects the Lord, Wisdom, Understanding, Science, and Knowledge rejoice along with them. For He hath revealed to us by all the prophets that He needs neither sacrifices, nor burnt-offerings, nor oblations, saying thus, "What is the multitude of your sacrifices unto Me, saith the Lord? I am full of burnt-offerings, and desire not the fat of lambs, and the blood of bulls and goats, not when ye come to appear before Me: for who hath required these things at your hands? Tread no more My courts, not though ye bring with you fine flour. Incense is a vain abomination unto Me, and your new moons and sabbaths I cannot endure." He has therefore abolished these things, that the new law of our Lord Jesus Christ, which is without the yoke of necessity, might have a human oblation.
1:14.s: The Epistle of Barnabas, Chapter II

1:14.t: For the feast is not on account of the days; but for the Lord’s sake, who then suffered for us, we celebrate it, for ‘our Passover Christ, is sacrificed.’ Even as Moses, when teaching Israel not to consider the feast as pertaining to the days, but to the Lord, said, ‘It is the Lord’s Passover.’ To the Jews, when they thought they were keeping the Passover, because they persecuted the Lord, the feast was useless; since it no longer bore the name of the Lord, even according to their own testimony. It was not the Passover of the Lord, but that of the Jews. The Passover was named after the Jews, my brethren, because they denied the Lord of the Passover. On this account, the Lord, turning away His face from such a doctrine of theirs, saith, ‘Your new moons and your sabbaths My soul hateth.’

You have become a surfeit to me: I will by no means forgive your sins. For which Aquila translated, I have labored in bearing; Symmachus ἐκοπώθην ἱλασκόμενος, that is, I have grown weary of showing mercy; to show that he will by no means have mercy any longer, because it is one thing to kill the servants sent to them, another to kill the Son. This sense we read also in the prophet Hosea: Your destruction, O Israel; only in me is your help (Hos 13:9). Which is understood thus: You would perish, Israel, because you are saved not by your own merit but only by my help.

1:15.t: "What then, if I have been overtaken?" saith one. Cleanse thyself. "How, and in what way?" Weep, groan, give alms, apologize to him that is affronted, reconcile him to thyself hereby, wipe clean thy tongue, lest thou provoke God more grievously. For so if one had filled his hands with dung, and then should lay hold of thy feet, entreating thee, far from hearing him, thou wouldest rather spurn him with thy foot; how then durst thou in such sort draw nigh to God? Since in truth the tongue is the hand of them that pray, and by it we lay hold on the knees of God. Defile it not therefore, lest to thee also He say, "Though ye make many prayers, I will not hearken."
1:15.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 51:5

1:15.t: Your hands are full of blood. He makes plain the reason why God turns his eyes away from them and does not hear their multiplied prayer: because they have shed the blood of the righteous one, and the wicked husbandmen have killed the heir sent to them. Hence the Savior too says to them: Fill up, then, the measure of your fathers (Matt 23:31). For they killed the Prophets sent to them; you, slay the Son of the householder. This testimony is to be used also against those who, while their hands are full of blood from their daily deeds, join day to night in prayer.

1:16.t: The ministers of the grace of God have, by the Holy Spirit, spoken of repentance; and the Lord of all things has himself declared with an oath regarding it, "As I live, says the Lord, I desire not the death of the sinner, but rather his repentance;" [Ezekiel 33:11] adding, moreover, this gracious declaration, "Repent, O house of Israel, of your iniquity." [Ezekiel 18:30] Say to the children of my people, Though your sins reach from earth to heaven, and though they be redder than scarlet, and blacker than sack-cloth, yet if you turn to me with your whole heart, and say, Father! I will listen to you, as to a holy people. [2 Chronicles 7:14] And in another place He speaks thus: "Wash you and become clean; put away the wickedness of your souls from before my eyes; cease from your evil ways, and learn to do well; seek out judgment, deliver the oppressed, judge the fatherless, and see that justice is done to the widow; and come, and let us reason together. […]
1:16.s: Clement's First Letter to the Corinthians, Chapter 8

1:16.t: But let us venerate to-day the Baptism of Christ; and let us keep the feast well, not in pampering the belly, but rejoicing in spirit. And how shall we luxuriate? "Wash you, make you clean." If ye be scarlet with sin and less bloody, be made white as snow; if ye be red, and men bathed in blood, yet be ye brought to the whiteness of wool. Anyhow be purified, and you shall be clean (for God rejoices in nothing so much as in the amendment and salvation of man, on whose behalf is every discourse and every Sacrament), that you may be like lights in the world, a quickening force to all other men; that you may stand as perfect lights beside That great Light, and may learn the mystery of the illumination of Heaven, enlightened by the Trinity more purely and clearly, of Which even now you are receiving in a measure the One Ray from the One Godhead in Christ Jesus our Lord; to Whom be the glory and the might for ever and ever. Amen.

For the Prophet also saith, "Wash you, make you clean, put away the wickedness from your souls"; so that such a one is washed and is clean. Since then these men had cast away all wickedness from their souls, and had companied with Him with a pure mind, therefore He saith according to the word of the Prophet, "he that is washed is clean already." For in that place also It meaneth not the "washing" of water, practiced by the Jews; but the cleansing of the conscience. Be we then also clean; learn we to do well.
1:16.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF JOHN 70

1:16.t:
Wash yourselves, be clean. In place of the former victims and burnt offerings and fat of fatlings and blood of bulls and goats, and in place of incense and new moons, sabbath, feast day and fasts, calends and other solemnities, the religion of the Gospel pleases me: that you be baptized in my blood through the washing of regeneration, which alone can forgive sins. For unless one is born again of water and the spirit, he will not enter the kingdom of heaven (John 3:5). The Lord himself too, ascending to the Father: Go, he says, teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit (Matt 28:19).

Take away the evil of your thoughts from my eyes. As John the Baptist said: Brood of vipers, who showed you to flee from the wrath to come? Bear therefore fruits worthy of repentance (Matt 3:7; […]

If your sins are like scarlet, they shall be made white as snow; and if they are red like crimson, they shall be like white wool. An excellent order: for it is not enough to have said, wash yourselves, unless he adds, be clean, so that after the washing of water they may have purity of heart. For blessed are the clean of heart, for they shall see God (Matt 5:8). And when they have purity of heart, they must take away evil from their minds, not in the sight of men but in the sight of God, from whom nothing can be hidden. And what he adds, Cease to act perversely, echoes that word of the Gospel: Behold, you have been made whole; sin no more, lest something worse befall you (John 5:14). Withdrawing, then, from vices, let him learn good, and seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, support the orphan and the widow; […]

And again the prophet Isaiah speaks as in the person of God, "Wash you, make you clean; put away iniquities from your souls from before My eyes. Cease from your iniquities." Observe the exactness of the expression: for His words are, "From before My eyes put away iniquities from your souls." For the wicked do sometimes escape the eyes of men, but never can they escape those of God. It is our duty therefore, inasmuch as God sees what is secret, to put away wickedness from before His eyes.
1:16.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

1:16.t: For he neglects being clean after washing, whosoever after tears keeps not innocency of life. And they therefore are washed, but are in no wise clean, who cease not to bewail the things they have committed, but commit again things to be bewailed. Hence it is said through Isaiah, Wash you, be ye clean.

Now they ask wrongly who persevere in sins and ill-advisedly entreat the Lord to forgive them the sins they do not at all forgive [others]. He condemns such as these through [the mouth of] Isaiah.… Still, having regard for such as these, Isaiah shows in what way they can obtain what they plead for when he goes on.

1:17.t: Let us labor earnestly then to become clean; He has enjoined nothing burdensome. "Judge the fatherless, and do justice for the widow." Thou seest everywhere how great account God makes of mercy, and of standing forward in behalf of those that are wronged. These good deeds let us pursue after, and we shall be able also, by the grace of God, to attain to the blessings to come.
1:17.s: ON THE EPISTLE TO THE HEBREWS 12:4

1:17.t: And if thou hast pity on the widow, thy sins are washed away. For, "Judge," saith He, "the orphan, and plead for the widow, and come and let us reason together, saith the Lord. And if your sins be as scarlet, I will make them white as snow; and if they be as crimson, I will make them white as wool." For not even a single scar of the wounds doth He suffer to appear.

Learn to do well. Virtue, then, must be learned, and the good of nature alone does not suffice for righteousness unless one is trained by fitting disciplines (1 Pet 2:11). Jesus the son of Sirach too says something of the kind: You have desired wisdom: keep the commandments, and the Lord will give it to you. And in what follows the same Isaiah recalls: Everyone who has not learned righteousness on earth will not do truth (Isa 26:10 LXX). Righteousness, then, must be learned, and the thresholds of the masters of wisdom must be worn down.

Seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge for the orphan, defend the widow: and come, and reprove me, says the Lord. The commandments of the Gospel succeed to the victims of the Jews, and therefore provision is made for orphans and widows, so that, secure about the protection of their wives and children, martyrs may go forth to battle. And when, he says, you have done these things, reprove me if I do not render the rewards I have promised. And when he says, Seek judgment, he shows that it is not for all to judge rightly, but for those who are prudent. So too Solomon, in a vision in a dream, asked this of the Lord, that having received wisdom he might judge the people justly.

1:18.t: As many as are persuaded and believe that what we teach and say is true, and undertake to be able to live accordingly, are instructed to pray and to entreat God with fasting, for the remission of their sins that are past, we praying and fasting with them. Then they are brought by us where there is water, and are regenerated in the same manner in which we were ourselves regenerated. For, in the name of God, the Father and Lord of the universe, and of our Saviour Jesus Christ, and of the Holy Spirit, they then receive the washing with water. For Christ also said, "Except ye be born again, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven." Now, that it is impossible for those who have once been born to enter into their mothers' wombs, is manifest to all. And how those who have sinned and repent shall escape their sins, is declared by Esaias the prophet, as I wrote above; he thus speaks: "Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from your souls; learn to do well; […]
In the scarlet color he indicates the blood of the prophets; in the crimson, that of the Lord, as the brighter.

The Father will be seated, having "his garment white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool." This is spoken anthropomorphically. And the spiritual sense? That he is the King of such as are not defiled with sins. For God says, "Your sins shall be as white as snow, and shall be as wool." Wool is the emblem of forgiveness of sins, as also of innocence.

[One] who is baptized is seen to be purified both according to the law and according to the gospel. According to the law, because Moses sprinkled the blood of the lamb with a bunch of hyssop; according to the gospel, because Christ's garments were white as snow, when in the gospel he manifested the glory of his resurrection, [one] then whose guilt is remitted is made whiter than snow.

What shall I say of human judgments, since in the judgments of God the Jews are set forth as having offended the Lord in nothing more than violating what was due to widows and the rights of minors? This is proclaimed by the voices of the prophets as the cause that brought upon the Jews the penalty of rejection. This is mentioned as the only cause that will mitigate the wrath of God against their sin, if they honor the widow and execute true judgment for minors. Here also the likeness of the church is foreshadowed. You see, then, holy widows, that that office which is honored by the assistance of divine grace must not be degraded by impure desire.

Shouldest thou then have gone all lengths in wickedness, yet say unto thyself, God is loving unto men and he desires our salvation: for "though your sins be as scarlet, I will whiten you as snow," saith He; and unto the contrary habit I will change you. Let us not therefore give up in despair; for to fall is not so grievous, as to lie where we have fallen; nor to be wounded so dreadful, as after wounds to refuse healing. "For who shall boast that he has his heart chaste? or who shall say confidently that he is pure from sin?" These things I say not to make you more negligent, but to prevent your despairing.

Why adornest thou thy body, while thy soul is neglected, possessed by uncleanness? Why bestowest thou not so much thought on thy soul, as thy body? Thou oughtest to bestow greater; but anyhow, beloved, we ought to bestow equal care upon it. For tell me, if any one asked thee which thou wouldest choose, that thy body should be fresh and of good habit and surpassing in beauty, and wear mean raiment, or having the body deformed and full of diseases, to wear gold and finery; wouldest thou not much prefer to have beauty depending on the nature of thy person, than on the raiment with which thou art clothed? And wilt thou choose this in the case of thy body, but the contrary in the case of thy soul; and, when thou hast that ugly and unsightly and black, dost thou think to gain anything from golden ornaments? What madness is this! Shift this adorning within, put these necklaces about thy soul. […]
1:18.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF JOHN 69

1:18.t: Thus, it is necessary for a man that he should be not only justified when unrighteous by the grace of God,—that is, be changed from unholiness to righteousness,—when he is requited with good for his evil; but that, even after he has become justified by faith, grace should accompany him on his way, and he should lean upon it, lest he fall. On this account it is written concerning the Church herself in the book of Canticles: "Who is this that cometh up in white raiment, leaning upon her kinsman?" Made white is she who by herself alone could not be white. And by whom has she been made white except by Him who says by the prophet, "Though your sins be as purple, I will make them white as snow"? At the time, then, that she was made white, she deserved nothing good; but now that she is made white, she walketh well;—but it is only by her continuing ever to lean upon Him by whom she was made white. Wherefore, Jesus Himself, on whom she leans that was made white, said to His disciples, "Without me ye can do nothing."
1:18.s: On Grace and Free Will, Chapter 13

1:19.t: This passage means the blessings that await the flesh when in the kingdom of God it shall be renewed, and made like the angels, and waiting to obtain the things "which neither eye has seen nor ear heard, and which have not entered into the heart of man."
1:19.s: ON THE RESURRECTION OF THE FLESH 26

1:19.t: "If ye be willing and obedient," He saith, "ye shall eat the good of the land." Seest thou that there needs the will only? will—not the common wishing of the multitude—but earnest will. For I know that all are wishing to fly up to heaven even now; but it is necessary to show forth the wish by works. The merchant too wishes to get rich; but he doth not allow his wish to stop with the thought of it; no, he fits out a ship, and gets together sailors, and engages a pilot, and furnishes the vessel with all other stores, and borrows money, and crosses the sea, and goes away into a strange land, and endures many dangers, and all the rest which they know who sail the sea. So too must we show our will; for we also sail a voyage, not from land to land, but from earth to heaven.
1:19.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF JOHN 1

1:19.t: "If ye be willing, and will hearken unto me, ye shall eat the good of the land; but if ye be not willing, the sword shall devour you." But perhaps one will say, "I am willing; (and no one is so void of understanding as not to be willing;) but to will is not sufficient for me." Nay, but it is sufficient, if thou be duly willing, and do the deeds of one that is willing. But as it is, thou art not greatly willing.… For he that wills a thing as he ought, puts also his hand unto the means which lead to the object of his desire. Thus, when hunger compels thee to take nourishment, thou waitest not for the viands to come unto thee of their own accord, but omittest nothing to gather victuals together. So in thirst, and cold and all other such things, thou art industrious and duly prepared to take care of the body. Now do this in respect of God's kingdom also, and surely thou shalt obtain it.

If you are willing and will hear, you shall eat the good things of the land; if you are not willing and will not hear (or, as it has in the Hebrew) and provoke me to anger, the sword shall devour you. For the mouth of the Lord has spoken. He preserves free will, so that in either direction there may be punishment or reward, not from God's prejudgment but from the merits of each. And I think those are called the good things of the land of which we read in the psalm: I believe that I shall see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living (Ps 26 [27]:13); and: Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the land (Matt 5:3). Or certainly, because he was speaking to the Jews, who could not yet grasp spiritual things, he promises them the good things of the present age, so that, enticed at least by present things, they might do what was commanded. […]

1:20.t: And that expression, "The sword shall devour you," does not mean that the disobedient shall be slain by the sword, but the sword of God is fire, of which they who choose to do wickedly become the fuel. Wherefore He says, "The sword shall devour you: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken it." And if He had spoken concerning a sword that cuts and at once despatches, He would not have said, shall devour.

1:21.t: How has the faithful city become a harlot, full of judgment! Righteousness rested in it, but now murderers. The Hebrew word JALIN (ילין), for which the Seventy translated slept, means both rested and will rest, that is, it signifies both the past and the future tense. Hence Aquila and Theodotion too speak as of the future. And he marvels in the prophetic spirit that the city which was once faithful, or the dwelling of the faithful, has suddenly become a harlot. This can indeed be understood also of the times of Isaiah, but it is referred more fully to the passion of Christ, when all turned aside and together became unprofitable (Ps 13 [14]:3). And although Zion is not found in the Hebrew, the Seventy nevertheless added it to make the sense plainer. Now Zion is the mountain on which the city of Jerusalem was founded; after it was taken by David it was called the city of David. Nor do I doubt that there were holy men in it when it had the tabernacle of God, and afterwards when the Temple was built; […]

1:22.t: Someone who looks at what is done divinely by the Word and denies the body, or looks at what is proper to the body and denies the Word's presence in the flesh or from what is human, entertains low thoughts concerning the Word … as a Jewish vintner, mixing water with the wine, shall account the cross an offense, or as a Gentile, will deem the preaching folly.

And who is sufficient for these things? For we are not as the many, able to corrupt the word of truth, and mix the wine, which maketh glad the heart of man, with water, mix, that is, our doctrine with what is common and cheap, and debased, and stale, and tasteless, in order to turn the adulteration to our profit, and accommodate ourselves to those who meet us, and curry favor with everyone, becoming ventriloquists and chatterers, who serve their own pleasures by words uttered from the earth, and sinking into the earth, and, to gain the special good will of the multitude, injuring in the highest degree, nay, ruining ourselves, and shedding the innocent blood of simpler souls, which will be required at our hands.

Your silver is turned into dross. He speaks to the city of Zion, in which righteousness formerly rested: that its silver, namely the teaching of the Scriptures, of which we read in the Psalms, The words of the Lord are pure words, silver tried by fire, proved in the earth, refined sevenfold (Ps 11 [12]:7), is turned into dross, which in Hebrew is called SIGIM (סיגים): namely the rust of metals, or the refuse and filth that are smelted out by fire; so that, since he had named silver, he keeps the metaphor. This can also be said: that the righteous and holy men who formerly lived in the city were afterwards turned into the filth of sins.

Your innkeepers mix wine with water. For which Symmachus translated, Your wine is mixed with water. And the sense is: the Law of God, pure and sincere, and (so to speak) resting on unmixed truth (Matt 15), has been violated by the traditions of the Pharisees; as the Lord teaches more fully in the Gospel, that they had abandoned the law of God and followed the commandments of men. […]

1:23.t:
Your princes are disobedient, companions of thieves. For disobedient, Aquila translated withdrawing, Symmachus turning aside. And by princes he means the Scribes and Pharisees, who, withdrawing from the Lord, or rather leaving the path of truth, walked on a perverse road and were companions of Judas, the betrayer and thief. This indeed we too must beware of, lest, by accepting gifts from men of the world who gather riches through robberies and the tears of the wretched, we be called not so much thieves ourselves as companions of thieves, and it be said to us: You saw a thief and ran with him, and you put your portion with adulterers (Ps 49 [50]:18).

All love gifts, they follow after rewards. In the catalogue of vices are numbered also those who love gifts. He did not say, those who accept them, for this often happens out of necessity; […]

1:24.t:
Therefore says the Lord of hosts, the mighty one of Israel. For the mighty one of Israel, which all translated alike, the Seventy alone, intending I know not what, put: Woe, you mighty of Israel; which we can expound thus, by saying that the princes too and the strong are rebuked, of whom it is written: The mighty shall mightily suffer torments (Wis 6:7); and: To whom more is given, more will be required of him (Luke 12:48). And we may turn this testimony to use, whenever there is need, against princes of the Church who destroy their own dignity by their deeds.

Ah, I will be comforted over my foes, and I will avenge myself on my enemies. Again in this place too the Seventy put what is not found in the Hebrew: For my fury has not ceased against my enemies. And he rebukes the Scribes and Pharisees, of whom he also speaks in the Gospel: Woe to you, Scribes and Pharisees (Matt 23:13ff.). […]

1:25.t: "For we are not as the rest, which corrupt the word of God." `For even if we use great sounding words, yet we declared nothing to be our own that we achieved, but all Christ's. For we will not imitate the false apostles; the men who say that most is of themselves.' For this is "to corrupt," when one adulterates the wine; when one sells for money what he ought to give freely. For he seems to me to be here both taunting them in respect to money, and again hinting at the very thing I have said, as that they mingle their own things with God's; which is the charge Isaiah brings when he said, "Thy vintners mingle wine with water:" for even if this was said of wine, yet one would not err in expounding it of doctrine too. `But we,' saith he, `do not so: but such as we have been entrusted with, such do we offer you, pouring out the word undiluted.'

And I will turn my hand upon you, and I will smelt away your dross to purity, and I will take away all your tin. For dross, which is Symmachus's translation, Aquila translated στέμφυλα, that is, grape-husks, Theodotion γιγαρτῶδες, that is, grape-stone; the Seventy alone, the unbelieving or the disobedient, rendering the sense rather than the words. For since he had said above, Your silver is turned into dross, he now keeps the metaphor: that he will turn upon her, that is, stretch out his hand to punish and to purge, and smelt away all the filth and vices of sins, so that, the tin being separated, pure silver may remain; which cannot be done without fire: by which he signifies that they are to suffer torments. We read also in Malachi of the Lord: He himself will go forth like the fire of a smelter, and like fullers' herb, and he will sit smelting and cleansing as silver and gold, and he will cleanse the sons of Levi (Mal 3:2, 3); […]

But for improvement, when God chastens his righteous ones for some small and venial sins, or to raise them to a higher state of purity, and delivers them over to various trials, that He may purge away all their unclean thoughts, and, to use the prophet's word, the "dross," which he sees to have collected in their secret parts, and may thus transmit them like pure gold, to the judgment to come, as He allows nothing to remain in them for the fire of judgment to discover when hereafter it searches them with penal torments according to this saying: "Many are the tribulations of the righteous."

But we know that even saintly men have been given over in the flesh to Satan and to great afflictions for some very slight faults, since the Divine mercy will not suffer the very least spot or stain to be found in them on the day of judgment, and purges away in this world every spot of their filth, as the prophet, or rather God Himself says, in order that He may commit them to eternity as gold or silver refined and needing no penal purification. "And," says He, "I will clean purge away thy dross, and I will take away all thy tin; and after this thou shall be called the city of the just, a faithful city."
1:25.s: First Conference of Abbot Serenus, Chapter 25

1:26.t: And I will restore your judges as they were before, and your counselors as of old. In the faithful city of Zion, which afterwards became a harlot, murderers dwelt in place of the righteous one, or of righteousness. Therefore the Lord turns his hand, to smelt her to purity and take away all her tin, and to restore her judges as they were at the beginning, and her counselors as of old. The former judges were Moses and Joshua son of Nun and the others, from whom a book of holy Scripture also took its name; and afterwards David and other righteous kings. He will therefore restore the likeness of the Judges: either, after the Babylonian captivity, as the Jews would have it, Zerubbabel, Ezra and Nehemiah and the other princes who were set over the people up to Hyrcanus, whom Herod succeeded in the kingdom; or certainly, more truly and more rightly, the Apostles and those who believed through the Apostles and were appointed princes of the Churches; […]

Within the order of laymen, there is a threefold order, that is, of the holy people, the holy masters and the holy leaders. As Isaias writes, "I will restore your judges as at first." For good leaders have good masters. And good leaders together with good masters have good people, since they teach them. On the contrary, evil leaders have evil masters, and consequently, they teach the people improperly. Bad people choose bad leaders.

1:27.t: Zion shall be redeemed in judgment, and they shall bring her back into righteousness, and he shall crush the wicked and the sinners together; and those who have forsaken the Lord shall be consumed; for they shall be confounded by the idols to which they sacrificed, and you shall blush over the gardens which you had chosen. Not all will be redeemed, nor will all be saved, but the remnant, of whom it was spoken above too. And they will be brought back in righteousness when the wicked and the sinners have been crushed and those who forsook the Lord consumed. And when these have been saved, those who formerly sacrificed to idols will be confounded, and will blush in the gardens which they had chosen. And he signifies places of luxury, groves and woods.

1:28.t: Moreover, who can agree with the thesis that you [the Pelagians] set down as your next heading: "In the day of judgment, no leniency shall be shown to the ungodly and to sinners, but they shall be consumed in eternal fires," for you prevent God from showing mercy, and you pass judgment on the sentence of the judge before judgment day, so that if he wanted to spare the unjust and the sinner, he could not, in view of your prescription? For, you say, it is written in Psalm 103, "Let sinners be consumed out of the earth, and the unjust, so that they be no more." And in Isaiah: "The unjust and the sinners shall burn together, and they who abandon God shall be consumed." And do you not know that a threat on the part of God at times hints at clemency? For he does not say that they shall be consumed in everlasting fires, but rather that they shall be consumed out of the earth and shall cease to be unjust. […]

1:30.t: For they shall be like a terebinth whose leaves fall off, and like a garden, or a paradise, without water. To this day the Jews, reading the holy Scriptures, are a terebinth, or an oak, as Symmachus translated. And according to the Gospel (Matt 21) they are the fig tree that withered, on which the Lord sought fruit and, not finding it, cursed it with everlasting barrenness. But even the very leaves and fruits of words have now ceased to be among them; the watered garden too, that is, the knowledge of the Scriptures, or the paradise of various trees, which is without spiritual grace, does not bear even herbs, of which the Apostle speaks: Let him who is weak eat herbs (Rom 14:2); and with its roots dried up, all its greenness has turned to dryness and squalor.

1:31.t:
And your strength shall be like the ash of tow. For ash, Symmachus translated ἀποτίναγμα: when tow is combed, and whatever filth it has is thrown away. So all the strength and pride of the sinners and wicked of Israel, who forsook the Lord and were therefore consumed, and sacrificed to idols, and will blush in the gardens which they chose, will be reduced to the refuse of tow, which is devoured by a light fire. For there follows: And its work, that is, the work of your strength, or of the idolatry in which you had gone astray, a tiny spark will consume.

And both shall be set on fire together, and there shall be none to quench it. Both, namely, the knowledge of the Jews and all the works they do; or else both the idol and Jerusalem, in which the idol was; and when the Lord sets it on fire, no one will be able to quench it. All of which we can also take of contrary doctrines: that both masters and disciples perish alike, and all their work is food for fire.

2:1.t:
[Passage quoted Isa. iv. 2.]

And the meaning of "the remnant of Israel" the prophet himself clearly explains by the words, "All who are registered in Jerusalem, and called holy." It will be clear to you, if you run through the whole course of this section, what that day is, in which it is said God will glorify and exalt the remnant of Israel and those who are called holy and to be written in (the book of) life. For in the beginning of his complete book the prophet having seen the vision against Judah and Jerusalem, and numbered in many words the sins of the whole people of the Jews, and uttered threats and spoken about their ruin and the complete desolation of Jerusalem, brings his vision about them to an end with the words :

" 30. For they shall be as a terebinth that has cast her leaves, and as a garden without water. 31. And their strength shall be as a thread of tow, and their works as sparks of fire, and the transgressors and the sinners shall be burnt together, and there shall be none to quench them." […]
2:1.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 2, Chapter 3

2:1.t: The word which Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem. In the former Vision too, which we have already expounded, where the Seventy translated, which he saw against Judea and against Jerusalem, there is written in the Hebrew AL JUDA UJERUSALEM (על יהודה וירושלם); and in this one, which is the second, the Hebrew likewise has it. And I wonder why the Seventy Translators said in that one, against Judea and Jerusalem, and in this one about Judea and about Jerusalem; unless perhaps, because there the nation is called sinful, a people full of sins, a most evil seed, sons of iniquity, and princes of Sodom and people of Gomorrah, and a harlot city, and other things of that kind, they translated the sense rather than the word; […]

2:2.t: He calls the church a mountain when he says, "In the last days the mountain of the Lord's house shall be established."

And in the last days the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be prepared on the top of the mountains. We read of the last days in Genesis too: that Jacob, calling his sons and saying, Come, that I may announce to you what is to come in the last days (Gen 49:1), afterwards said to Judah, from whose seed Christ was born: A prince shall not fail from Judah, nor a leader from his thighs, until he comes for whom it is laid up; and he shall be the expectation of the nations. In these last days will be the last hour, of which John the Apostle speaks: My little children, it is the last hour (1 John 2:18); in which the stone cut from the mountain without hands grew into a great mountain and filled the whole earth; by which the prince of Tyre is said in Ezekiel to have been wounded (Ezek 28:16 LXX). This mountain is in the house of the Lord, for which the Prophet sighs, saying: One thing have I asked of the Lord, this will I seek: that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life (Ps 26 [27]:4); […]
