And he shall be for a sanctification to you, but for a stone of stumbling and for a rock of offense to the two houses of Israel: for a snare and for a ruin to those who dwell in Jerusalem; and very many of them shall stumble, and shall fall, and shall be broken, and shall be ensnared, and shall be taken. The Seventy translated this place thus: Thus says the Lord: With a strong hand they have withdrawn from the journey of the way of this people, saying: Lest perhaps they say, It is hard. For all that this people speaks is hard; but do not fear its fear, nor be troubled. […]

According to the Seventy, the people resisted the will of God with a strong hand, and says that all that the Lord has commanded is hard, according to what we read in the Gospel: This saying is hard; who can hear it (John 6:61)? Hence they are commanded to hear the Lord and to fear him alone.

8:13.t: And what does the prophet Symeon say of Christ? "Behold This child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel, and for a sign that shall be spoken against." For the Immanuel is set by God the Father for the foundations of Sion, "being a stone elect, chief of the corner, and honourable." Those then that trusted in Him were not ashamed: but those who were unbelieving and ignorant, and unable to perceive the mystery regarding Him, fell, and were broken in pieces. For God the Father again has somewhere said, "Behold I lay in Sion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence, and He that believeth on It shall not be ashamed; but on whomsoever It shall fall, It will winnow him." But the prophet bade the Israelites be secure, saying, "Sanctify the Lord Himself, and He shall be thy fear: and if thou trust upon Him, He shall be thy sanctification, nor shall ye strike against Him as on a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence." […]
8:13.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

8:13.t: But that the phrase, that God is hallowed by us, is a confession of our regarding Him as Holy of Holies, and does not bestow on Him any additional holiness, you may understand hence. One of the holy prophets said, "Hallow the Lord, and He shall be Your fear: and if you trust in Him, He shall be holiness unto you." Do we then make God holy? Is it the act of human nature to bestow ought on God? Does the thing made benefit the Maker? Does any man imagine that He, Who of his fulness richly distributes to the creature His gifts, will Himself receive ought of us, whose place it is to listen to the words of the blessed Paul; "What have you that you have not received? When, therefore, the prophet said, "Hallow the Lord, and He shall be your fear, and holiness to you;" we affirm that what he teaches is, 'Believe that He is holy, for then you will fear Him; and so He will thus be to you the means of holiness.'' And it is written again of Christ the Saviour of us all; "Hallow Him, Who despised Himself." […]
8:13.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

8:13.t: In the first petition of the Lord's Prayer, our sanctification is sought, and this through the gift of fear, when he says: "Our Father, who art in heaven; hallowed be thy name." Isaiah: "Sanctify the Lord of hosts, and let him be your dread and your fear."

8:14.t: On that day the Sadducees, who say that there is no resurrection, came to him. There were two heresies among the Jews, one of the Pharisees and the other of the Sadducees. The Pharisees held up a righteousness of traditions and observances, which they call deuteroses, and hence they were also called 'divided' by the people; while the Sadducees, which is interpreted 'just', themselves also claimed for themselves what they were not. And whereas the former believed and confessed the resurrection of both body and soul, and angels and spirit, the latter, according to the Acts of the Apostles, denied it all. These are the two houses of which Isaiah teaches quite plainly that they would stumble on the stone of stumbling.

He will be for a sanctification to believers, but to unbelievers for a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, that is, to the two houses of Judah and Israel; and especially for a snare and a ruin to those who dwell in Jerusalem, on whom very many will strike, and will fall, and will be broken, and, ensnared in the chains of their sins, will be led into captivity. The two houses the Nazaraeans (who receive Christ in such a way that they do not give up the observances of the old Law) interpret as two families, Shammai and Hillel, from whom arose the Scribes and Pharisees, whose school Akiba took over, whom they assert to have been the teacher of Aquila the proselyte, and after him Meir, whom Johanan the son of Zakkai succeeded, and after him Eliezer, and in order Telphon, and again Joseph the Galilean, and up to the capture of Jerusalem Joshua. […]

For if they have trusted in him, they will have him for a sanctification, and will not strike against him as against a stone of offense and as against a rock of ruin. From this place the Apostle too takes a testimony, that Christ became an offense to the Jews, but to the Gentiles foolishness (1 Cor 1:23). And again: Israel, by pursuing the law of righteousness, has not attained to the law of righteousness (Rom 9:31). Why? Because not from faith, but as if from the works of the law, they stumbled against the stone of stumbling, as it is written: Behold, I will lay in Zion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense: everyone who believes in him shall not be put to shame (ibid., 33). So those who did not receive Emmanuel, but for whom he became a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, will be broken and led captive. […]

8:16.t:
[Passage quoted, Isa. viii. 16-20 a.]

IN the Epistle to the Hebrews, the apostle, quoting the above passage, "Behold, I and the children which God has given me," expounds it of the Christ, saying, "Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself took part of the same, that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death."

And here the prophet calls God's children the Apostles, through whom he teaches that the Lord of Sabaoth, Who dwells in Mount Zion, will do signs and wonders in the house of Jacob, and that they will be manifest if sealed, as is our custom, with the seal of Christ on their foreheads, and taught no more to learn the Law of Moses, since it stands no longer, and since that which is called the house of Jacob is deserted by God.

This is rendered obscurely in the Septuagint:

"Then they shall be manifest who seal up the law, so as not to learn. And he will say, I await God, who turns his face away from the house of Jacob, and I will trust in him." […]
8:16.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 9, Chapter 14

8:16.t: Bind up the testimonies, seal the law among my disciples, and I will wait for the Lord, who hides his face from the house of Jacob, and I will look for him. The voice of the Lord speaking to the Prophet: Because, he says, the Lord has become a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense to the two houses of Israel, and they would not receive Emmanuel sent to them: Bind up the testimonies of the old Instrument, and hand them over to my disciples, who have received the Gospel, namely the Apostles, or apostolic men. Or certainly, let the law and the prophecy until John be bound up among them (Matt 11), and be shut and sealed, so that what they read they may not understand. For in place of disciples, according to the ambiguity of the Hebrew speech, we can also interpret doctrines.

Hence the Prophet answered: Because, the Gospel taking its place, the Law has been shut and sealed among the Jews, and you command that it be assigned not at all to the Jews but to the nations: therefore I will wait for Emmanuel, whom you promise is to come, of whom you said above that he himself is our dread and he himself our terror, and that he is for a sanctification to us; and I will look for the Lord who hides his face from the house of Jacob, that is, from the Jews, because they would not receive him. The Seventy translated this place thus: Then they who are sealed shall be manifest, that they may not learn the law. Which has this sense: when very many have fallen and been broken, and have struck against the stone of stumbling and the rock of offense, then those who are sealed among the people will be manifest, so that they may by no means learn the law of Moses, but obey the precepts of the Gospel.

8:18.t: "Give a wise man an occasion, and he will be the wiser," said the divine saying. Taking, then, our "occasion" from the most sacred Apostles for the understanding of the prophetic words, let us pray to God that we may receive wisdom and be able to become "the wiser" through the "occasion" of the Apostles for expounding the prophets. The Apostle, recalling this saying, "Behold, I and the children whom God has given me," then goes on and expounds: "Since therefore the children shared in blood and flesh, he too became near to them, being made a partaker of theirs, that through death he might destroy him who had the dominion of death, that is, the devil, and deliver those who through fear of death were, throughout their whole life, subject to the guilt of bondage." Therefore, "since the children were made partakers of blood and flesh," our Savior too "shared in blood and flesh." For it was foreign to his nature and his divinity to take up "blood and flesh"; […]

Then in what follows the Savior prophesies in the prophet, saying that it will come to pass that, when he has received the "children," "signs and wonders shall come to pass in Israel." For it stands thus: "And there shall be signs and wonders in Israel from the Lord of Sabaoth, who dwells on Mount Zion." For he who "dwells in" the watchtower and can behold the truth in every soul, he it is who works "signs and wonders" through the Savior, and after the Savior through the Apostles; and wherever a soul is found fit for the ministry of the "signs and portents" of God — whether according to spiritual healing or perceptibly, for exhorting to faith those who see — God, who then wrought "signs and wonders," is not idle to work them even now.

So the word that He shall send through His Christ, Who is Himself the Word and the Message, shall return to Him with great power. For when He shall come and bring it, He shall come down like rain and snow, and through Him all that is sown shall spring up and bear righteous fruit, and the word shall return to His sender; but not in vain shall His going have been, but thus shall He say in the presence of His sender:—Behold, I and the children that the Lord has given Me. And this is the voice through which the dead shall live. Concerning it our Redeemer testifies, saying:—The hour shall come when even the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of Man and shall come forth from their tombs; as it is written, In the beginning was the voice, that is the Word. Again He said, The Word became a body and dwelt amongst us. And this is that voice of God which shall sound from on high and raise up all the dead.
8:18.s: Demonstration 8 (Of the Resurrection of the Dead), Section 15

8:18.t: Behold, I and my children, whom the Lord has given me for signs and portents of Israel, from the Lord of hosts who dwells on Mount Zion. The Lord, he says, commanded me to bind up the testimony among the Jews and to hand over and seal the law for his disciples, because he had hidden his face from the house of Jacob: therefore I will look for him and wait for my Lord, and not only I, but also the children whom the Lord has given me, namely the other prophets and the sons of the prophets, who were born not of the will of the flesh and of blood, but of God (John 1:13). Of whom the Apostle too spoke: My little children, with whom I am again in travail until Christ be formed in you (Gal 4:19). And these children, that is, the prophets, were given for signs and for portents to Israel, according to what we read in Ezekiel: And Ezekiel shall be for a sign to you (Ezek 24:24). […]

8:19.t: "And if they say to you: seek out ventriloquists and those who cry out from the earth, who speak empty things, who cry out from the belly — does not a nation seek to its own God? Why do they seek the dead among the living?" Attend, for these things are spoken obscurely, and the meaning must, by God himself granting and revealing it, cohere with what went before. He teaches us therefore not to be disciples of any discourses save the heavenly and the good. For there are certain men "who speak" and who promise true teaching, who "speak" not heavenly but earthly things. "He who is of the earth speaks of the earth; he who comes from heaven is above all; what he has seen and heard, that he testifies." […]

"And if they say to you: seek out ventriloquists and those who cry out from the earth, who speak empty things." He named them "empty-speakers." Every discourse that is spoken is either empty or full of truth. Every discourse is empty which is false, but that is full of truth which has the knowledge of the God of the universe and teaches us to believe God, who promises the kingdom of heaven to his saints. See, then, what they say who were not "empty-speakers" nor ever appeared empty in the sight of the Lord God: "We have all received of his fullness." Those who are "empty-speakers" do not have "all of the fullness," but they are "all" empty of truth, empty of virtue, empty of Christ. "If they say to you: seek out those who cry out from the earth, who speak empty things, who cry out from the belly." I wish to state also the reason why the discourse has now taken up this chief one of the "ventriloquist" demons, so as to say: "If they say to you: seek out ventriloquists." […]

Now let us return to what we had begun. "If" therefore "they say to you: seek out ventriloquists and those who cry out from the earth, who speak empty things, who cry out from the belly" — "does not a nation seek to its own God?" — answer them these things; but it is said elliptically, ‘answer them these things: "does not a nation seek to its own God?"’ Every "nation," if it "seeks," refers to its own "God" what it has "sought": answer them these things. But you, O Israelites, having the true "God, who is over all," when you "seek," do not "seek out ventriloquists" nor "those who cry out from the earth" nor "empty-speakers," but your own "God." "Why do they seek the dead among the living?" For "dead" are the demons, deprived of the true "life," which says: "I am the life." Do not therefore inquire of the "dead" concerning living matters, for you have received the "law."

And when they say to you, Seek from the Pythons and from the diviners, who hiss in their incantations: does not a people inquire of its God? on behalf of the living, of the dead? To the law rather and to the testimony. But if they do not speak according to this word, there will be no morning light for them. And it shall pass through it: it shall fall and shall hunger: and when it hungers, it shall be angry, and shall curse its king and its God. And it shall look up above, and shall gaze at the earth, and behold, tribulation and darkness, dissolution, distress, and pursuing gloom: and it shall not be able to fly away from its distress. If it is the voice of the prophet Isaiah, as the Jews judge: Behold, I and my children, whom the Lord has given me for a sign and for a portent of Israel, then these things that follow too must be believed to be said by him to his disciples. […]

But, as we said above, if it is the person of Christ saying: Behold, I and my children, whom God has given me, then he himself also speaks these things to the Apostles and to the believers from the nations who have received his Gospel. If, he says, your fathers whom you have left say: seek the ventriloquists, whom we understand as pythons (such as the slave girl we read of in the Acts of the Apostles (Acts 16), who was a source of gain to her masters), and those who speak from the earth, which the magi promise to do in the calling up of souls, and the other kinds of evil arts: you ought to know this, that each nation consults its own gods and questions the dead about the welfare of the living.

But the Nazaraeans set out this place thus: When the Scribes and Pharisees tell you to listen to them, who do everything for the sake of the belly, and in the manner of magi hiss in their incantations so as to deceive you, you ought to answer them this: It is no wonder if you follow your traditions, since each nation consults its own idols. So we too ought not to consult you, the dead, about the living: rather God has given us the law and the testimonies of the Scriptures; and if you will not follow them, you will not have light, but gloom will always oppress you, which will pass through your land and doctrine: so that when those deceived by you see themselves in error and suffering a famine of truth, then they will be saddened, or angry, and will curse you, whom they used to think of as their gods and kings. And in vain will they look back to heaven and earth, since they are always in darkness and cannot fly away from your snares.

8:20.t: O you, who could not be persuaded to "seek" those things from the "ventriloquists" and "from those who cry out from the earth" empty discourses — attend to the word of truth and the "law," receiving it "for a help to your law." In your "law" it is written: "you shall not" follow "idols"; acting according to the "law," do not attend to "ventriloquists," nor to "those who cry out from the earth." "For he gave the law for a help, that they may say: not like this word, for which no gifts are to be given." For he who has taken up the "law" and has come to know that "the law is for a help" and above all "spiritual" — the law which forbids "ventriloquists" and auguries — he, when he has understood the "law," ought in wonder to say that there is no word in the world, among Greeks or Barbarians, such as is the word of the "law"; for from every word, from all teaching which promises truth, the "law" differs — the law which was given to us by God. "For he gave the law for a help, that they may say: not like this word." […]

So he teaches the disciples, and adds: to the law rather and to the testimony. If, he says, you are in doubt about anything, know that it is written: The nations which the Lord your God will destroy before your face listen to dreams and to diviners; but to you the Lord your God has not so delivered: The Lord your God will raise up for you a Prophet from your brothers, like me; him you shall hear (Deut 18:15). Hence, if you wish to know things that are doubtful, give yourselves rather to the law and to the testimonies of the Scriptures. But if your congregation will not seek the word of the Lord, it will not have the light of truth, but will move about in error and darkness.

But to you God has given the law as a help, so that you can say: the divination of the heathen, who often deceive their worshippers, is not such as ours, which is brought forth from the law without any payment. Hence the Seventy translated: Not as this word, for which there is no giving of gifts. For freely, he says, you have received, freely give (Matt 10:8).

Serenus: God at man's creation implanted in him naturally complete knowledge of the law, and if this had been kept by man, as at the beginning, according to the Lord's purposes, there would not have been any need for another law to be given, which He afterwards proclaimed in writing: for it were superfluous for an external remedy to be offered, where an internal one was still implanted and vigorous. But since this had been, as we have said, utterly corrupted by freedom and the opportunity of sinning, the severe restrictions of the law of Moses were added as the executor and vindicator of this (earlier law) and to use the expressions of Scripture, as its helper, that through fear of immediate punishment men might be kept from altogether losing the good of natural knowledge, according to the word of the prophet who says "He gave the law to help them:" and it is also described by the Apostle as having been given as a schoolmaster to little children, as it instructs and guards them to prevent them from departing through […]
8:20.s: The Second Conference of Abbot Serenus, Chapter 23

8:21.t: The light will pass through it, that is, through your congregation, or land, and you will fall, and you will hunger, and when you hunger you will be angry, according to what is written: And if they are not filled, they will murmur (Ps 58 [59]:16): and you will curse God your king, and in your necessities you will look up above to heaven and down to the earth: and behold, tribulation and darkness, dissolution of the knees, and distress of mind, and gloom of the eyes, and you will not be able to be rescued from the distress. This according to the Hebrews.

But upon the unbelievers will come a most grievous famine, not a famine of bread nor a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the word of God (Amos 8). And when you hunger you will be saddened, and will curse your prince and your fathers' traditions, that is, the devil and your ancient errors. And he says this to those who have suffered famine of the truth, and will look up above to heaven and down to the earth, and will be in distress, in darkness, and in tribulation: so that they may not see until the time when they too are converted to the Lord. These places call for a broad explanation, but we spare the size of the books, to remove the reader's weariness. These things we have touched on in part according to the translation of the Seventy, which in very many places is out of tune with the Hebrew.

9:1.t:
[Passage quoted, Isa. ix. 1-6.]

THIS also was fulfilled in our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ besides all the other prophecies, when according to the wondrous Evangelist—

[Passage quoted, Matt. iv. 12-25.]

I have quoted this passage in its entirety, because the prophecy promised that there would be a great light in Galilee, or in the land of Zabulon and Nephthalim, which are the same as Galilee. Now why did He pass most of His life in Galilee of the Gentiles? Surely that He might make a beginning of the calling of the Gentiles, for He called His disciples from thence. Wherefore, shortly after, in the same Gospel you will find that Matthew was called from Galilee, and in another Gospel, Levi also. And Philip, according to John, came from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter, which was in Galilee. The marriage too, in the same Gospel, was in Cana of Galilee, when the Lord miraculously transformed the water into wine. […]
9:1.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 9, Chapter 8

9:1.t:
"Wherefore they will wish," he says, "to have been burnt with fire, those before named for unto us a child is born, and to us a son is given, the Angel of Great Counsel." To us, that is, who in Galilee of the Gentiles have believed on Him, to whom He has brought light and joy, and the new and fresh drink of the mystery of the new Covenant: according to the prophecy which says:

"First drink this, drink quickly—land of Zabulon, and land of Nephthalim, and the rest who dwell by the coast, across Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles: O people that sat in darkness, behold a great light, and to them that sat in darkness and the shadow of death a light is risen."

These are they who from the Gentiles believed in the Christ of God, and the disciples and apostles of our Saviour, whom He called from the land of Zabulon and Nephthalim, and chose for the preachers of His Gospel. To them therefore who believed, the Angel of Great Counsel is given as a son to bring them salvation, but to them who disbelieved fire and burning.
9:1.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 7, Chapter 1

9:1.t: Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, and the rest. These were the first to hear the Lord preaching, so that where Israel's first captivity at the hands of the Assyrians had been, there the proclamation of the Redeemer should arise.

At the first time the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali was lightened: and at the last the way of the sea beyond the Jordan, of Galilee of the nations, was made heavy. The people that walked in darkness has seen a great light: to those dwelling in the region of the shadow of death, light has risen upon them. LXX: Drink this first, act quickly, region of Zebulun, land of Naphtali, and the rest of you who are by the sea beyond the Jordan, of Galilee of the nations. The people that walked in darkness has seen a great light: you who dwell in the region and shadow of death, light shall rise upon you. We have set down the double edition because the testimony is well known and was used by the Evangelist Matthew: so that either the difference of the translation or the likeness may be recognized. And first it must be noted that the Evangelist Matthew set down this testimony not according to the Seventy but according to the Hebrews. […]

9:3.t: It says, too, that the spring of their joy will be the shining of a great light, for them who before His Coming sat continually in darkness and the shadow of death. But that when the light of salvation has sprung up, they will rejoice as men rejoice in harvest, and as they who divide the spoils. And this was actually fulfilled, when our Lord and Saviour, calling His Apostles from Galilee, shewed forth to them His miracles and His teaching. The prophecy says that they will rejoice before Him, "as men rejoice in harvest." In what harvest, I ask, but that of which He spake in His teaching, "Lift up your eyes and behold the lands, that they are already white unto harvest"? By this He meant the gathering in of the Gentiles: of whom it is also said, "They shall rejoice, as they who divide the spoils." Therefore the disciples and evangelists of our Saviour, dividing between them the lands of the nations, and all the earth under heaven, despoiled the countless princes of this world, who were before rulers of the nations.
9:3.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 9, Chapter 8

9:3.t: You have multiplied the nation, you have not magnified the joy: they shall rejoice before you, as they rejoice in the harvest, as victors exult when the prey is taken, when they divide the spoils. For the yoke of its burden, and the rod of its shoulder, and the scepter of its oppressor you have overcome, as in the day of Midian. For every violent plundering is with tumult: and the garment mixed with blood shall be for burning and food for the fire. LXX: The greatest part of the people you have led down in your joy: and they shall rejoice in your sight, as they are wont to rejoice in the harvest, and as those who divide the spoils: because the yoke that was set upon them has been taken away, and the rod from their neck. For the rod of the oppressors shall be scattered, as in the day of Midian. For every robe gathered by deceit, and the garment of exchange, they shall restore: and they shall wish that they had been burned with fire. […]

The Seventy signify that not all but a certain part of the people believed: although for what they said, you have led down in joy, others have interpreted you have magnified. And while in the rest they hold the same sense, they add that he, that is, the devil, will restore the robe gathered by deceit and the exchanged garment: namely, that he is going to restore with their former ornaments all the souls which he had stripped of God's help; and not he alone, but also his satellites, the demons: who, if the choice were given them, would rather choose to perish in flames than to lose their prey.

Whatever is said in the Bible of the sun shedding light, or of other diffusions, or of banquets, is said of His bounty. Hence, in the Psalm: "The household shall divide the spoils." And in Isaiah: "They rejoice before You as men make merry when dividing spoils." These are the gifts of Christ's lavishness.

9:4.t: And we should also recognize that He says there will be another reason for their joy, viz.: their relief from the external yoke of the law, that of old was laid on them, which neither they nor their fathers were able to bear. And not only was this yoke removed from them, but the rod of the exactors which before pressed on their neck. He shews who the exactors are in another passage, where He says: "My people, your factors take your corn, and the exactors rule over you." But these men of Zabulon and Nephthalim will rejoice having seen the great light for these reasons, and they who exacted of them of old will be required to repay even to the last farthing, and repaying every garment and vestment they will be burned with fire in the day of retribution.
9:4.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 9, Chapter 8

9:4.t: But you, O Lord and Savior, have pulled from their shoulders the yoke of his burden, that is, of the devil, who before exulted in the world, who ruled over all nations, who pressed down the necks of all with the most heavy yoke of slavery; and the rod with which he struck all men and compelled them to render him their sins as a kind of tribute; and you have made those freed serve you, without any army and without shedding of blood, by a hidden hand: as once under Gideon you gave the people of Israel victory over the Midianites (Judg 7).
In the mystery of the establishment of judges, Christ is symbolized by Gedeon, of whom Isaiah speaks: "As on the day of Madian."

9:5.t: And that which follows I leave you to consider by yourself, only remarking that this Being Who is called Eternal Father, and Prince of Endless Peace, and Angel of Great Counsel is prophesied of as being begotten and becoming a child, and on His birth among men wills that they shall be burnt with fire who grudge the salvation He wins for the Gentiles, be they evil daemons, or be they wicked men, of whom He says, "That every garment and raiment wrought by guile, they will repay with interest." And who can these be, but those of whom it was elsewhere spoken in the person of our Saviour, "They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture did they cast lots "? And they who are partakers of their sin, who will also desire, when they shall see their own judgment at some future time, that they had been burnt with fire before they sinned, before the Angel of Great Counsel had been sinned against by them?
9:5.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 7, Chapter 1

9:5.t: For just as a garment that has been bloodied with human blood cannot be washed, but, stained with blood, is burned with fire, so that the stains of the foul gore perish along with the garment: so the violent plundering of the devil, and the tumult and crowds by which he had subjected the human race to himself, have been assigned to the fires of Gehenna.

9:6.t: "Unto us a child is born, and unto us a young man is given, and the government shall be upon His shoulders;" which is significant of the power of the cross, for to it, when He was crucified, He applied His shoulders, as shall be more clearly made out in the ensuing discourse.

And when Isaiah calls Him the Angel of mighty counsel, did he not foretell Him to be the Teacher of those truths which He did teach when He came [to earth]? For He alone taught openly those mighty counsels which the Father designed both for all those who have been and shall be well-pleasing to Him, and also for those who have rebelled against His will, whether men or angels.

Likewise Isaiah also says, "For unto us a child is born." But what is there unusual in this, unless he speaks of the Son of God? "To us is given he whose government is upon his shoulder." Now, what king is there who bears the ensign of his dominion upon his shoulder, and not rather upon his head as a diadem, or in his hand as a scepter, or else as a mark in some royal apparel? But the one new King of the new ages, Jesus Christ, carried on his shoulder both the power and the excellence of his new glory, even his cross; so that, according to our former prophecy, he might thenceforth reign from the tree as Lord.

He therefore is God, but begotten for this special result, that He should be God. He is also the Lord, but born for this very purpose of the Father, that He might be Lord. He is also an Angel, but He was destined of the Father as an Angel to announce the Great Counsel of God. And His divinity is thus declared, that it may not appear by any dissonance or inequality of divinity to have caused two Gods.

[Passage quoted, Isa. ix. 1-7.]

This is the third prophecy of the Child, making known the same thing in different ways. As our present object is to exhibit the manner of God's coming to men, note the number of ways in which He is shewn forth. First, He was set before us under the name of Emmanuel, God born of a Virgin; secondly, as the Child of the prophetess and the Holy Spirit, being none other than the before-named; thirdly, in the present passage, being one and the same as in the former, wherein His Name is said to be, according to the Septuagint, Angel of Great Counsel, and as some of the copies have, "Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty God, Potentate, Prince of Peace, Father of the World to Come." In the Hebrew, as Aquila says:

"For unto us a child is born, to us a son is given, and a measure was upon his shoulders. And his name was called Wonderful Counsellor, Mighty, Powerful, Father, even Prince of Peace, and of his peace there is no end."

And as Symmachus:

"For a youth is given to us, a son is given us; […]
9:6.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 7, Chapter 1

9:6.t: And all this, He says, they will suffer, because "Unto us a child is born, a son is given to us, the Angel of Great Counsel.'' Who are meant by "us," but we who have believed in Him, and all Galilee of the Gentiles, on whom the great light is sprung up? And what is this light but the Child that was born, and the Son that was given us by God, Who is named the Angel of Great Counsel, and the Prince of Peace, the Potentate, the Mighty God, and the Father of the world to come? But I have already shewn in its right place that these words can only be referred to our Lord and Saviour.
9:6.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 9, Chapter 8

9:6.t: Furthermore, we must prove that this Jesus was beforehand promised from ancient times in the Prophets, and was called the Son of God. David said:—Thou art My Son; today have I begotten Thee. Again he said:—In the glories of holiness, from the womb, from of old, have I begotten thee, a child. And Isaiah said:—Unto us a child is born, unto us a Son is given, and His government was upon His shoulder, and His Name shall be called Wonderful, and Counsellor, and mighty God of the ages, and Prince of peace. And to the increase of His government and to His peace there is no end. Therefore tell me, O wise doctor of Israel, who is He that was born and whose name was called Child and Son and Wonderful and Counsellor, the mighty God of the ages, and Prince of peace, to the increase of whose government and to whose peace (he said), there is no end? For if we call Christ the Son of God, David taught us (this); and that we call Him God, this we learned from Isaiah. And His government was laid upon His shoulder; […]
9:6.s: Demonstration 17 (Of Christ the Son of God), Section 9

9:6.t: O clap your hands together all ye people, because unto us a Child is born, and a Son given unto us, Whose Government is upon His shoulder (for with the Cross it is raised up), and His Name is called The Angel of the Great Counsel of the Father.

For we too say plainly, that the prophet, wishing to make manifest to men the mystery concerning Christ, called the Self-Existent "Angel," that the meaning of the words might not be referred to the Father, as it would have been if the title of "Existent" alone had been found throughout the discourse. But just as our word is the revealer and messenger (or "angel") of the movements of the mind, even so we affirm that the true Word that was in the beginning, when He announces the will of His own Father, is styled "Angel" (or "Messenger"), a title given to Him on account of the operation of conveying the message. And as the sublime John, having previously called Him "Word," so introduces the further truth that the Word was God, that our thoughts might not at once turn to the Father, as they would have done if the title of God had been put first, so too does the mighty Moses, after first calling Him "Angel," teach us in the words that follow that He is none other than the Self-Existent Himself, that the mystery […]

So we have in another place: "A child is born to us, and a son is given to us." In the term child there is an indication of age; in the term son a reference to the fullness of Godhead. He was made of his mother and born of the Father, but as the same person he was born and given. Do not think of two but of one. For the Son of God is one person, born of the Father and sprung from the virgin. The names differ in order but unite in one, just as the scriptural lesson just read teaches: "Man was made in her, and the Highest himself has founded her." He was man indeed in body, but the Highest in power. And while he is God and man through diversity of nature, he is the same person, not two persons, though being God and man. He has, therefore, something peculiar to his own nature and something in common with us, but in both cases he is one and in both he is perfect.

And not only did the Father send the Son but also gave him, as the Son himself gave himself. For we read, "Grace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, who gave himself for our sins." If they think that the Son was subjected to God because he was sent, they cannot deny that it was of grace that he was given. But he was given by the Father, as Isaiah said: "Unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given." But he was given by the Spirit and was sent by the Spirit. For since the prophet has not defined by whom he was given, he shows that he was given by the grace of the Trinity; and inasmuch as the Son himself gave himself, he could not be subject to himself according to his Godhead. Therefore that he was given could not be a sign of subjection in the Godhead.

Therefore, in order to call the Gentiles to the grace of his resurrection (for it is indeed a rich and fertile land that produces eternal fruits, fruits a hundred and sixty times over), he subjected his shoulder to work, subjecting himself to the cross, in order to carry our sins. And so the Prophet says: His authority is on his shoulder (Isaiah 9:6), that is, the power of divinity over the bodily passion, or the cross surpassing the body. Therefore, he placed his shoulder on the plow, enduring all insults, subjected to labor in such a way that he was wounded because of our iniquities, and weakened because of our sins.
9:6.s: On the Blessings of the Patriarchs 6.31

9:6.t: Christ, then, is the beginning of our virtue. He is the beginning of purity, who taught maidens not to look for the embraces of humanity but to yield the purity of their bodies and minds to the service of the Holy Spirit rather than to a husband. Christ is the beginning of frugality, for he became poor, though he was rich. Christ is the beginning of patience, for when he was reviled, he reviled not again. When he was struck, he did not strike back. Christ is the beginning of humility, for he took the form of a servant, though in the majesty of his power he was equal with God the Father. From him each various virtue has taken its origin.For this cause, then, that we might learn these different virtues, "a son was given us, whose beginning was upon his shoulder." That "beginning" is the Lord's cross—the beginning of strong courage, wherewith a way has been opened for the holy martyrs to enter the sufferings of the holy war.

"'Messenger' of great counsel," the Son of God is called, because of the other things which He taught, and principally because He announced the Father to men, as also now He saith, "I have manifested Thy Name unto the men." For after having said, "I have finished Thy work," He next explaineth it in detail, telling what sort of work. Now the Name indeed was well known. For Esaias said, "Ye shall swear by the true God." But what I have often told you I tell you now, that though it was known, yet it was so only to Jews, and not to all of these: but now He speaketh concerning the Gentiles. Nor doth He declare this merely, but also that they knew Him as the Father. For it is not the same thing to learn that He is Creator, and that He hath a Son.
9:6.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF JOHN 81

9:6.t: For a little child is born to us, a son is given to us: and the government is upon his shoulder; and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counselor, God, Mighty, Father of the age to come, Prince of peace. His dominion shall be multiplied, and of peace there shall be no end: upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to establish it and strengthen it in judgment and righteousness, from henceforth and for ever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will do this. LXX: For a little child is born to us, a son is given to us, whose government is upon his shoulder: and his name is called messenger of great counsel. For I will bring peace upon the princes, and his health: great is his government, and of peace there is no bound, upon the throne of David and his kingdom: to set it right and to help in judgment and righteousness: from this time now and for ever. The zeal of the Lord Sabaoth will do these things. […]

But Christ is in such manner a prophet, the Lord of prophets, as Christ is an angel, the Lord of angels. For He is also called the Angel of great counsel. Nevertheless, what says the prophet elsewhere that not an ambassador, nor an angel, but Himself coming will save them; that is, He will not send an ambassador to save them, nor an angel, but Himself will come. Who will come? The Angel himself? Certainly not by an angel will He save them, except that He is so an angel, as also Lord of angels. For angels signify messengers. If Christ brought no message, He would not be called an angel: if Christ prophesied nothing, He would not be called a prophet. He has exhorted us to faith and to laying hold of eternal life; He has proclaimed something present, foretold something future because He proclaimed the present, thence He was an angel or messenger; because He foretold the future, thence He was a prophet; and that, as the Word of God He was made flesh, thence He was Lord of angels and of prophets.

The Redeemer therefore was led to His saving passion: but they laid His cross, it says, upon Simon the Cyrenian. Another holy evangelist, however, tells us that the Lord Himself carried, the tree: and necessarily both the one and the other are true. For the Saviour indeed bore the cross, but in the middle of the way perhaps the Cyrenian met them, and they seized him, and made him carry it instead. And there is an important reason for the fact, that Christ the Saviour of all did carry the cross: for it is said of Him by the voice of Isaiah, that "to us a Child is born: a Son also is given us, Whose government is upon His shoulder." […]
9:6.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

9:6.t: And so the Lord was handed over to their savage wishes, and in mockery of His kingly state, ordered to be the bearer of His own instrument of death, that what Isaiah the prophet foresaw might be fulfilled, saying, “Behold a Child is born, and a Son is given to us whose government is upon His shoulders.” When, therefore, the Lord carried the wood of the cross which should turn for Him into the sceptre of power, it was indeed in the eyes of the wicked a mighty mockery, but to the faithful a mighty mystery was set forth, seeing that He, the glorious vanquisher of the Devil, and the strong defeater of the powers that were against Him, was carrying in noble sort the trophy of His triumph, and on the shoulders of His unconquered patience bore into all realms the adorable sign of salvation: as if even then to confirm all His followers by this mere symbol of His work, and say, “He that taketh not his cross and followeth Me, is not worthy of Me.”

Surely the entire divinely arranged plan of our Redeemer's [coming] in the flesh is the reconciliation of the world—it was for this purpose that he became incarnate, for this he suffered, for this he was raised from the dead—that he might lead us, who had incurred God's anger by sinning, back to God's peace by his act of reconciliation. Hence he was rightly given the name "Father of the world to come" and "Prince of peace" by the prophet; and the apostle, writing about him to those from among the nations who had believed, said, "And coming, he brought the good news of peace to you who were from far off and peace to those who were near, since through him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father."

Clothed in flesh, [Christ] descended into the water as "an angel of great counsel," that is, as a herald of the Father's will to Jewish people. By his deeds and his teaching he moved sinners, so that he would be killed—he who, by his bodily death, was able not only to heal those who were ailing spiritually but also to bring the dead back to life. The movement of the water, then, suggests the Lord's passion, which occurred by the Jewish nation being moved and stirred up.

"Which will be to all people," not to all the people of the Jews, nor to all the people of the nations, but to all the people who, either from the Jews or from the nations of the whole world, are brought together in one flock to one confession of Christ. From one and the same partaking of the mysteries of Christ they are called "Christian." …The light of life rose for those of us dwelling in the region of the shadow of death.

But who is the good counselor? Certainly that one of whom it is said: 'His name shall be called Wonderful, Counselor, God, the Mighty, the Father of the world to come, the Prince of Peace.' He is the Angel of great counsel: this is he to whom we ought to attend with a pure heart. Ecclesiasticus says: 'Before all works let a true word precede you, and before every act a stable counsel.' The true word, which can neither be deceived nor deceive, is the only-begotten Son of God and his doctrine and his life. Let this word precede you and this stable counsel. Stable counsel is none other than that of my God; 'the counsel of the Lord remains forever.'

Supposing I wanted to know how the Word of God can be the Restorer: Isaiah speaks of it: "A child is born to us, a son is given us; upon His shoulder dominion rests. They name Him Wonder-Counselor, God-Hero, Father-Forever, Prince of Peace." He it is who restored the hierarchy of heaven, and that below heaven which had totally fallen. Hence He must needs have touched both heaven and earth. This Hierarch had to be preeminent, endowed with awareness, acceptable to God, victorious, most generous, and just. He is called "Wonder" because He had to be preeminent in power, showing the miracle of miracles in His own Person, the plurality of natures. He is called "Counselor" because He was the best Counselor and the most wise, and from Him come forth documents of the greatest certainty. He is called "God" because He was acceptable to God, not only because in the form of God, but as God. He is called "Strong" because He overcame the world, despoiled Hades, and restored Paradise. […]

9:7.t:
Now consider yourself whether it does not overstep the limits of human nature that His peace should be said to be endless, and that He should be called Eternal Father; and also that He should be called not simply Angel, but Angel of Great Counsel, and Mighty God, and the other names in the list. And it says too that the kingdom of David will be restored by Him, which you will understand thus: there were many promises given to David, in which it was said:

"And I will set his hand in the sea, and his right hand in the rivers: he shall call upon me, Thou art my father, my God, and the helper of my salvation, And I will make him my firstborn, high above the kings of the earth. For ever I will keep my mercy for him, and my covenant shall stand firm with him, and I will make his seed for ever and ever, and his throne as the days of heaven."

And again:

"Once have I sworn by my holiness, I will not fail David, his seed shall remain for ever, and his throne is as the sun before me, and as the moon established for ever." […]
9:7.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 7, Chapter 1

9:7.t:
He says that the ground of this whole dispensation is the zeal of the Lord, "The zeal of the Lord of Sabaoth will do this." What is the character of this zeal? Is it not that recorded by Moses, where he says:

"They have provoked me to jealousy, but not according to God. They have angered me with their idols. And I will provoke them to jealousy by a nation which is not. By a foolish nation I will anger them "?
9:7.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 7, Chapter 1

9:7.t: And what follows: His dominion shall be multiplied, and of peace there shall be no end, in place of which the Seventy translated: Great is his government: we ought to know that the Hebrew word MESRA (משרה), both here and above, the Seventy interpreted ἀρχὴν, that is, government. In place of which we rendered government above, here dominion. But Aquila, deceived by the ambiguity of the word, interpreted μέτρον, that is, measure, which is called by the same name in Hebrew and in Latin. Nor can anyone doubt about the manifold dominion of the Savior and his peace, which has no end, who has read in the Psalms: Ask of me, and I will give you the nations for your inheritance, and the ends of the earth for your possession (Ps 2:8); and again: And abundance of peace, until the moon be taken away (Ps 71 [72]:7), that is, until the consummation of the age. […]

When Israel had been saved through the apostles, all the world flocked to the threshold of truth and of the peacemaker Solomon, of whom it was said, "His dominion will be increased and there will be no end of peace." For he [Christ] is "the stone broken off from the mountain," and in his earthly reign of faith, as he falls upon his enemy, he alone possesses a peaceful dominion throughout the earth.

And, indeed, just as in his divinity the Mediator between God and human beings foresaw the mother of whom he willed to be born when he should so will, so also in his humanity he chose the time that he wished for his nativity. Moreover, he himself granted that that [time] should be such as he willed, namely, that in a calm among the storm of wars a singular tranquility of unusual peace should cover the whole world.… He chose a time of utmost peace as the time when he would be born because this was the reason for his being born in the world, that he might lead the human race back to the gifts of heavenly peace.… Our Lord was born in a time of peace, so that even by the circumstance of the time he might teach that he was the very one of whom the prophecy sent before [him] spoke: "His sovereignty will be multiplied, and there will be no end of peace." […]

All these things, as the apostle teaches, "were done as an example for us" and were written down for us, and so we must scrutinize them carefully for their spiritual meaning. King Solomon, whose name means "peaceful," typologically designates our Redeemer himself, of whom Isaiah says, "His sovereignty will be increased, and there will be no end of peace." The temple that he built is his catholic church, which he gathers into the one structure of his faith and charity from all the believers throughout the world, as it were from living stones.

This voice of repentance is that of the Jewish people and of all who found in Christ access to the salvation for which they were searching. I now know with certainty that you are the one concerning whom it was said "his government will be increased and there will be no end to peace" and that you govern the kingdom in which the pure of heart will see God with unceasing happiness. I beg you, therefore, to strengthen and increase the faith that you imparted to me through the bestowal of your sacraments and heavenly gifts. Thus, having received the pledge of the Spirit, may I remain confident that you will forevermore preserve from destruction the generation of works which were begotten by my heart after the washing of my body and that you will never remove my name from the heavenly home which you deigned to grant to my fathers who, through the law, faithfully and devoutly awaited your coming.

What does the spiritual house or temple that King Solomon made for the Lord in Jerusalem signify? Solomon himself, whose name means "peaceful," is a fitting symbol of the one about whom the prophet sang, "His government will be increased, and there will be no end to peace." [This is] the same one concerning whom the apostle also wrote to the church of the Gentiles, "and he came and preached peace to you who were far off and peace to those who were near, for through him we both have access in one Spirit to the Father."That it took Solomon seven years to build the temple, which he completed and dedicated in the eighth year, was a sign that for seven years, or the entire span of the present age, the Lord would build the church as a heavenly dwelling for the gathered faithful. In the future life, however, when he appears in the glory of the resurrection, he will complete and perfect the church and raise it forevermore to the joy of life immortal in the vision of his beauty. […]

In this verse, Solomon signifies the everlasting light by "length of days," the survival of death by "years of life" and the state of happiness to be discovered by "growth in peace." Isaiah refers to the same reality when he says, "His government will be increased, and there will be no end to peace." For when the people of God are obedient to God's law, both historically and at the present time, they are enabled to live for a long time in the repose of peace.

Solomon gave the name "parables" or "metaphors" to this book [Proverbs] because he wanted us to understand it profoundly, not just according to the literal sense. He prefigures the Lord in this respect, who would speak to the crowds through parables. For just as Solomon's own name and peaceful reign foretold the enduring kingdom of Christ and of the church, concerning which it is written "his government will be increased, and there will be no end to peace upon the throne of David and his kingdom," so also did his construction and dedication of the temple artfully refer to the building of holy church, which will be dedicated for all eternity at the resurrection. The testimony of the crowds of people who greeted Christ with palm branches and praises at his entry into Jerusalem also declares him to be the son of David and the spiritual king of Israel.

Isaiah said, "His government will be increased, and there will be no end to peace upon the throne of David and his kingdom, to confirm and strengthen it in right judgment and justice."He did not say "to acquire the glory of worldly riches" or "to have victory over many peoples and cities" or "to conquer the powerful," but "to confirm it in right judgment and justice."

For it is through this that the church is strengthened and the kingdom of Christ is extended both within each of the faithful and throughout the entire world.

9:8.t: WHAT DOES IT MEAN THAT DEATH WAS SENT INTO JACOB AND CAME INTO ISRAEL, WHEN JACOB HIMSELF IS CALLED ISRAEL? — He gave two names to one people, so that from the names their merits might be understood. For the one who was surnamed Israel was previously called Jacob. Wrestling with the Savior, he realized that the one whom he saw in bodily form was God; and therefore he was called "the man seeing God" (Gen. 32:24–28). Therefore the people whom he calls Jacob, in this passage and for this reason, signifies the carnal people, in the way that names are given by parents to their offspring. But these, that is, the Jews, because of their evil deeds were not called Israelites, since they sacrificed to calves and lights in Samaria, by the zeal and command of King Jeroboam. The people, however, who in Jerusalem offered sacrifices in the temple of the Lord through the priests of God, were called Israel. Samaria therefore, because of its wickedness, was handed over to captivity and death; […]
9:8.s: QUESTIONS ON THE OLD AND NEW TESTAMENTS, QUESTION 37: WHAT DOES IT MEAN THAT DEATH WAS SENT INTO JACOB AND CAME INTO ISRAEL?

9:8.t: WHAT DOES IT MEAN THAT DEATH WAS SENT INTO JACOB, THAT IT HAS COME INTO ISRAEL, SINCE JACOB HIMSELF IS ISRAEL? — He gave two names to one people. For the one who was first called Jacob later received the name Israel, when he wrestled with the Son of God and saw Him through understanding, "the man seeing God." (Isa.9:8) Therefore the people whom he calls Jacob, in this passage and for this reason, is understood as not seeing God, but is regarded as carnal, because of its evil works: so that, just as Jacob, before he saw God Christ, was not called Israelite, so these, while they are called the people Jacob, are signified as not seeing God. Israel, however, he calls the people who, by the works of God, are made worthy to see God. Therefore the people Jacob, because it relied on carnal help, despairing of the assistance of God (for it loved idols), is given over to death, when the king of Assyria is stirred up against them. […]
9:8.s: QUESTIONS ON THE OLD AND NEW TESTAMENTS, QUESTION 13: DEATH SENT INTO JACOB AND ISRAEL

9:8.t: The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it fell upon Israel. And all the people of Ephraim shall know it, and those who dwell in Samaria, saying in pride and greatness of heart: The bricks have fallen, but we will build with squared stones; they have cut down the sycamores, but we will change them for cedars. And the Lord shall raise up the enemies of Rezin against him, and shall turn his foes into tumult, Syria from the East, and the Philistines from the West, and they shall devour Israel with whole mouth. For all this his fury is not turned away, but his hand is still stretched out, and the people has not returned to him who strikes it, and they have not sought the Lord of hosts. We read above (2 Kgs 16) that in the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah king of Judah, Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel went up to Jerusalem to take it by storm. […]

According to the anagogy, our writers expound this passage thus: God sent his Son to Jacob, that is, to the Jews; and he came to Israel, that is, to the people of the nations, whom the Apostle too says are called Israel (Rom 9). Others, however, thus: The Lord sent his Word to the Church, which supplanted the former people, and it fell upon Israel, that is, upon the heretics, who boast that they see God.

The Fifth edition and Aquila: where are your words?, for in Hebrew it is written dabarach; they read dabar, that is, word, in place of deber, which is interpreted death, according to what we read in Isaiah: The Lord sent death into Jacob, and it came into Israel, that is, deber, in place of which we translated: The Lord sent a word into Jacob, and it came into Israel, that is, dabar.

We read in Isaiah, at least according to the Seventy translators — otherwise the Hebrew has it differently —: I sent death upon Jacob, and it came upon Israel. Jacob is the name of the body being born; Israel, a name of blessing. For because he wrestled all night and conquered in the struggle, and at the rising of the morning star could say with the Apostle: The night is far spent, the day has drawn near, for this reason he received the name Israel, of one seeing God. Death, therefore, is first sent upon Jacob, so that we may mortify our members which are upon the earth, and through the mortification of the bodily members may come to the death of Israel, so that all the incitements of the passions in us may die.

For it is written, "The Lord sent a Word into Jacob, and it hath fallen upon Israel." For Jacob means one that overthrows another, and Israel, one that sees God. And what is signified by Jacob but the Jewish people, and by Israel but the Gentile world? For in that very One Whom Jacob aimed to overthrow by the death of the flesh, the Gentile world, by the eyes of faith, beheld God. And thus the Word, that was sent to Jacob, lighted upon Israel; for Him whom the Jewish people rejected when He came to them, the Gentile world at once owned and found.
9:8.s: Morals on the Book of Job 2.57

9:8.t: And Isaiah shows this: "The Lord has sent word against Jacob, it falls upon Israel." He has sent word against Jacob. Jacob is a name of nature, for He was of his seed; but it falls upon Israel: Israel is a spiritual name. We are the sons of Israel and the sons of Abraham according to the promise, for we are the imitators of Abraham's faith.

9:9.t: So the people of Ephraim and those who dwell in Samaria shall know, who because of their multitude are lifted up into pride and say: The kingdom of Judah is small, and in comparison with ours most worthless. So, while they collapse like bricks, let us build ourselves a house of squared stone. When their sycamores, which are cheap wood, have been cut down by hostile incursion, we will build up our rule with cedars, which do not rot, so that they may signify an everlasting kingdom.

So let their leaders know, and all who dwell in Samaria, that is, who say that they keep the law of God, and are in an abundance of virtues, and bear the fruits of righteousness (for this is what Ephraim means), who in the pride of their heart despise the Church, and, thinking its simplicity to be want of skill, say: In place of its bricks we will build our churches with squared and very strong stones, and in place of unfruitful trees, soon to perish, we will raise up the loftiest cedars; cedars which the Lord will crush, and which the righteous man, in the person of the wicked, relates that he saw, and their place was not found (Ps 36 [37]).

9:10.t: So the Lord says that Rezin, which means worldly wisdom, whose help Ephraim used, will be turned against him, and all his enemies will fight against him, and he will be assailed both from the East and from the West, and they will devour Israel with whole mouth. In place of which the Seventy translated: And let us build ourselves a tower: and God will dash down those who rise up against mount Zion, and will scatter his enemies. For they desire to build themselves a temple in Samaria too, in the likeness of the Temple of God; but although they have moved their feet from the East and said: Come, let us build a tower, and make ourselves a name before we are scattered (Gen 11:4), with the Lord fighting against them their agreement will be dissolved and scattered, and their tongues will be divided against one another, lest by agreeing they become worse; rather they will be destroyed by one another. And when they have been so struck and devoured by their enemies, still they will not return to the Lord; […]

Because the prophet recognized that the Jewish people would perish from the faith and because he foresaw that there would arise within the church holy apostles, through whom many of the Gentiles would be established in the strength of faith and life, he spoke with great encouragement, saying, "The stones have fallen, but we will build with square stones." Having foreseen the rise of the apostles, martyrs and doctors of the holy church, he was less troubled by the fall of the stones, which represents the judgment of the Jews, because he also saw the work of Almighty God, which is the holy church built from square stones.Four tables were built from the square stones, therefore, inasmuch as faith, life, patience and kindness were given from the lives of the saints as an example for the people to follow, that they might already have a foretaste of the table. That is, the people might know the virtues through which they can offer a sacrifice of prayer to Almighty God on the altars of their hearts. […]

9:11.t: Let all the people of Ephraim, then, and those who dwell in Samaria know this: that the Syrian, who is now its help, will go over to the enemy. Or certainly, that against the Syrian himself sudden wars of adversaries arise, and all are turned into tumult: so that against Israel Syria moves from the East, and the Philistines, that is, the Palestinians, from the West, and together they devour Israel. And when they have done these things, my hand is nonetheless stretched out, or lifted high, over Israel, and does not cease to strike them. And struck by God they will not return to him who strikes them, nor will they seek the Lord of hosts, worshiping golden calves in place of God.

9:13.t: Against them the prophet complains to the Lord, saying, "You have bruised them, and they have refused to receive correction." … Hence again the Lord says, "The people are not returned to him who has struck them." … Hence the Lord reproaches the people of Israel, captive yet not converted from their iniquity, saying, "The house of Israel is become dross to me; all these are brass, and tin, and iron and lead, in the midst of the furnace." This is as though he said unmistakably, "I wished to purify them in the fire of tribulation, and I wanted them to become silver or gold. But they have turned from me in the furnace into brass, and tin, and iron and lead, because even in tribulation they have rushed forward not to virtue but to vices." When brass is struck, it gives off a greater sound than do other metals. He … who when chastised breaks forth into sounds of murmuring has turned to brass in the midst of the furnace. Tin, however, when skillfully treated, presents the deceptive appearance of silver. […]

9:14.t: And the Lord will destroy from Israel head and tail, bending and perverting, in one day. The aged and honorable, he is the head; and the prophet who teaches falsehood, he is the tail. And those who call this people blessed shall be leading it astray, and those who are called blessed shall be cast headlong. Therefore the Lord will not rejoice over its young men, and he will not have mercy on its orphans and widows, because every one is a hypocrite and wicked, and every mouth has spoken folly. For all this his fury is not turned away, but his hand is still stretched out. For impiety is kindled like a fire: it shall devour brier and thorn, and shall be kindled in the thicket of the forest, and shall be rolled together in the pride of smoke. In the wrath of the Lord of hosts the earth has trembled, and the people shall be like food for the fire. […]

According to tropology, the Lord will take away head and tail, the greater and the lesser alike. By naming the tail, he shows that the heretics are not men but beasts of burden, which use this member to cover their dung and to keep off small creatures. And after the head he adds the tail bending and perverting, because they overturn the precepts of the law and pervert the right way.

Where the head and the tail are said through the prophet to be destroyed, it is clear that priests are designated by the head and prophets by the tail. The crown, therefore, is removed from the head when those who are seen to preside over the body of the church abandon the rewards of heavenly compensation. Once its leaders fall, normally, the army that follows them also succumbs. Hence, soon after the condemnation of the leaders, Job comments on the manifold afflictions of the church: "He destroyed me on every side, and I perish; and he has removed my hope like uprooting a tree." For the church is destroyed on every side and perishes in the persons of its sick members when those who seem to be its strength are corrupted, that is, when the crown is removed from the head because its leaders have abandoned their pursuit of eternal rewards. It is in reference to the sick who have fallen that Job then adds, fittingly: "and he removed my hope like uprooting a tree." A tree is felled by a gust of wind. […]
9:14.s: Morals on the Book of Job 14.43-44

9:15.t: Who the head is, he himself has interpreted: the aged and honorable. And who the tail is: The prophet, he says, who teaches falsehood, that is, the false prophet.

He will also destroy the aged man, because he is the head, and the false prophet, who is set in the tail, both teachers and disciples alike: the one sort who for gifts praise sinners, the other who, being praised, do not perceive their own evils nor do penance.

9:16.t: He has spoken of the leaders; now he joins the people as well to the nobles, because teachers and disciples, the learned and the unlearned crowd, will perish alike. For those who called the people blessed are seducers; and those who were called blessed, not for virtue but for gifts, will be cast headlong into death. Hence also we read above: My people, those who call you blessed lead you astray, and trip up the paths of your feet (Isa 3:12).

9:17.t: In such a people God will have mercy on no person: not on the orphan, not on the widow, because every one is a hypocrite, pretending one thing and doing another: promising chastity and living luxuriously, making a show of poverty and filling the purse. Hence he adds and says: And every mouth has spoken folly. For all these things the Lord does not cease to be angry, but still raises his hand to strike.

Therefore the Lord will not rejoice in their young men: For woe to the city whose king is a youth (Eccl 10:16). And those who have lost God as Father, or the true Lord, will not obtain mercy. For every heretic is a hypocrite, doing one thing and pretending another, and whatever he says, though it may seem to be wisdom, is nevertheless folly. For these things he stretches out his hand to punish, and the devouring flame will consume all their impieties like thorns. And words without virtues, which are compared to an unfruitful forest, will be wrapped in the pride of smoke.

9:18.t: And because they have done these things, impiety will be kindled like fire, so that the ravening flame devours not the tilled field but briers and thorns, and consumes not fruit-bearing trees but the unfruitful forest in which wild beasts dwell. For this reason it is said that the thicket of the forest, when fire is set beneath it, is rolled together in the pride and height of the smoke. For everything that is lofty and rises up on high can be called proud. In place of which the Seventy, meaning I know not what, translated: and it will devour all things round about the hills.

9:19.t: Hence also at the wrath of the Lord the earth trembled, and the people became fodder for the fire, because there was such cruelty in it that it did not spare even the dearest name of brotherhood, but, deserting and despising the right, it was sated with the things that were on the left, while it hungers for pleasures and evils, and always longs to join worse things to evil ones.

At their punishment all the ground will tremble, and the deceived peoples will be handed over to everlasting burnings, because for the sake of shameful gain they do not spare even their own, but vie with one another in taking plunder from the peoples they have deceived, leaving good things and lingering in the worst. And though they always find what is on the left, yet they are never sated with their errors, devouring the flesh of their own arm, and fighting against the Church with equal zeal. On account of luxury and pleasures and gains from the peoples they have discord among themselves, so that from one heresy two arise, and these in turn are divided into parts, so that they may lead away flocks of their own and devour the houses of widows and of sinful women, always learning and never coming to the knowledge of the truth (2 Tim 3). In all these things the fury of the Lord will not be turned away, consuming and overthrowing vices; […]

9:21.t: Manasseh and Ephraim too, who were born of one womb and begotten of the same parent, broke out into such madness that they were at odds with one another in hostile hatred. Let us read the volumes of Kings and Chronicles, and we shall find the civil wars of Samaria among themselves, while some fight for one king and others for another, and how, when their own kings had been killed, they agree on attacking Judah.

10:1.t: Woe to those who make unjust laws, and who in writing have written injustice, to oppress the poor in judgment, and to do violence to the cause of the humble of my people, that widows might be their prey, and that they might plunder the orphans. What will you do in the day of visitation, and of the calamity coming from afar? To whose help will you flee? And where will you leave your glory? that you may not be bowed down under the chain, and fall with the slain. For all these his fury is not turned away, but his hand is still stretched out. Most think that these things too are still said against the ten tribes which dwelt in Samaria, because they joined these as well to their former crimes. To us, however, it seems that the prophetic word cries out against the judges of the tribe of Judah and of Jerusalem, namely the scribes and the δευτερωτὰς, because they wrote unjust laws against the law of God, and by their traditions overturned the truth of judgment. […]

10:3.t: What shall we do in the day of visitation, with which one of the Prophets terrifies me, whether that of the righteous sentence of God against us, or that upon the mountains and hills, of which we have heard, or whatever and whenever it may be, when He will reason with us, and oppose us, and set before us those bitter accusers, our sins, comparing our wrongdoings with our benefits, and striking thought with thought, and scrutinising action with action, and calling us to account for the image which has been blurred and spoilt by wickedness, till at last He leads us away self-convicted and self-condemned, no longer able to say that we are being unjustly treated—a thought which is able even here sometimes to console in their condemnation those who are suffering.

10:5.t: And Sennacherib also said thus:—I will go up to the summit of the mountains and to the shoulders of Lebanon. I will dig and drink water and will dry up with my horses’ hoofs all the deep rivers. And because he thus exalted himself, Isaiah again said concerning him:—Why does the axe boast itself against him that cutteth with it, or the saw exalt itself against him that saweth with it, or the rod lift itself up against him that wieldeth it? For thou, Sennacherib, art the axe in the hands of Him that cuts, and thou art the saw in the hands of Him that saws, and the rod in the hand of Him that wields thee for chastisement, and thou art the staff for smiting. Thou art sent against the fickle people, and again thou art ordained against the stubborn people, that thou mayest carry away the captivity and take the spoil; and thou hast made them as the mire of the streets for all men and for all the Gentiles. […]

Woe to Assur, the rod of my fury, and he is the staff; in their hand is my indignation. Against a deceitful nation I will send him, and against the people of my fury I will give him charge, to take spoils and to seize prey, and to make it a thing trodden down like the mire of the streets. But he does not think so, and his heart does not reckon so, but his heart will be set on crushing, and on the slaughter of very many nations. For he says: Are not my princes all of them kings? Is it not: as Carchemish, so Chalanno and as Arpad, so Hamath? Is it not: as Damascus, so Samaria? As my hand found the kingdoms of the idol, so also their images from Jerusalem and from Samaria. Shall I not, as I did to Samaria and to her idols, so do to Jerusalem and to her images? Let us set down in this place the translation of the Seventy, which disagrees with the Hebrew in very many things. LXX: Woe to the Assyrians: the rod of my fury is he, in their hands; […]

10:10.t: Long ago, indeed, when the former people sinned, Judah fell away from religion and fashioned "graven images in Jerusalem," and he who was called Israel did so "in Samaria". But if now too someone should consider, out of the multitude of those sinners who are gathered together, he will not be reluctant to say that each one who makes for himself a god — whatever he reckons to be good — and serves sin, is accursed, making a "graven image" and casting a work of the craftsman's hands and setting it up in secret; for in the secret place of the heart we make many idols, if we sin. Hence the word teaches us to do penance and to "wail over the graven images" and idols that are "in Jerusalem and Samaria". And if indeed we sin, we who desire to be of the Church, we make "graven images in Jerusalem"; but if those who are established outside the Church — as heretics — sin, they make "idols in Samaria". Nevertheless God, according to his goodness, calls all to penance, saying: "Wail, you graven images in Jerusalem and in Samaria; […]

10:12.t: "But when the Lord has finished doing all things on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, he will bring judgment upon the great mind, the prince of the Assyrians, and upon the loftiness of the glory of his eyes". We are taught what shall come to be for our enemy the devil, whom the prophecy has now called a certain "great mind". For just as "the serpent was wiser than all the beasts that are upon the earth", and "the sons of this age are wiser than the sons of light in their generation", and "the steward of iniquity acted wisely" according to a wisdom that is not good, in the same way this one, who is figuratively called "the prince of the Assyrians", is a "great mind", and one may marvel at the greatness of his "mind"; which he has misused for the instructing of the wise of this world, who compose the falsehood of their sects with every appearance of truth and with all their power, and put it on display. […]

And it shall be, when the Lord has accomplished all his works on mount Zion and in Jerusalem, I will visit upon the fruit of the proud heart of the king of Assur, and upon the glory of the haughtiness of his eyes. For he said: By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom I have understood, and I have removed the bounds of the peoples, and I have plundered their princes, and like a mighty one I have pulled down those who sat on high; and my hand has found the strength of the peoples as a nest; and as eggs are gathered which have been left, so I have gathered all the earth, and there was none who moved a wing, or opened the mouth, or chirped. For fruit the Seventy translated sense, or great mind. […]

10:13.t: But let us also see how great his self-inflation is, that we may guard against it and not permit him to speak true things over us. What, then, does he say? "By my strength I will act, and by the wisdom of my understanding I will take away the borders of the nations". He reckons that by his own might he is able to accomplish in us whatever he wishes. And truly, if we are conquered and after these words we sin — if after the Church we go again into the circus and to the horse-races and to the assemblies of the Gentiles — what else happens than that he possesses us as those he has overcome? And what the devil said, "By my strength I will act," comes to pass in us who sin, as he threatened. And also, if we commit fornication after chastity of long duration, after much holiness, what else happens than that he is proved to have spoken true things over us, he who said: "By my strength I will act"? But let us look at what else this boaster promises. […]

And by the prophet, "the enemy said, I will pursue and overtake," and again by another, "I will grasp the whole world in my hand as a nest, and take it up as eggs that have been left."
