And yet our teachers here are more in number and greater. For no less than prophets and apostles and patriarchs, and all righteous men, are by us set over you as teachers in every Church. And not even so is there any profit, but if you have joined in chanting two or three Psalms, and making the accustomed prayers at random and anyhow, are so dismissed, ye think this enough for your salvation. Have ye not heard the prophet, saying (or rather God by the prophet), "This people honoreth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me?" Therefore, lest this be our case too, wipe thou out the letters, or rather the impressions, which the devil hath engraven in thy soul; […]
29:13.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF MATTHEW 11:9

29:13.t: Let us humor the Jews for a little while, and listen patiently to the absurdities of those among them who are called wise; and then we shall understand what are the Jewish fables, of men who, without the authority of Scripture, without any support of reason, invent certain fabulous animals; of whom Isaiah prophesied, saying: "This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me. But they worship me in vain, teaching the doctrines and commandments of men" (Isa. 29:13). Approving this testimony in the Gospel, the Savior convicts them of having preferred the commandments of men to the Law of God. "For God says: Honor father and mother"; but they handed down: "That whoever says to father and mother, Whatever gift is from me will profit you, shall not honor his father and his mother" (Matt. 15:3 ff.).

And the Lord said: Because this people draws near with its mouth, and glorifies me with its lips, but its heart is far from me, and they have feared me by the commandment of men and by doctrines; therefore, behold, I will proceed to cause wonder in this people by a great and astounding marvel: for wisdom shall perish from its wise men, and the understanding of its prudent men shall be hidden. LXX: And the Lord says: This people draws near to me with its mouth, and honors me with its lips, but its heart is far from me: in vain do they worship me, teaching the precepts and doctrines of men. Therefore, behold, I will proceed to remove this people: for I will remove them, and I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and hide the understanding of the prudent. The Lord used this testimony against the Pharisees in the Gospel of Matthew, saying: Why do you also transgress the commandment of God for the sake of your traditions (Matt 15:3). […]

Leah, too, got children by her handmaid, from the desire of having a numerous family. Zilpah, her handmaid, is, interpreted, an open mouth. So Leah's handmaid represents those who are spoken of in Scripture as engaging in the preaching of the gospel with open mouth, but not with open heart. Thus it is written of some: "This people honor me with their lips, but their heart is far from me." To such the apostle says: "Thou that preachest that a man should not steal, dost thou steal? Thou that sayest a man should not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery?"

You understand what I said. I called those neighbours who “drew nigh,” and at the same time “stood afar off.” For they “drew nigh” in the body, but “stood afar off” in their heart. Who were in the body so near to Him as those who lifted Him on the Cross? Who in heart so far off as those who blasphemed Him? Hear this sort of distance described by the Prophet Isaiah; observe this nearness and distance at one and the same time. “This people honours Me with their lips:” behold, with their body they draw near; “but their heart is far from Me.” The same persons are at the same time “near” and “afar off” also: with their lips they are near, in heart afar off.

29:14.t: It is of … those … who practice idle discourse that God's Scriptures say superbly: "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise and bring to nothing the cleverness of the clever."

Philosophers also declare that they pursue this virtue, but their patience is as false as is their wisdom, for how can anyone be either wise or patient unless he knows the wisdom and patience of God? For he himself warns and states concerning those who think that they are wise in this world: "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the prudence of the prudent I will reject." … Therefore, if their wisdom is not true, their patience cannot be true either. For if that man who is humble and meek is patient, and yet we see that the philosophers are not humble or meek but very pleasing to themselves, and displeasing to God by the very fact that they are pleasing to themselves, it is evident that patience is not found where there is the arrogant boldness of an affected freedom and the shameless boasting of the proud and half-naked breast.
29:14.s: Treatise IX. On the Advantage of Patience 2

29:14.t: For it is written, in Isaiah: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the understanding of the prudent I will reject (Isa. 29:14). He destroys the wisdom of the wise when he does what it denies can be done; and he rejects the understanding of the prudent when he proves that God, whom they call unconcerned, has undertaken the things that they think foolish, namely that the Son of God, incarnate of the Virgin, should be crucified for human salvation; a deed which he truly attests by power, not by words.

From my youth up until now I have spent many years in writing various works and have always tried to teach my hearers the doctrine that I have been taught publicly in church. I have not followed the philosophers in their discussions but have preferred to acquiesce in the plain words of the apostles. For I have known that it is written, "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise and will bring to nothing the understanding of the prudent," and "the foolishness of God is wiser than men." This being the case, I challenge my opponents thoroughly to sift all my past writings and, if they can find anything that is faulty in them, to bring it to light. One of two things must happen. Either my works will be found edifying and I shall confute the false charges brought against me; or they will be found blameworthy and I shall confess my error.

Therefore he threatens, according to the Seventy, that he will proceed, not to remove them to the Assyrians and Babylonians, but to scatter them through the whole world. According to the Hebrew, he says that he will cause great wonder and an astounding marvel to the people of the Jews, so as to destroy the wisdom of those who did not receive the power of God and the wisdom of God, and to hide and conceal the understanding of the prudent: that is, lest they find him who is contained in the letter. From this place the Apostle Paul, writing to the Corinthians, set down a testimony: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the understanding of the prudent I will reject (1 Cor 1:19): setting out the same sense in other words; not that God is an enemy of wisdom, of which he is the father, and through whom all wisdom among men exists; but he set it down with an addition, as it is in the Hebrew: of the wise of the people and of its prudent, that is, of the people of the Jews. […]

29:15.t: He forgets the words of the Educator: "Every man that passes beyond his own bed, who says in his soul: Who sees me? Darkness compasses me about, and the walls cover me, and no man sees my sins: whom do I fear? The Most High will not remember." Such a person is most wretched, for he fears only the human observation and thinks to hide from God. "He does not know," Scripture continues, "that the eyes of the Most High Lord are far brighter than the sun, beholding all the ways of men and looking into the most hidden parts." Another time, the Educator gives warning through Isaiah: "Woe to you who made your counsel in secret and say: Who sees us?" A light that can be seen by the senses may pass unnoticed, but that which illumines the mind cannot be ignored.

Woe to you who are deep of heart, to hide counsel from the Lord, whose works are in darkness, and they say: Who sees us, and who knows us? This thought of yours is perverse, as if the clay should think against the potter, and the work say to its maker: You did not make me; and the thing formed say to him who formed it: You do not understand. LXX: Woe to those who make deep counsel, and their works shall be in darkness, and they say: Who sees us? who shall know us, and what we are doing? shall you not be reckoned as the potter's clay? Shall the thing made say to its maker: You did not make me wisely; or the thing formed to him who formed it: You did not make me? Against the same men of whom he had said above: I will destroy the wisdom of the wise, and the understanding of the prudent I will reject, or, as the prophet writes, hide, the word of God is now also directed: those who are wise in themselves and prudent in their own sight. […]

29:16.t: This thought of yours, he says, is perverse: that you should think the maker does not know what he has made, and the Creator is ignorant of his creature; as if the clay and the work should say to the potter and its maker: You did not make me, or you did not make me well, nor do you understand your handiwork. The Apostle uses this testimony in other words in writing to the Romans, where he discusses the deep knowledge of God and seeks to refute the false charge of men: O man, who are you to answer back to God? Does the thing formed say to him who formed it: Why have you made me thus? Or has not the potter power over the same clay to make one vessel unto honor and another unto dishonor (Rom 9:20-21). In all these that rule must always be observed: the Evangelists and Apostles translated from the Hebrew into Greek as seemed good to them, without loss to the sense.

29:17.t: Is it not yet a little while, and a short time, and Lebanon shall be turned into Charmel, and Charmel shall be reckoned as a forest? And in that day the deaf shall hear the words of the book, and out of darkness and gloom the eyes of the blind shall see. And the meek shall increase their joy in the Lord, and the poor among men shall exult in the Holy One of Israel: for he who prevailed has failed. The scorner is consumed, and all who watched for iniquity have been cut down: who made men sin by a word, and tripped up him who reproved in the gate, and turned aside in vain from the righteous. Let the Jews answer, and the friends of the bare history alone, who seek not fruit on the tree but only the leaves and the shade of words, which quickly withers and perishes: how at the coming of the Lord the Savior (since from the times of Isaiah to the dispensation of the flesh he assumed is, compared with eternity, a short and little space of time) Lebanon, a mountain of Phoenicia, was turned and transferred into Mount Carmel, […]

Note that [Paul] taught Greeks in Jerusalem, and Jews in Damascus which is a Gentile city, even though this should signify that Gentiles were to be included in the city of God and Jews were to fall into the faithlessness of the Gentiles, in accordance with what Isaiah said, "Lebanon shall be changed into Carmel, and Carmel shall be regarded as a wasteland."

29:18.t: When Lebanon has been changed into Charmel, and Charmel into a forest, then those who before were deaf and could not hear the words of the prophetic book (of which we said above that all holy Scripture is called one book, as the Preacher says (Eccl 12:11): The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails fixed deep, which are given from the councils by one shepherd) shall hear, and shall speak, those to whom the Savior will say: Ephphetha, which means be opened (Mark 7). And where we translated: out of darkness and gloom the eyes of the blind shall see, whose interpretation is easy, Aquila and Theodotion and Symmachus translated: The eyes of the blind shall see darkness and gloom: to show that the mysteries of Christ were to be laid open to the people of the nations, which before was blind, according to what is said: Dark water in the clouds of the air (Ps 17 [18]:12). And in the same psalm it is written of God: He made darkness his hiding place (ibid., 12). […]

Neither was heaven created in any six-day period and the stars illuminated and the dry land separated from the water and the trees and vegetation planted. Rather, Scripture customarily uses "day" to denote an unspecified period of time, as the apostle did when he said, "Behold, this is the day of salvation." He was not referring to a particular day but to the entirety of the time of the present life in which we labor for eternal salvation. The prophet also spoke not of one specific day but of numerous moments of divine grace, saying, "In that day, the deaf will hear the words of this book." Moreover, it is difficult to understand how in one day God made heaven and earth and all the brush of the field and every plant of every region, unless we say that all creatures were created simultaneously in formless matter, according to which it is written: "He who lives forever created all things together."

29:19.t: When those who were before blind have either beheld all the mystical things, or have lifted their eyes from blindness and darkness to see, so that the true light may rise for those who sit in darkness and the shadow of death: then the meek, of whom it is written: Blessed are the meek, for they shall possess the earth (Matt 5:4); or the poor, whose prince says in the psalms: This poor man cried, and the Lord heard him (Ps 33 [34]:7); and: who shall judge the poor of the people, and shall save the sons of the poor (Ps 71 [72]:4), of whom it is said to the Jews: You have despised the counsel of the poor man: these shall increase their joy in the Lord, so that he who glories may glory in the Lord (2 Cor 10); and the poor among men, or those despaired of and despised by men, who before had no knowledge of the Law, shall exult in the Holy One of Israel, who says: Be holy, for I am holy (Lev 11:44).

29:20.t: And there is every exultation, because he who prevailed has failed. The scorner is consumed, or the arrogant and proud one, who had said: By strength I will do it, and by wisdom; I will remove the bounds of the nations and lay waste their strength; who mocked all, so much so that the saint too said: My loins are filled with illusions (Ps 37 [38]:8). And all who watched for iniquity have been cut down, or destroyed, whose destruction, because of their evil watchings, does not slumber: who made the whole race of men sin by a word of blasphemy, so that they denied the Word of God and set their mouth against heaven. He means the demons, who, wicked themselves, made all men sin in speech, blaspheming with various dogmas; and as far as in them lay they tripped up him who reproved in the gate and in judgment, and made him turn aside from righteousness, who was in the gates of the daughter of Zion, lifted up from the gates of death; and who rebuked those who hated him who reproved in the gates. […]

29:22.t: What at the beginning of the chapter we translated according to the Hebrew: Thus says the Lord to the house of Jacob, he who redeemed once Abraham, and brought him out of the Chaldeans, and led him into the land of promise (Gen 11), is perfectly plain. But what the Seventy translated: Thus says the Lord concerning the house of Jacob, which he separated from Abraham, can be understood thus: that he separated the scribes and Pharisees, who blasphemed the Lord, from Abraham, who saw the day of the Lord and rejoiced (John 8). For if they had been sons of Abraham, they would have done the works of Abraham. And the Apostle argues that those are to be called sons of Abraham (Heb 11) who have the likeness of Abraham's faith, that is, the people of the nations, which was called the son of Abraham not from works but from faith.

Therefore thus says the Lord to the house of Jacob, he who redeemed Abraham: Jacob shall not now be confounded, nor shall his face now blush: but when he sees his sons, the works of my hands, in his midst sanctifying my name: and they shall sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall proclaim the God of Israel; and those who err in spirit shall know understanding, and the mutterers shall learn the Law. LXX: Therefore thus says the Lord concerning the house of Jacob, which he separated from Abraham: Jacob shall not now be confounded, nor shall he now change his face; but when he sees his sons, my works: for my sake they shall sanctify my name, and they shall sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall fear the God of Israel; and those who err in spirit shall know understanding, and the mutterers shall learn obedience; and what follows, ÷ and the stammering tongues shall learn to speak peace ⁚, is to be marked with an obelus. […]

30:1.t: Reprimand is disapproval expressed in correction or strongly worded blame. The Educator resorts to this method of training when he says through Isaiah, "Woe to you, apostate children, says the Lord, that you would take counsel and not of me, and make treaties and not of my Spirit." He flavors each pronouncement in turn with the tart spice of fear to whet the appetite of his people for salvation and make them more aware of it, just as wool to be dyed is usually steeped first in an astringent to prepare it to preserve the dye.

Let every man and woman among us, whether meeting together at church, or remaining at home, call upon God with much earnestness, and He will doubtless accede to these petitions. Whence does this appear evident? Because He is exceedingly desirous, that we should always take refuge in Him, and in everything make our requests unto Him; and do nothing and speak nothing without Him. For men, when we trouble them repeatedly concerning our affairs, become slothful and evasive, and conduct themselves unpleasantly towards us; but with God it is quite the reverse. Not when we apply to him continually respecting our affairs, but when we fail to do so, then is he especially displeased. Hear at least what He reproves the Jews for, when He says, "Ye have taken counsel, but not of Me, and made treaties, but not by My Spirit." For this is the custom of those who love; they desire that all the concerns of their beloved should be accomplished by means of themselves; […]

Woe, you deserting sons, says the Lord: that you should take counsel, and not from me; and weave a web, and not by my Spirit; that you might add sin upon sin. You who walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked my mouth, hoping for help in the strength of Pharaoh, and having confidence in the shadow of Egypt. And the strength of Pharaoh shall be to you for confusion, and the confidence in the shadow of Egypt for disgrace. For your princes shall be in Tanis, and your messengers have come as far as Hanes. All are confounded over a people that will not be able to profit them: they were not for help nor for any use, but for confusion and for reproach. LXX: Woe, you transgressing sons, says the Lord. You have taken counsel, and not through me; and a pact, not through my spirit, that you might add sins to sins: you who go to go down into Egypt, and have not asked me, that you may receive help from Pharaoh and be protected by the Egyptians. […]

Some think this place was written against the ten tribes in Samaria, because, seeking help from the Egyptians, they were taken captive by the Assyrians. According to tropology: all who, despising the religion of God, return to their vomit, and, having lost the name of sons, are called most shameless dogs, take counsel not through the Lord, and strike a covenant not through the spirit of the Lord, and add sins to sins: so that, overcome by flattering vices, they also accept the perversity of false doctrines, and go down into the darkness of Egypt, seeking the help of Pharaoh, who reigns in Egypt, whose protection leads to disgrace and to everlasting reproach. For his princes are in Tanis, that is, in a humble and lowly command, most evil messengers, who labor in vain over a people that will not be able to profit them. For as the salvation of their disciples helps holy teachers, so the perdition of those seduced destroys the patriarchs of those who have fled to the help of Egypt.

In this are reproved certain ones who wish to be governed by their own knowledge; of whom Isaiah says: 'Woe to you, deserting children! That you would take counsel and not from me, and would begin a web and not through my Spirit.' They weave spider's webs who cite sacred Scripture for evil purposes. Bernard says: 'You will never understand Paul unless you find the spirit of Paul.'

30:2.t: You who go down, he says, into Egypt, and have not asked my mouth. Not that they did not ask, but that they would not hear the counsel of the prophet, hoping for help in the strength of Pharaoh, and having confidence in the protection, or shadow, of Egypt. For the strength of Pharaoh, which is put twice in this place, the Hebrew has written MAOZ (מעוז). We have noted this so that, where we read in the last vision of Daniel (Dan 11) the God MAOZIM (מעוזים), we may understand not, as Porphyry dreams, the God of the village of Modim, but the mighty and strong God. Pharaoh among the Egyptians is the name of the royal power; and each is called by a particular name as well, as Pharaoh Neco and Pharaoh Hophra: as if we were to set Caesars and Augusti before the proper names of kings. And the strength of Pharaoh, he says, shall be to you for confusion, and the confidence in the shadow of Egypt for disgrace. […]

Scripture is the mouth of God. Hence Isaiah: "Woe to you who walk to go down into Egypt," that is, to secular sciences, "and have not asked at My mouth," that is, Sacred Scripture. We need not go down to other sciences in order to gain certainty before having had the witness on the mountain, that is, of Christ, Elias and Moses, meaning of the New Testament, of the Prophets and of the Law.

30:4.t: And what follows: For your princes shall be in Tanis, and your messengers have come as far as Hanes, is to be read with mockery and ἐμφατικῶς: that, despising the counsel of God, they sent their princes to Tanis, a city of Egypt, in which was the royal house of Pharaoh, and where under Moses very many signs and portents were performed, as the Psalmist says: Who did wonders in the land of Egypt, in the plain of Tanis (Ps 77 [78]:43). And the same Isaiah says against Egypt: Where now are your wise men? Let them tell you and say what the Lord Sabaoth has purposed against Egypt. The princes of Tanis have failed (Isa 19:12-13); and he records that they failed at that time when the Lord entered Egypt upon a light cloud. We do not read of Hanes, a city of Egypt, anywhere else; but from his saying: Your messengers have come as far as Hanes, we understand that it is the farthest city of Egypt, toward the Ethiopians and the Blemmyes; […]

30:6.t: It is written in Isaiah: "the vision of the quadrupeds in tribulation and distress", and the rest, up to the place where he says: "the riches of the asps will not profit them". Let each one of us consider how great wealth of asps he has borne before this, how great riches of beasts, and how a rational man never sat upon our donkey — not the word of Moses, not of Isaiah, not of Jeremiah, nor of all the rest of the prophets — and he will see that the word of God and reason then sat upon us, when the Lord Jesus came and commanded his disciples that, going, they should untie "the colt of a donkey", which before had been tied up, so that it might walk free.
30:6.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 37

30:6.t: But if you wish to learn yet more beasts, the prophet Isaiah will teach you, who, under "the vision" which he entitled "of the quadrupeds in the desert", speaks by the prophetic spirit certain such things concerning beasts: "in tribulation", he says, "and anguish, the lion and the lion's whelp; thence also the offspring of flying asps, who carried upon asses and camels their riches to a nation which shall not profit them". Can these things in any way be seen as said of bodily beasts, even by those who are exceedingly friends of the letter? For how can "the lion and the lion's whelp" or "the flying asps" "carry upon camels and asses their riches"? But evidently the prophet, filled with the Holy Spirit, enumerates the contrary powers of the most wicked demons, and designated that they place "the riches" of their deceptions upon souls stolid and perverse, which by a figure he compares to camels and asses. […]

The burden of the beasts of the South. For this the Hebrew says MASSA BEEMOTH NEGEB (משא בהמות נגב), which the Seventy translated: The vision of the four-footed beasts in the desert. The foregoing exposition, which we have woven with a very full unfolding of the history, is the interpretation of this place: that, according to prophetic custom, the burden, that is, the weight and load of torments and punishments, came not only upon Babylon and Philistia, and Moab, and Damascus, and Egypt, and the desert of the sea, and also Edom and Arabia, and the valley of Zion, and lastly Tyre, but also upon the beasts of the South, which the Seventy translated four-footed beasts in the desert. He means the tribe of Judah, which, situated in the southern part, borders on the wilderness; and those who, rejecting the prophecy of Jeremiah, when Jerusalem had been taken, would not dwell in Judea, but fled through the desert to the Egyptians. […]

In a land of tribulation and anguish, the lioness and the lion: from them the viper and the flying basilisk: carrying their riches on the shoulders of beasts of burden, and their treasures on the hump of camels, to a people that will not be able to profit them: Egypt shall help in vain and to no purpose. LXX: In tribulation and anguish, the lion and the lion's whelp: thence asps and the offspring of flying asps: who carried their riches on asses and camels to a nation that will not profit them: the Egyptians will profit you emptily and vainly. For lion the Hebrew has written LEIS (ליש); and for flying basilisk, which the Seventy translated offspring of flying asps, in the Hebrew it is called ἐμπρηστὴς and flying, which we can call the burner, and in Hebrew it is named SARAPH (שרף). Again, in the place where we translated carrying on the shoulders of beasts of burden, for beasts of burden all alike translated πώλους, that is, the foals of asses. […]

30:7.t: Therefore I have cried out concerning this: it is only pride: be still. For which the Seventy translators, meaning I know not what, translated: Announce these things, since this consolation of yours is vain. Further, Symmachus translated ταραχαί εἰσιν κατοικεῖν, that is, there are tumults, that they may dwell. The Hebrew word REEB (רהב) Aquila translated ὅρμημα, that is, onset and pride; Symmachus disturbance; the Seventy vanity; Theodotion breadth; it is written with three letters, RES and HE and BETH, and it is the very word read in the Psalms: I will be mindful of Rahab and of Babylon, who know me (Ps 86 [87]:4). And the sense is: Since in the Egyptians there is vain help, I have commanded her, that is, Jerusalem, or I have cried out, that the Egyptians had only the name of a kingdom, and pride without strength; and that Israel ought to sit or dwell in its own land, and not seek help in vain from the weak.

30:8.t: The box-wood tree, because of its light material, trains the child’s hand when it is used for forming the outlines of the letters of the alphabet. Hence Scripture says: ‘Write upon box,’ in order that you may be admonished by the wood itself (which is an evergreen and is never devoid of foliage) never to be deprived of the support of your hope, but rather that the hope of salvation may be generated by faith.

Now go in and write for them on boxwood, and inscribe it carefully in a book: and it shall be in the last day for a testimony forever. The Hebrews say that, since in the prophets there is one spirit, and all times are joined together with the Lord, Jeremiah is commanded, and it is God's charge, that, having entered Egypt, he should write for them on boxwood, which is a wood that does not rot; or, as Symmachus translated, ἐπὶ πτυχὶ, that is, on a very broad tablet. For them, doubtless for the Jews: and that he should set it out carefully in a book, so that there may be no difficulty in reading it, so that when the prophecy has been fulfilled in fact, they may then understand that the word of the prophets is true. We run over the plain things so that we may linger on the more obscure.

30:9.t: For it is a people provoking to anger, and lying sons, sons unwilling to hear the law of God. Who say to the seers: Do not see; and to those who look: Do not look out for us the things that are right: speak to us pleasing things; see errors for us. Take the way away from me: turn the path aside from me: let the Holy One of Israel cease from before our face. It is plain that they provoked the Lord to anger, unwilling to hear the words of Jeremiah (Jer 43). They said to him: Do not see for us what we do not want: do not forbid us the way of Egypt, nor preach the things that are right; but say what pleases us, that we may go on into Egypt, which heaps sins upon sins. Why do you press upon us what we do not willingly hear? why do you show the way by which we do not wish to go? Why do you so often repeat in our ears: Thus says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel? Let this preaching cease from us. According to tropology, all heretics are called lying sons. For they went out from us, but they were not of us (1 John 2); […]

30:10.t: The chief priests and the Pharisees, through the agency of Pilate, sealed the tomb; but the women saw him who was risen.… The chief priests lacked understanding, but the women beheld with their own eyes. When the soldiers came into the city and told the chief priests what had happened, they said to the soldiers, "Say, his disciples came by night and stole him while we were sleeping." Well did Isaiah foretell this also, in their persons: "But tell us, and relate another error." Christ has risen and come back from the dead, and by a bribe they persuade the soldiers.

Say, when is a person most insulted—when he is silent, and one makes no answer, or, when he does speak (and is unheeded)? So that the insult is greater in the present case, when He does speak and thou wilt not hear: greater the contempt. "Speak not to us," we read, they said of old to the Prophets: but ye do worse, saying, Speak: we will not do. For there they turned them away that they should not even speak, as feeling that from the voice itself they got some sort of awe and obligation; whereas you, in the excess of your contempt, do not even this. Believe me, if you stopped our mouths by putting your hands over them, the insult would not be so great as it is now. For say, whether shows greater contempt, he that hears, even when hindering by this action, or, he that will not even hear? […]
30:10.s: HOMILIES ON THE ACTS OF THE APOSTLES 19

30:12.t: Therefore thus says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel: Because you have rejected this word, and have hoped in false accusation and tumult, and have leaned upon it: therefore this iniquity shall be to you like a breach that falls, and is sought for in a high wall: since suddenly, when it is not hoped for, its crushing shall come. And it shall be broken in pieces as a potter's jar is shattered with a very mighty crushing: and there shall not be found among its fragments a sherd in which a little fire may be carried from the burning, or a little water drawn from the pit. Because, he says, you said above: Let the Holy One of Israel cease from before our face, or, as the Seventy translated, take away from us the word of Israel, therefore thus says the Lord, the Holy One of Israel, and he thrusts himself upon you against your will, so that him whom you neglected when he warned you, you may feel when he punishes. […]

30:15.t: Would you know the power of repentance? Would you understand this strong weapon of salvation and the might of confession? By confession Hezekiah routed 185,000 of the enemy. That was important, but it was little compared to what shall be told. The same king's repentance won the repeal of the sentence God had passed on him. For when he was sick, Isaiah said to him, "Give charge concerning your house, for you shall die, and not live." What expectation was left? What hope of recovery was there when the prophet said, "For you shall die"? But Hezekiah did not cease from penitence, for he remembered what was written: "In the hour that you turn and lament, you shall be saved." He turned his face to the wall, and from his bed of pain his mind soared up to heaven—for no wall is so thick as to stifle reverent prayer—"Lord," he said, "remember me." "For it is sufficient for my healing if you remember me. You are not subject to circumstances but are yourself the legislator of life. […]

For thus says the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel: If you return and are quiet, you shall be saved: in silence and in hope shall be your strength; and you would not, and you said: By no means; but we will flee to horses: therefore you shall flee; and we will mount upon swift ones: therefore swift shall they be who pursue you. A thousand men from before the terror of one: and from before the terror of five you shall flee. LXX: Thus says the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel: When you have returned and groaned, then you shall be saved, and you shall know where you were: because you trusted in vain things, your strength has become vain; and you would not hear, but you said: We will flee upon horses: therefore you shall flee; and we will be upon light riders: therefore light shall they be who pursue you. A thousand shall flee at the voice of one, and at the voice of five many shall flee. […]

30:17.t: When Moses fought against Amalek, it was not with the sword but with prayer that he prevailed. Therefore, if we wish to be lifted up, we must first prostrate ourselves.… We do not understand the prophet's words: "One thousand shall flee at the rebuke of one." We do not cut away the causes of the disease, as we must do to remove the disease itself. Else we should soon see the enemies' arrows give way to our javelins, their caps to our helmets, their saddle horses to our chargers.

Until you are left like the mast of a ship on the top of a mountain, and like a signal upon a hill. Jeremiah too writes that, when those who had fled into Egypt had been slain by sword and famine, a few remained who returned to Judea (Jer 44). And as, when a ship has been broken and its framework dissolved, only the tree that is called the mast remains, and is set up as a signal on the summit of a mountain or on a lofty hill, so, as a signal and a trace, scarcely one or two would remain, to show the power of God. And then, he says, all the remnant of Judah, who now are entering the land of Egypt to dwell there, will know, when they have returned to the land of Judea, whose word is fulfilled, mine or theirs.

30:18.t: Therefore the Lord waits, that he may have mercy on you, and therefore he shall be exalted in sparing you, because the Lord is a God of judgment: blessed are all who wait for him. Great is the clemency of God, that he waits for our repentance, and, until we are converted from our vices, holds back his mighty hand, so as not to be compelled to strike. And he has mercy and spares for this reason, that his mercy may be exalted, and the goodness of the Creator made known to all. Or certainly, according to what he says in the Gospel (John 12:32): When I am lifted up, I will draw all things to myself, he is exalted on the cross for this reason, that he may spare all. For he is the God of judgment; and blessed are all who wait for the Lord, who waits for their conversion. But whose this conversion is, and what it is, the following words will show.

30:19.t: For the people of Zion shall dwell in Jerusalem. The Jews refer this to the times of Cyrus, when the people returned from Babylon to Judea under Zerubbabel and Jeshua the high priest. But we, as we have often said already, refer all the promises that exceed the modest measure of that time to the coming of Christ, at which the people once captive, set free by the passion of the Lord, dwelt in Zion and Jerusalem, that is, in the watchtower and the vision of peace, that is, in the Church. Further, as to the word of holiness added in the Seventy, who said: for a holy people dwells in Zion, we can interpret it thus: we say that no one dwells in Zion except one who is holy, and who hears the Lord saying: Be holy, for I too am holy (Lev 11:44).

Weeping, you shall by no means weep; showing mercy, he will have mercy on you: at the voice of your cry, as soon as he hears, he will answer you. When you have returned to Zion and dwelt in Jerusalem, you shall by no means weep as you had wept before, but your weeping shall be turned into joy: For blessed are those who weep, for they shall laugh (Luke 6:21). And after you have cried out and said to the Lord: I cried with my whole heart, hear me, O Lord (Ps 118 [119]:145); and again: I cried, have mercy on me, and I will keep your commandments (Ps 85 [86]); and elsewhere: I waited in the morning and cried out (Ps 118 [119]:147); and your voice has been so clear that it pierces the heavens: at once the Lord will answer you, and you will be like Moses, of whom it is written: Moses spoke, and the Lord answered him (Exod 19:19).

The Divine protection then is inseparably present with us, and so great is the kindness of the Creator towards His creatures, that His Providence not only accompanies it, but actually constantly precedes it, as the prophet experienced and plainly confessed, saying: "My God will prevent me with His mercy." And when He sees in us some beginnings of a good will, He at once enlightens it and strengthens it and urges it on towards salvation, increasing that which He Himself implanted or which He sees to have arisen from our own efforts. For He says "Before they cry, I will hear them: While they are still speaking I will hear them;" and again: "As soon as He hears the voice of thy crying, He will answer thee." And in His goodness, not only does He inspire us with holy desires, but actually creates occasions for life and opportunities for good results, and shows to those in error the direction of the way of salvation.
30:19.s: The Third Conference of Abbot Chaeremon, Chapter 8

30:19.t: These two then; viz., the grace of God and free will seem opposed to each other, but really are in harmony, and we gather from the system of goodness that we ought to have both alike, lest if we withdraw one of them from man, we may seem to have broken the rule of the Church's faith: for when God sees us inclined to will what is good, He meets, guides, and strengthens us: for "At the voice of thy cry, as soon as He shall hear, He will answer thee;" and: "Call upon Me," He says, "in the day of tribulation and I will deliver thee, and thou shalt glorify Me." And again, if He finds that we are unwilling or have grown cold, He stirs our hearts with salutary exhortations, by which a good will is either renewed or formed in us.
30:19.s: The Third Conference of Abbot Chaeremon, Chapter 11

30:20.t: And the Lord will give you scant bread and short water. If we refer these things to the times of Zerubbabel, the interpretation is easy: that under him there was no perfect joy, as David says: When the Lord turned back the captivity of Zion, we became like those comforted: so that they received not full and perfect comfort, but a likeness of comfort. But if to the coming of the Savior, then by the scant bread and short water, according to the Apostle Paul and this same prophet Isaiah, the word of the Gospel is foretold, which, in place of the long-drawn observances and commandments of the Law, summed up all things in one word: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. For the Lord has made a word completed and cut short upon the earth (Gal 5).

And he will no longer make your teacher fly away from you, and your eyes shall see your instructor, and your ears shall hear the word of one admonishing behind your back: This is the way, walk in it, neither to the right nor to the left. LXX: And those who deceive you shall no longer come near you, because your eyes shall see those who led you astray, and your ears shall hear behind you the words of those who deceive, who said: This is the way, let us walk in it, whether to the right or to the left. In this place the Seventy's edition and the Hebrew disagree greatly. First, then, we shall treat of the common edition, and afterward follow the order of the truth. […]

He has seen us sinning and has borne with it. He who forbade us to sin before we did it does not stop waiting to pardon us even after we have sinned. The one we have rejected is calling us. We have turned away from him, but he has not turned away. Hence Isaiah said, "Your eyes shall see your teacher, and your ears shall hear the voice of a counselor behind you." A person is counseled to his face, so to speak, when he is created for righteousness and receives the precepts of rectitude. When he despises these precepts, it is as if he is turning his back to his Creator's face. But he still follows behind us and counsels us that we have despised him, but he still does not cease to call us. We turn our backs on his face, so to speak, when we reject his words, when we trample his commandments under foot; but he who sees that we reject him still calls out to us by his commandments and waits for us by his patience, stands behind us, and calls us back when we have turned away.

30:21.t: God opens the bosom of his loving kindness to us if we return to him after sinning, for he says by the prophet, "If a man puts away his wife, and she goes from him and marries another man, shall he return to her any more? Shall not that woman be polluted and defiled? But you have prostituted yourself to many lovers; nevertheless return to me, says the Lord." Note how the plea of justice is proposed in regard to the wife who commits fornication and is deserted, and yet, for us who return after our fall, it is not justice but loving kindness that is shown. The inference is obvious, namely, that if our sins are spared with such great love, how great would be our wickedness if we sinned but failed to return after our sin, and what pardon can the wicked expect from him who does not cease to call them after they have sinned! […]

We are truly repentant if we weep bitterly over the actions we have committed. Let us consider the riches of our Creator's attitude toward us. He has seen us sinning, and has borne with it. He who forbade us to sin before we did it, does not stop waiting to pardon us even after we have sinned. The one we have rejected is calling us. We have turned away from him, but he has not turned away. Hence Isaiah said, "Your eyes shall see your Teacher, and your ears shall hear the voice of a Counselor behind you." A person is counseled to his face, so to speak, when he is created for righteousness and receives the precepts of rectitude. When he despises these precepts, it is as if he is turning his back to his Creator's face. But he still follows behind us, and counsels us that we have despised him but that he still does not cease to call us. We turn our backs on his face, so to speak, when we reject his words, when we trample his commandments under foot; […]

30:22.t: And you shall defile the plates of your graven images of silver, and the garment of your molten image of gold, and you shall scatter them like the uncleanness of a menstruous woman: Go out, you shall say to it. LXX: And you shall defile the silvered and gilded idols: you shall break them in pieces and scatter them like the water of a menstruous woman, and you shall cast them away like dung. When you have understood the truth, and the deceivers have not come near you, but your eyes have seen your instructor and your ears have always heard: This is the way, walk in it, neither to the right nor to the left: then you will break in pieces and scatter all the errors and idols and likenesses of the truth which an artful tongue had composed in the splendor of eloquence, which is what silver means, and in the reasoning of wisdom, which is what gold signifies; […]

30:23.t: And rain shall be given to your seed wherever you sow in the land, and the bread of the fruits of the land shall be most abundant and rich. LXX: Then there shall be rain for the seed of your land, and the bread of the fruits of your land shall be plentiful and rich. It is written in the volume of Kings (1 Kgs 18) that after the false prophets had been slain by Elijah, rain was given to the land of Israel; and that the bread of Elisha, and afterward of the Savior, was most abundant and most rich, and had such fullness that many thousands of men were filled from it (2 Kgs 4; John 6). So also in the present place, rain will not be given to the spiritual seed, nor the most abundant and richest bread of the land, until the silvered and gilded idols have been broken in pieces and reckoned as a dunghill. For unless vices depart, virtues do not enter.

In that day the lamb shall feed in your possession at large. And your bulls and the foals of asses that work the ground shall eat mingled mash, as on the threshing floor it has been winnowed. LXX: And in that day your cattle shall feed in a rich and spacious place. Your bulls and your oxen that work the ground shall eat chaff mixed with winnowed barley. In the abundance of all things, when the heavenly rain comes down, and that bread which came down from heaven, which whoever eats will never hunger, the lambs shall feed in a most spacious place, those who follow the Lamb wherever he goes and who are always on the right hand. The bulls are the leaders of the flock, of whom we read: The assembly of bulls among the cows of the peoples (Ps 67 [68]:31); and the foals of asses, sitting on which the Lord entered Jerusalem (Matt 21), who work the ground, shall eat from the threshing floor in such a way that it has been winnowed, namely, so that no chaff be mixed in their food; […]

But that we must attain to spiritual knowledge in the order of which we have already spoken, we are taught also by the blessed Apostle. For when he wanted not merely to draw up a list of all his own virtues, but rather to describe their order, that he might explain which follows what, and which gives birth to what, after some others he proceeds as follows: "In watchings, in fastings, in chastity, in knowledge, in long suffering, in gentleness, in the Holy Ghost, in love unfeigned." And by this enumeration of virtues he evidently meant to teach us that we must come from watchings and fastings to chastity, from chastity to knowledge, from knowledge to long sufering, from long suffering to gentleness, from gentleness to the Holy Ghost, from the Holy Ghost to the rewards of love unfeigned. When then by this system and in this order you too have come to spiritual knowledge, you will certainly have, as we said, not barren or idle learning but what is vigorous and fruitful; […]
30:23.s: The First Conference of Abbot Nesteros, Chapter 16

30:25.t: HOW THE PROPHECY AGREES WITH THE GOSPEL, CONCERNING THE DARKENING OF THE SUN AND CERTAIN OTHER THINGS. — Since at the Lord’s first coming it was foretold that the sun would be darkened at his passion, at the very hour when it is proved to have happened, that is, at midday, for therefore it is written in the prophet Amos: “And it shall come to pass in that day, says the Lord, I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day” (Amos 8:9). On that day, therefore, from the sixth hour the sun was darkened until the ninth hour, and therefore the prophecy of the aforementioned prophet was fulfilled. The image of this event, which is to occur at the Lord’s second coming, was shown in the Lord’s passion; for at the end, when the Lord begins to come to judge the world, the heavenly lights will be released from their service, as the Lord says: “In those days the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light” (Matt. 24:29). […]
30:25.s: QUESTIONS ON THE OLD AND NEW TESTAMENTS, QUESTION 105: ON THE DARKENING OF THE SUN

30:25.t: And there shall be upon every high mountain and upon every lifted-up hill streams of running waters in the day of the slaughter of many, when the towers have fallen. In this place the Jews refer the many slain and the falling towers to the power of the Roman empire, of which the Apostle too speaks (2 Thess 2:7): Only let him who holds now hold, until he be taken out of the way: namely, that at that time the blessedness of the people of Israel will be so great that not only the valleys and plains but all the mountains and hills will be watered with flowing waters. But let us understand by the mountains and hills those who are lifted on high by virtues, who hunger and thirst for righteousness (Matt 5), whom the Lord invites to drink. For whoever drinks of his waters will never thirst (John 4). Hence in the psalm too we read: Bless the Lord from the fountains of Israel (Ps 67 [68]:27). And in the Gospel it is said that whoever drinks of the waters of Jesus, rivers of living water shall flow from his belly (John 7). […]

For the flocks of the believers have, as it were, a pasture full of divers plants and flowers, in the holy Scriptures, which are their wise guides: and filled with spiritual joy at the glorious doctrines and instructions which they contain, they frequent the sacred courts. And this it is which long ago was proclaimed in the words of Isaiah: "And there shall be upon every high mountain, and upon every high hill, running waters upon that day." And again; "And the mountains shall drop sweetness: and the hills flow with milk." For it is the custom of divine Scripture to compare to mountains and hills those set over others, and whose office it is to teach, inasmuch as they are high exalted, in respect, I mean, of their thoughts being occupied with elevated subjects, and withdrawn from things earthly: while the waters and the sweetness and the milk are the instructions which flow from them as from fountains. […]
30:25.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

30:26.t: And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day when the Lord binds up the wound of his people and heals the stroke of its blow. LXX: And the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun sevenfold, in the day when the Lord heals the crushing of his people and cures the pain of your blow. I wonder how in the present place the same Seventy translated moon and sun, following the Hebrew, when above they translated the Hebrew words LABANA (לבנה) and HAMMA (חמה), which Aquila renders white and heat, and by which he signifies the moon and the sun, as brick and wall, in the place where it is written: And the moon shall blush, and the sun shall be confounded; for which they translated: the bricks shall melt, and the wall shall fall. Hence the suspicion comes to me that they did not err from the beginning, but were gradually corrupted by the fault of copyists. […]

Moreover, when the day of judgment has been completed and the glory of the future life has become evident with the new heaven and the new earth, then will come to pass what the same prophet announced elsewhere: "The light of the moon will be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be increased sevenfold, like the light of seven days."

30:27.t: But in both editions it must be noted that it is not the Lord, but the name of the Lord, that comes after a long time, of which it is said in the Psalms: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord; the Lord is God, and he has shone upon us (Ps 117 [118]:26). And he himself says in the Gospel: I have come in the name of my Father, and you have not received me (John 5:43). And it is well said that he comes after a long time, since human impatience says: How long, O Lord, will you forget me unto the end? How long do you turn your face away from me? (Ps 12 [13]:1). His burning fury also comes with glory, so that him whom we despised in humility we may fear in majesty. This very thing is written in the psalms too: God manifestly will come, our God, and will not keep silence. Fire will burn in his sight, and round about him a mighty tempest (Ps 49 [50]:3, 4). For he himself says in the Gospel (Luke 12:49): I have come to cast fire upon the earth, and how I wish that it may burn! […]

Behold, the name of the Lord comes from afar: his fury is burning and heavy to bear. His lips are filled with indignation, and his tongue is like a devouring fire. His spirit is like an overflowing torrent reaching to the middle of the neck, to destroy the nations unto nothing, and the bridle of error that was in the jaws of the peoples. You shall have a song, like the night of a hallowed solemnity, and gladness of heart, like one who goes with the pipe to enter into the mountain of the Lord, to the Mighty One of Israel. LXX: Behold, the name of the Lord comes after a long time: his fury burning with glory, the utterance of his lips, an utterance full of wrath, and the wrath of his fury shall devour like fire; and his spirit, like water in a valley, dragging, shall come up to the neck, and shall be divided to confound the nations for their vain error, and error shall be cast away, and it shall take them in their sight. […]

30:28.t: His spirit too, like water in a valley, dragging, will come up to the neck, to make punishments overflow upon sinners. It will be divided according to the quality of their deserts, to destroy and confound the nations which vain error had led astray, so that they may understand that they have been overthrown.

30:29.t: Hence it is said to men of this kind, who prevailed in the power of this world and took delight in their own error, that they will not always be doing this. And some of our writers think that this passage especially, and the whole tenor of the chapter, is spoken against the heretics and all the doctrines that are contrary to the truth: that when the time of judgment has come, they shall by no means enter his holy places and his mountain, that is, the Church of the Lord, lest under the name of religion they gather riches and abandon themselves to luxury, as though celebrating the feasts of the Lord. The Jews understand these things of the nations Gog and Magog, which they think will come from the North, that is, from the regions of Scythia, of whom Ezekiel speaks more fully (Ezek 38-39).

30:30.t: And the Lord will make the glory of his voice heard, and will show the terror of his arm in the threatening of his fury and in the flame of devouring fire: he will dash them down with whirlwind and with hailstone. For at the voice of the Lord Assyria, struck with the rod, will tremble, and the passing of the rod will be founded, which the Lord will make to rest upon him with timbrels and with harps, and in chief battles he will overthrow them. For Topheth has been prepared from yesterday, prepared by the king, deep and wide; its fuel is fire and much wood: the breath of the Lord like a torrent of sulphur kindling it. LXX: And the Lord will make the glory of his voice heard, and will show the fury of his arm with fury and wrath: and with a devouring flame of fire he will strike with lightning vehemently, and like water and hail coming down with violence. […]

30:31.t: At the command of his voice Assyria, struck with the rod, will tremble: every impious man, every imitator of the hostile nation; not that on the day of judgment the Assyrian alone is to be struck, but that by the Assyrian we should understand the devil.

Further, what is said according to the Seventy: At the voice of the Lord the Assyrians will be overcome by the stroke, when he has struck them, and there will be round about him that from which he had the hope of help, in which he trusted; they themselves with timbrels and harp will fight against him by a change, signifies that those who were once subject to the devil rise up against him, and fight against him with joy and gladness by a sudden change, when, understanding their error, they destroy him by whom they had been deceived. And it is said to him that from the beginning he deceived himself, thinking his kingdom everlasting, he for whom Gehenna and eternal punishments are prepared.

30:32.t: Then there follows: And the passing of the rod will be founded, which the Lord will make to rest upon him. And the sense is: the rod will not strike him and then be lifted again, and, in the manner of those who flog, make an end of beating; but he will make it remain in his punishments as if founded and fixed with a deep root. And if it is understood in this way, where will the repentance of the devil be? Especially since it is said to sinners: Go into the eternal fire, which God has prepared for the devil and his angels (Matt 25:41). With timbrels and with harps, and in chief battles, he will overthrow them: that is, the Lord will overthrow the demons and all the impious, to the joy of all.

30:33.t: For from yesterday, that is, from time past, Topheth, that is, a broad and spacious Gehenna, has been prepared by the king, the Lord, to burn them with eternal fires. Its nourishment and kindling is fire and much wood, that is, perpetual flame and the punishments of sinners. And since the prophetic word had foretold this as of a furnace and an oven of burning fire, it keeps the metaphor, so that we may know that it is kindled by the breath and spirit and will of the Lord, with sulphur mixed in, which rouses the flames, to make the torments more bitter.

31:1.t: Let our course take us to regions above, because it is better to ascend. Finally, as was read today, "Woe to them that go down to Egypt." Surely it is not wrong to go to Egypt, but to change to the ways of the Egyptians, to change to the violence of their treachery and to the ugliness of their wantonness—this is wrong. He that changes in this way descends, and one who descends falls. Let us keep away, then, from the Egyptian who is a man, but [let us] not [keep away] from God. Even the king of Egypt himself fell under the dominion of his own vices and in comparison with him Moses was accounted a god, ruling over kingdoms and subjecting powers to himself. So we read that it was said to Moses: "I shall make you a god to Pharaoh."

Woe to those who go down into Egypt for help, hoping in horses, and having confidence in chariots, because they are many, and in horsemen, because they are exceedingly strong, and have not trusted in the Holy One of Israel, and have not sought the Lord. But he, being wise, has brought evil, and has not taken away his words; and he will rise up against the house of the most wicked, and against the help of those who work iniquity. Egypt is man and not God, and their horses are flesh and not spirit: and the Lord will incline his hand, and the helper will collapse, and he to whom help is given will fall, and all of them together will be consumed. […]

These things, indeed, we can also understand of those who, in a time of persecution and of tribulation and distress, do not trust in the Lord, but in the help of the Egyptians, that is, of worldly men; not knowing that Abraham was endangered in Egypt, and that the people of God served with clay and bricks in that region, which is spiritually called the iron furnace. Hence in the Apocalypse of John too we read: The place in which the Lord was crucified is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt (Rev 11:8).

31:2.t: But he, being wise, that is, the Lord, brought evil upon them, and the worst, namely Nebuchadnezzar; or evil in the absolute sense, signifying a thing, not a person; and he did not take away his words, which he had spoken through the prophets. Wherefore he will rise up against the tribe of Judah, the house of the most wicked, and against the help of the Egyptians, who work iniquity.

31:3.t: For Egypt, or the Egyptian, as the Seventy translated, is man and not God, and their horses are flesh and not spirit. Hence it is also written in Jeremiah: Cursed is the man who has his hope in man, and has made firm the flesh of his arm, and whose heart has departed from the Lord. And he will be like a tamarisk in the desert, which will not see when good things come (Jer 17:5, 6). And in another place it is written: Vain is the salvation of man (Ps 59 [60]:13), or, as it stands better in the Hebrew, in man. And when the Lord stretches out his hand to punish, or inclines it, under the metaphor of a charioteer, and slackens the reins of the running horses, the Egyptian helper will collapse, and Israel, to whom help was being given.

31:4.t: For thus says the Lord to me: as when a lion roars, and a lion's whelp, over its prey, and a multitude of shepherds comes against it, it will not dread their voice, nor be afraid at their multitude: so will the Lord of hosts come down to fight upon Mount Zion and upon its hill. Like birds flying, so will the Lord of hosts protect Jerusalem, protecting and delivering, passing over and saving. In plain passages we set down one edition, especially where there is no difference of sense. When the Israelites, and the Egyptians in whose help they trusted, have been slain in Egypt, the captives will return to Jerusalem in the reign of Cyrus. And by two likenesses the strength of the Lord, who had promised that he would be their helper, is shown. […]

31:5.t: Let us state the other comparison as well: as birds, to defend their young, fly over their nests, and if they see a serpent or a man, or other birds approaching their chicks, forget their own weakness and fight with beak and claws, and redouble the grief of their breast with chattering cries: so the Lord will protect Jerusalem, and will deliver it, passing over, and will save it. For passing over, in the Hebrew it is PHASE; in the three translators, besides the Seventy, ὑπερβαίνων is set down. From this it is plain that Pascha, that is, the Phase of the Lord, signifies not passion but passage. And that the Lord, in the likeness of birds, was a protector over Jerusalem, he himself testifies in the Gospel: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those who were sent to you (Matt 23:37): how often I wished to gather your children, as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you would not? […]

31:6.t: Turn back, as you had withdrawn into the depth, sons of Israel. For in that day a man will cast away the idols of his silver and the idols of his gold, which your hands have made for you for sin. And Assyria will fall by a sword not of a man, and a sword not of a human being will devour him: and he will flee, not from the face of the sword, and his young men will be tributaries. And his strength will pass away from terror, and his princes will flee in fear, said the Lord, whose fire is in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem. LXX: Turn back, as you had withdrawn into the depth, sons of Israel. For in that day a man will cast away the idols of his silver and the idols of his gold, which your hands have made for you for sin. And Assyria will fall by a sword not of a man, and a sword not of a human being will devour him, and he will flee, not from the face of the sword; his young men will be overcome: for they will be surrounded by rock as by a rampart, and will be conquered; and whoever flees will be taken. […]

31:9.t: Fire and light are written in Hebrew with the same letters, ALEPH, VAU, RES; if it is read UR, it means fire; if OR, light. This is said because for fire, which Symmachus alone translated, Aquila and Theodotion translated light. But what is meant by what we read in the Septuagint: They will be surrounded by rock as by a rampart, and will be conquered: and whoever flees will be taken, I am unable to know. Unless perhaps we can say this: that the young men of the Assyrian king, who are to be conquered and taken, are surrounded by rock, that is, by the strength of the Lord, as a city is surrounded by a rampart. Further, what follows: Blessed is he who has seed in Zion, and kinsmen in Jerusalem, we can interpret so as to say that it fits the sense of the present passage, in that the divine word exhorts those fleeing into Egypt to return to Jerusalem and beget sons. To this city so great a blessedness is promised that it is defended and protected by the help of the Lord; […]

Of this love that is begun here to be perfected from the sight of the Lord in the eternal kingdom Isaiah rightly speaks, saying, "The Lord lives, whose fire is in Zion, and his furnace in Jerusalem." It is, however, greater to be a furnace than a fire because a fire can also be small, but a larger flame is kindled in a furnace. Zion truly is said to be speculation but Jerusalem the vision of peace. Truly we sometimes catch a glimpse of our peace here in order there later to see it fully. Therefore through the Lord's love the fire is in Zion and his furnace in Jerusalem because here we burn in some measure with the flames of his love when we glimpse him, but there we shall burn totally when we shall fully see him whom we love.

If the breads of the furnace that were baked in secret signify the interior devotion of the mind of the faithful confirmed by the fire of charity, breads which were also commanded by the law to be offered in the sacrifice of the Lord, it is most fitting that the hearts which were made to burn constantly with the flame of intimate love and virtue and to beget words are symbolized through the furnaces in which the same breads were baked. The prophet spoke beautifully about these things when he referred to "the Lord whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem." It is also written: "Did our hearts not burn within us when he spoke along the way and opened the Scriptures to us?"

The precept of the law, therefore, is to be taken in a more spiritual sense. For there is spiritual seed which is conceived through the love and fear of God in the spiritual womb, travailing and bringing forth the spirit of salvation. And in this sense must be understood this verse: Blessed is he who hath seed in Zion and posterity in Jerusalem. For does it mean that, although he be a whoremonger and a drunkard and an idolater, he is still blessed if only he hath seed in Sion and posterity in Jerusalem? No one in his senses will say this.
31:9.s: An Exact Exposition of the Orthodox Faith, Book 4, Chapter 24

31:9.t: But if you ask how these things come about, ask grace, not doctrine; desire, not understanding; the groaning of prayer, not the study of reading; the Bridegroom, not the master; God, not man; darkness, not clarity; not light, but the fire that wholly inflames and carries into God through ecstatic anointings and most ardent affections. Which fire is indeed God, and his furnace is in Jerusalem, and Christ kindles this in the fervor of his most ardent passion, which only he truly perceives who says: My soul has chosen hanging, and my bones death. Whoever loves this death can see God, because it is indubitably true: No man shall see me and live. Let us die, therefore, and enter into the darkness; let us impose silence upon our cares, concupiscences, and phantasms; let us pass over with Christ crucified from this world to the Father, so that, when the Father is shown to us, we may say with Philip: It suffices us; let us hear with Paul: My grace suffices for you; […]

32:1.t: Behold, a king will reign with righteousness, and princes will rule in judgment. And a man will be like one who is hidden from the wind and conceals himself from the tempest: like streams of waters in thirst, and the shade of a jutting rock in a desert land. The eyes of those who see will not be dimmed, and the ears of those who hear will listen diligently. And the heart of the foolish will understand knowledge, and the tongue of stammerers will speak quickly and plainly. He who is senseless will no longer be called a prince, nor will the deceitful man be called great. For the fool will speak foolish things, and his heart will work iniquity, to accomplish pretense, and to speak deceitfully to the Lord, and to empty the soul of the hungry, and to take away drink from the thirsty. The vessels of the deceitful man are most evil: for he has devised schemes to destroy the meek with the word of a lie, when the poor man spoke judgment. […]

These things are according to the Hebrew, from which the Seventy disagree in most places not only in words but also in senses. For when the righteous king has reigned, and his princes have ruled with judgment, there will be a man hiding his words, a man who by nature is God, and he will hide his words, speaking to them in parables (Matt 20:21, 23, 24, and 25). And he will hide them as from running water, that is, from the people of the Jews, which, like water, is borne and drawn this way and that at the will of its teachers. This man, hiding his words among the unbelieving, will appear in Zion, that is, in the Church, like a glorious river running down in a thirsty land. For he will appear to the people of the Gentiles, which before suffered thirst for the truth; and the river of God will water the thirsty fields, the river of which it is written: The rush of the river makes glad the city of God (Ps 45 [46]:4). And in another place: The river of God is filled with waters (Ps 64 [65]:10). […]

32:2.t: And whoever is under his shelter will be as safe in tribulations and distresses, and in the tempest of this world, as one who, fleeing wind and whirlwind, hides himself in a safe place; and as one who finds the purest springs in the desert; and as one who, in fierce heat, when the blaze of the sun scorches everything, rests under a jutting rock. Where we said: like streams of waters in thirst, the Seventy translated: and he will appear in Zion like a running river. For the Hebrew word about which we argued above, BASAION (בציון), which means in thirst, or in dryness, and in a pathless place, the Seventy and Theodotion translated in Zion, reading SION, which is written with the same letters, for SAION, that is, thirst.

32:3.t: When, therefore, Christ has reigned, and his princes have ruled in judgment, the eyes of those who believe will not be dimmed, and the ears of those who hear, which before were deaf, will attend diligently, and the heart of those once foolish will understand knowledge, and the tongue of the stammering and the mute, which could not utter Christ, will confess the Lord with full and open speech.

32:5.t: He who is foolish will no longer be called a prince (1 Cor 1). For God has made foolish the wisdom of this world. Nor will the deceitful and perverse teacher be called great among the peoples: namely the scribes and Pharisees, to whom the Lord said: Fools and blind, which is greater, the gold or the temple that sanctifies the gold? (Matt 23:17).

32:6.t: For the fool will speak foolish things, for which in the Hebrew it is written: NABAL NABALA IDABBER (נבל נבלה ידבר). We say this in order to explain the words of Abigail, who says of Nabal the Carmelite: According to his name he is foolish (1 Sam 25:25). For truly the fool will speak foolish things, and his heart will accomplish iniquity: he who feared where there was no fear, and practiced folly in place of wisdom, saying: If this man were from God, he would not break the sabbath (John 9:16). This the master of the synagogues does to this day, to accomplish pretense, for which in the Hebrew is written ONEPH (חנף), that is, ὑπόκρισις. Hence it is said again and again to the Pharisees: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites (Matt 23:14). And he will speak, he says, deceitfully to the Lord: Master, we know that you are from God, and that you have no concern for men; is it lawful to give tribute to Caesar, or not? (ibid. 22:16, 17). […]

What follows contains nearly the same sense as the Hebrew, and can be fitted to the heretics. For these speak a lie against the Lord, and pervert the hungry and thirsty souls, and make them go away empty; so that even if they have anything good by nature, they lose it through the fault of their teachers, whose whole counsel is to destroy the humble with unjust words and to scatter the words of the humble in judgment. In which it must likewise be noted that whoever can be deceived by them is humble, and clings to the earth.

32:7.t: For all the vessels and weapons of the deceitful teacher and prince are most evil; he contrives snares to destroy the simple with the word of a lie, saying to the deceived people: Search and see, that a prophet does not arise from Galilee (John 7:52). When the poor man spoke to them judgment: he who, though he was rich, became poor for our sake (2 Cor 8). For truly Christ spoke judgment and righteousness to them, saying: If I do not do the works of my Father, do not believe me: but if I do them, even if you will not believe me, believe the works (John 10:37).

32:8.t: This poor man who speaks judgment, the prince and Lord, will think the things that are worthy of a prince, saying: I came only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel (Matt 15:24). And he will be anxious for the unbelieving, desiring to save those who do not believe; and he will stand over his leaders, the Apostles, to one of whom he says: But you, a man of one mind with me, my leader and my familiar friend (Ps 54 [55]:14).

32:9.t: After the calling of the nations, when Christ the king has ruled with righteousness, and his princes, the Apostles and apostolic men, have presided over the believers with judgment, the prophetic word will be directed to the wealthy women, whom we must take either as the cities of Judea, or as the synagogues of that time, or, as most think, as the matrons of the rich men of the former people of the Jews, to whom, as to women lying prostrate after their ruin, it is said: Rise; and they are nonetheless called confident daughters, or hoping; and they are commanded to hear the words of the Lord, and to remember the days and the year, of which we shall speak in what follows, as the Savior himself says: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me: he has sent me to preach the gospel to the poor, to proclaim release to the captives and sight to the blind, to call the acceptable year of the Lord (Luke 4:18, 19); […]

32:11.t: Hence they are summoned to lamentation, and are commanded to bare their breasts and to gird their loins, because the country once desirable, and the fruitful vine, of which it is written: I planted you a fruitful vine, wholly true: how have you turned into the bitterness of a strange vine? (Jer 2:21), has been destroyed by the ravaging Roman.

32:13.t: Over the ground, he says, of my people thorns and briers, or grass will come up. And the sense is: if thorns and briers have filled the land of Judea, which is the land of promise, how much more the other cities, which are full of joy, and which that saying of the Gospel will overtake: Woe to you who rejoice now, for you will weep (Luke 6:25)!

What was said above according to the LXX: Over the land of my people thorns and grass will come up, can be referred both to the heretics and to all the simple among believers, who do not understand Holy Scripture as befits its majesty. Hence we have fitted each to each: that the land of the people of God brings forth thorns for the heretics, and grass for all the unskilled in the Church.

If those very persons, who amid the darkness of the present life shine bright by virtuous attainments—if they also cannot be void of contagion, with what guilt of wickedness are those bound, who still live after the flesh? If those persons cannot be free from sin who are already walking in the way of heavenly desires, what about those who still lie under the loads of sinful habits, who, abandoned to the gratifications of their fleshly part, still bear the yoke of rottenness? So Peter says, "And if the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?" And it is said by Isaiah, "Upon the land of my people shall come up thorns and briars; how much more upon all the houses of joy in the joyous city." The "house of joy in the joyous city" is the mind of the wicked, which neglects to regard the punishments that are destined to come, in the gratification of the flesh, and going away from itself, it revels in empty mirth.
32:13.s: Morals on the Book of Job 17.23

32:14.t: Wealthy women, rise and hear my voice: confident daughters, take in my speech with your ears. After days and a year you too will be troubled, you confident ones: for the vintage is ended; the gathering will come no more. Be astonished, you wealthy women; be troubled, you confident ones: strip yourselves and be confounded. For which Symmachus translated be made naked; there follows: Gird your loins, lament upon your breasts, over the desirable country, over the fruitful vine: thorns and briers will come up over the ground of my people: how much more over all the houses of joy of the exulting city? For the house has been forsaken; the multitude of the city has been left; darkness and groping have come upon the caves for ever: the joy of wild asses, pastures of flocks. Until the spirit is poured out upon us from on high: and the desert will be in Carmel, and Carmel will be counted as a forest. And judgment will dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness will sit in Carmel. […]

For the Lord, that is, my temple, has been forsaken, as I said to the Apostles: Rise, let us go hence (John 14:31); and to the unbelieving: Your house will be left to you desolate (Luke 13:35). Palpable darkness has taken possession of the inner sanctuaries of the Temple and its secret mysteries, and they have become no longer storerooms for the vessels of the Lord, but caves for ever. For they had heard from the Lord Savior (Matt 21:13): The house of my Father shall be called a house of prayer: but you have made it a den of robbers. The joy, he says, of wild asses, pastures of flocks. This is to be understood either according to the letter, in that all things are deserted; or spiritually, in that, Israel having been driven out, savage men who have no knowledge of God dwell in Judea.

32:15.t: And this is to be until the spirit is poured out upon us from on high, which the Savior, ascending to the Father, promised to believers, saying: Behold, I go, and I will send you the Paraclete, the Spirit of truth (John 16). And again: Until you receive power from on high (Luke 24:49). And what he had said above: Yet a little while, and Lebanon will be in Carmel, and Carmel will be counted as a forest: and in that day the deaf will hear the words of the book, and out of darkness and gloom the eyes of the blind will see (above, Isa 29), he now repeats in other words: that the wilderness of the nations is turned into the riches of Israel, and Israel is counted among the nations: at which time judgment will have dwelt in the desert, the Lord and Savior, to whom the Father has given all judgment (John 3). And righteousness will rest in Carmel, of which it was said above: And the desert will be in Carmel: that judgment and righteousness dwell in the desert, and rest in Carmel, which before was called the desert.

32:17.t: The work of righteousness too will be peace, which, according to the Apostle, surpasses all understanding (Phil 4).
