58:14.t: Then you shall delight upon the Lord, and I will lift you up above the heights of the earth, and I will feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father. For the mouth of the Lord has spoken. LXX: And you shall be confident upon the Lord, and he will lift you up above the good things of the earth, and he will feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father. For the mouth of the Lord has spoken. When you have called the sabbaths delightful, and have not moved your foot on the sabbath to do servile work, nor spoken a word, that is, have always kept silent and fulfilled what is commanded, Keep your tongue from evil, and let your lips speak no deceit (Ps 33 [34]:14), then you will delight in the Lord, and will see fulfilled in yourself: Delight in the Lord, and he will give you the petitions of your heart (Ps 36 [37]:4). Or: you will have confidence in the Lord, according to what is written: He who trusts in the Lord is blessed; […]

I used to strive daily to win my way outside the world, outside the flesh; to drive all phantasms of the body from the eyes of my soul, and to see incorporeally supernal joys; and not only with my voice but in the core of my heart I used to say, "My heart hath said unto Thee, I have sought Thy face, Thy face, Lord, will I seek." Moreover desiring nothing, fearing nothing, in this world, I seemed to myself to stand on a certain summit of things, so that I almost believed to be fulfilled in me what I had learnt of the Lord's promise through the prophet, "I will lift thee up upon the high places of the earth." For he is lifted up upon the high places of the earth who treads under foot through looking down upon them in his mind even the very things of the present world which seem lofty and glorious. […]

59:1.t: Behold, the hand of the Lord is not shortened, that it cannot save, nor is his ear made heavy, that it cannot hear; but your iniquities have divided between you and your God, and your sins have hidden his face from you, so that he would not hear. LXX: Is the hand of the Lord not able to save, or is his ear made heavy, that it cannot hear? But your sins separate between you and God, and because of your sins he has turned his face away from you, so as not to have mercy. The things which I have now said I will do, You shall be confident in the Lord, and he will lift you up to the good things of the land, and will feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father, I could have fulfilled before as well. For my hand is not shortened and drawn in, so that I cannot stretch it out to set my people free; nor do I have deaf ears, so that I cannot hear. […]

One of the saints once said: The following I have taken as a sign. When a solitary does not serve God in the right way, and is not zealous in His works, God certainly will send him a temptation to occupy his thoughts, lest he be wholly idle and, by complete idleness, his mind turn aside to thinking of the things of the left hand. But if he is not willing to think of excellence, the influence of the temptations will cause him to think of it and not to think of idle things. This God does with every man who loves Him. When He sees that he begins to disdain His works, he sends a heavy sorrow in order to make him wise and to chastise him. Therefore, when such people call to Him, He does not pay attention, nor does He hasten to free them, till they have become weary and know that they have to bear these things on account of their neglect. ‘When ye spread forth your hands, I will hide mine eyes from you; yea, when ye make many prayers, I will not hear. […]

59:2.t: Let us consider our sins, and reviewing the secrets of our action and mind, let us weigh the merits of our conscience.

The Lord can prohibit adversities, but the merits of sinners cause him to give no aid.… Therefore, let your sins and offences be numbered; let the wounds of your conscience be considered; and let each one cease to complain about God and about us, if he understands that he deserves what he suffers.
59:2.s: Treatise V. An Address to Demetrianus 11

59:2.t: What the middle wall of partition is, he interprets by saying, "the enmity having abolished in His flesh, even the law of commandments contained in ordinances." Some indeed affirm that he means the wall of the Jews against the Greeks, because it did not allow the Jews to hold intercourse with the Greeks. To me, however, this does not seem to be the meaning, but rather that he calls "the enmity in the flesh," a middle wall, in that it is a common barrier, cutting us off alike from God. As the Prophet says, "Your iniquities separate between you and Me;" for that enmity which He had both against Jews and Gentiles was, as it were, a middle wall. And this, whilst the law existed, was not only not abolished, but rather was strengthened; "for the law," saith the Apostle, "worketh wrath."

It is the greatest punishment to commit sin, though we may remain unpunished; as on the other hand, it is the greatest honour and repose to live virtuously, though we may be punished. For sins separate us from God; as He Himself speaks; "Have not your sins separated between you and Me?" But punishments lead us back to God. As one saith, "Give peace; for Thou hast recompensed us for all things." Suppose any one hath a wound; which is the most deserving of fear, gangrene, or the surgeon's knife? the steel, or the devouring progress of the ulcer? Sin is a gangrene, punishment is the surgeon's knife. As then, he who hath a gangrene, although he is not lanced, hath to sustain the malady, and is then in the worse condition, when he is not lanced; so also the sinner, though he be not punished, is the most wretched of men; and is then especially wretched, when he hath no punishment, and is suffering no distress.

For He Himself never turns away from us, but it is we who put ourselves far off: for "I am a God" we read "at hand and not a God afar off." And again, when He was rebuking them by the mouth of this prophet He said "Do not your sins separate between you and me?" Inasmuch then as this is the cause which puts us far from God, let us remove this obnoxious barrier, which prevents any near approach being made.

But now hear how this has actually occurred in real instances. Amongst the Corinthians some man of mark committed a sin such as was not named even among the Gentiles. This man was a believer and belonged to the household of Christ; and some say that he was actually a member of the priesthood. What then? Did Paul cut him off from the communion of those who were in the way of salvation. […]

But the sins, he says, of yours, like a wall set up in the midst, divide you and God. Hence the Savior too in his passion made both one (Eph 2), and, dissolving the middle wall of partition, destroyed the enmity in his own flesh, so that those whom the wall of sins had divided the blood of Christ might join together. He opened the gate of paradise, which had been shut for a long time (Gen 3), and quenched the fiery sword with his own blood, so that the thief might hear: Today you shall be with me in paradise (Luke 23:43). What follows, And because of your sins he has turned his face away from you, so that he would not hear, or so as not to have mercy, shows this: that he could not bear the stench of their sins and their iniquities, but turned away his face, so as not to see their foulness and be compelled at once to strike. Hence the sinner, longing to see the face of the Lord, says in the psalm: How long, Lord, will you forget me to the end? How long will you turn your face away from me? (Ps 12 [13]:1). […]

59:3.t: But such meditation, because it is evil, the Holy Spirit blames in these words, and reproves too in other terms, saying, ‘Your hands are polluted with blood, your fingers with sins; your lips have spoken lawlessness, and your tongue imagineth iniquity: no man speaketh right things, nor is there true judgment.’ But what the end is of such perverse imagining, He immediately declares, saying, ‘They trust in vanities and speak falsehood; for they conceive mischief, and bring forth lawlessness. They have hatched the eggs of an asp, and woven a spider’s web; and he who is prepared to eat of their eggs, when he breaks them finds gall, and a basilisk therein.’ Again, what the hope of such is, He has already announced. ‘Because righteousness does not overtake them, when they waited for light, they had darkness; when they waited for brightness, they walked in a thick cloud. They shall grope for the wall like the blind, and as those who have no eyes shall they grope; they shall fall at noon-day as at midnight; […]

For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity; your lips have spoken falsehood, and your tongue utters iniquity. There is none who calls for righteousness, nor is there any who judges truly; but they trust in nothing and speak vanities. LXX: For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with sins. Your lips are defiled with iniquity, and your tongue meditates unrighteousness. No one speaks righteous things, nor is there righteous judgment. They trust in vain things and speak empty things, iniquities and sins. What he named above in general, he now sets out in its parts. And we must note that he by no means charges them with the idolatry in which they were held in the times of Isaiah, but with the shedding of blood, of which he had already spoken before: The righteous man perishes, and there is none who considers it. And righteous men are taken away, and no one understands in his heart. For the righteous man has been taken away from the face of iniquity; […]

Their lips too and their tongue speak iniquity and falsehood, so that instead of Christ they promise themselves the Antichrist; and there is no one among the people who calls for righteousness and judges truth, or, as it is in the Hebrew, faith, that is, who believes in Christ; but they trust in nothing and speak vanities. Hence the Apostle commands that we should not give heed to Jewish fables and the commandments of men who turn away from the truth (Titus 1). For truly they trust in nothing and follow vanities; in which the Lord's prophecy is fulfilled: I have come in the name of my Father, and you have not received me; if another comes in his own name, him you will receive (John 5:43).

59:4.t: They have conceived toil and brought forth iniquity; they have broken the eggs of asps and woven the webs of the spider. He who eats of their eggs shall die, and what has been warmed shall break out into a basilisk. Their webs shall not serve for a garment, nor shall they be covered with their works. LXX: For they are in labor with pain and beget iniquity. They have broken the eggs of asps and woven the web of the spider. And he who wishes to eat of their eggs, breaking one, will find it rotten, and in it a basilisk. Their web shall not serve for a garment, nor shall they be covered with their works. Those who await the coming of the Antichrist, and cannot say, From your fear, Lord, we have conceived, and been in labor, and brought forth; we have wrought the spirit of your salvation upon the earth (Isa 26:18), rightly conceive pain and bring forth iniquity, so that the one whom they seek with much labor they may receive in iniquity. […]

59:5.t: Of such a kind as this, perhaps, is that of which the prophet says, touching the ungodly, "They weave a spider's web." For as in the cobweb there is the appearance of something woven, but no substantiality in the appearance,—for he who touches it touches nothing substantial, as the spider's threads break with the touch of a finger,—just such is the unsubstantial texture of idle phrases. "Not dividing His own essence by begetting and being at once begetter and begotten." Ought we to give his words the name of argument, or to call them rather a swelling of humours secreted by some dropsical inflation? … Who is so distracted, who is so demented, as to make the statement against which Eunomius thinks he is doing battle? For the Church believes that the true Father is truly Father of His own Son, as the Apostle says, not of a Son alien from Him.

These break and burst the eggs of asps, so as to take their poisons into their own minds; to them it is said in the Gospel: Serpents, brood of vipers (Matt 3:7). And he fittingly set down the eggs of asps and serpents, which are said to produce eggs first. And because they not only retain the poisons of malice in their hearts, but also meditate on the law of the Lord day and night, muttering old wives' fables, therefore it is said: And they weave the webs of the spider, with which they catch flies and gnats and small creatures; but if anything strong comes against them, it flies through as though through empty air. He who eats, he says, of their eggs shall die, that is, he who yields to their counsels, as Abel yielded to Cain when he said, Let us go out into the field (Gen 4:8), will at once be killed; or, as the Seventy translated: He who wishes to eat of their eggs, crushing one, will find it rotten, and in it a basilisk. […]

Some explain this place thus: The eggs of asps they have split, or broken: that is, they abandoned all the biting words of the Prophets, and wove for themselves the smooth speeches of the false prophets; and whoever eats of them will be struck by the serpent, and will understand that the words of falsehood have profited him nothing.

Those who bent their knee to drink are those who inclined themselves totally to philosophy: and the same are inclined to an infinite number of errors, and that is how the leaven of error is warmed. They warm the eggs of asps, so that what has been warmed breaks out into a serpent.

59:6.t: And because he had said above, They weave the webs of the spider, he explains that the weaving of these webs does no good. Their labor, he says, and all their doctrine does not make the garment of Christ, nor a cloak by which the nakedness of the soul may be covered; but they sweat with fruitless labor, as this same Prophet says: This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me. And in vain do they worship me, teaching the doctrines and precepts of men (Isa 29:13); following these, they neglect the law of God. And so that we may know that works are signified by the web, he added: Nor shall they be covered with their works.

Their works are useless works, and the work of iniquity is in their hands. Their feet run to evil, and they hasten to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are useless thoughts; desolation and destruction are in their ways. The way of peace they have not known, and there is no judgment in their steps. Their paths have become crooked to them; everyone who treads in them does not know peace. LXX: For their works are works of iniquity, and their feet run to malice; swift to shed harmless blood; and their thoughts are the thoughts of fools. Destruction and misery are in their ways, and the way of peace they have not known, and there is no judgment in their ways. For their paths are perverse, which they pass along, and they do not know peace. Therefore they are not covered with their works, because their works are works of iniquity, which the Apostle calls unfruitful, that is, having no fruits (Eph 5).

59:7.t: And their feet run to evil and hasten to shed harmless blood (Prov 1). For they had this custom in the slaying of the Prophets too. To them Stephen said: For which of the Prophets did your fathers not persecute? (Acts 7:52). And the Lord in the Gospel: Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the Prophets and stone those who are sent to you (Matt 23:37); and again: All the righteous blood that has been shed upon the earth shall come upon you, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah the son of Barachiah, whom you killed between the Temple and the altar (ibid., 35). Hence it is said to them above as well: For your hands are defiled with blood, and your tongue speaks iniquity (Isa 59:3). And through this practice of cruelty and blasphemy they came to the slaying of the Lord, just as Judas too came by the way of avarice to murder, or rather to sacrilege joined with avarice.

What follows, Their thoughts are the thoughts of fools; destruction and misery are in their ways, and the way of peace they have not known, and, above, Their feet are swift to shed blood, the Apostle set down in Romans (ch. 3). Many, not knowing this, think it was taken from the thirteenth psalm, in which the verses were added in the common edition and are not found in the Hebrew; about this we spoke more fully at the beginning of this volume.

59:8.t: Rightly did they not know the way of peace, who refused to receive its author. For he is our peace, who says to the Apostles: My peace I give you, my peace I leave you (John 14:27); and to Jerusalem: If you knew the things that are for your peace; for the days shall come upon you, and your enemies shall surround you with a rampart, and besiege you, and dash your children to the ground (Luke 19:42, 43). And those who have not received peace consequently have no judgment in their ways either: namely him of whom it was said above, Behold my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved whom my soul has loved; he shall bring forth judgment to the nations (Isa 42:1). It follows: Their ways are perverse, not by nature, but by their own will. For whatever is perverted and bent is twisted from straight into crooked. The whole doctrine of the Pharisees is a subversion of the truth; whoever walks by it not only does not find peace, but does not even know it, so as to know what he ought to seek.

59:9.t: Because of this judgment is far removed from us, and righteousness will not overtake us. We waited for light, and behold, darkness; for brightness, and we have walked in darkness. We have groped for the wall like the blind, and we have felt about as if without eyes; we have stumbled at noon as in darkness; in dark places as dead men. We shall all roar like bears, and like doves we shall moan in meditation. We waited for judgment, and there shall be none; for salvation, and it is far removed from us. LXX: Therefore judgment has departed from them, and righteousness does not overtake them. While they waited for light, darkness came upon them. Waiting for it, they shall walk in darkness; they shall grope for the wall like the blind, and shall feel about as though having no eyes. They shall fall at noon as at midnight; like dying men they shall groan; like a bear and like a dove they shall walk together. We waited for judgment, and there is none; salvation has departed far from us. […]

59:10.t: So they grope at the holy Scriptures like the blind feeling for a wall, seeking in them only the words and the leaves, not the sense and the fruit which is held in the letters. Then he adds and says: We have stumbled, or we shall fall at noon as in darkness; in dark places, as dead men. For while the sun of righteousness flashes its brightness over the whole world, they linger in darkness, namely as men dead in sin.

59:11.t: We shall all roar, he says, like bears, and like doves we shall moan in meditation; so that they are at once cruel and wretched: fierce and savage toward the lowly and those subject to them, fearful and trembling toward those who are stronger, whom they dread as doves dread hawks. We read in another place too: Like a she-bear robbed of her cubs; and in Daniel the bloody kingdom, in which there are three rows of teeth, is compared to a most ferocious she-bear (2 Sam 17:8; Dan 7). And like doves we shall moan in meditation, without sense and understanding of the Scriptures, meditating only on the words, which they chant by heart. But just as the doves of which it is written, Ephraim is like a dove that has no sense (Hos 7:11), and as in the Gospel the simplicity of doves is set against the malice of serpents (Matt 10), so in the present place simplicity without prudence, which is close to folly, is shown in the mere meditation of words. They will wait for judgment, and there will be none; […]

59:12.t: Our iniquities are multiplied before you, and our sins have answered against us; for our crimes are with us, and we have known our iniquities: to sin and to lie against the Lord; and we have turned away so as not to go behind our Lord, so as to speak calumny; and we have conceived transgression, and have spoken from the heart words of falsehood. And judgment is turned backward, and righteousness has stood far off, for truth has fallen in the street, and equity could not enter. And truth has been given over to forgetfulness, and he who departed from evil lay open to be a prey. LXX: For our iniquity is great in your sight, and our sins have withstood us. For our iniquities are in us, and we have known our unrighteousnesses. We have acted impiously, and we have lied, and we have departed from our God. We have spoken unjust things and been disobedient. We have been in labor with and meditated from our hearts unjust words. […]

59:13.t: And what are the iniquities? To sin and to lie against God; or, as Aquila translated according to the Hebrew, to deny God: which refers to the Savior. And we have forsaken, they say, our God, saying: We know that God spoke to Moses; but as for this man, we do not know where he is from (John 9:29); so as to speak calumny: If this man were from God, he would not break the sabbath (ibid., 16); and: By Beelzebub the prince of demons he casts out demons (Luke 11:15). And transgression, which in Greek is called more expressively ἀπόστασις, when someone denies God and is convicted of prevarication. We have conceived and spoken from the heart words of falsehood, despising the law of God and following the traditions of men, which they call δευτερώσεις, and which we feigned in our heart:

59:14.t: And judgment is turned backward, and righteousness has stood far off. For what share has righteousness with iniquity? What agreement has Christ with Belial? Righteousness has taken its stand among the nations and has departed from us, because truth has fallen in the street. For wide and spacious is the way that leads to death (Matt 7), because they would not enter the narrow way in which truth abides.

59:15.t: And truth has been given over to forgetfulness, of which it is written: Truth has sprung from the earth, and righteousness has looked down from heaven (Ps 84 [85]:12). Here we must observe that truth is named often, so that the person of Christ might be shown; forsaking him, they followed falsehood. And he who departed from evil lay open to be a prey. Although this seems obscure, it can be explained thus: when we were fashioning falsehood from our own heart and forsaking the law of God, righteousness stood far off, and truth fell in the streets, and equity could not enter in to us, and the Son of God, who is the truth, was given over to forgetfulness; so much so that whoever wished to depart from the traditions of the Jews at once lay open to plots and persecutions, so that they cast out of the synagogues the man blind from birth who had received his sight (John 9). […]

And the Lord saw, and it appeared evil in his eyes, that there is no judgment; and he saw that there is no man, and he was at a loss, because there is none to meet him. And his own arm will save for him, and his righteousness itself has strengthened him. He has put on righteousness as a breastplate, and a helmet of salvation upon his head. He has put on the garments of vengeance, and is covered as with a cloak of zeal. As for vengeance, as for the repayment of indignation to his foes, and recompense to his enemies, he will repay recompense to the islands. LXX: The Lord saw, and it did not please him, because there was no judgment. And he saw, and there was no man. And he considered, and there was none to defend. And he avenged them with his arm, and upheld with mercy. And he put on righteousness as a breastplate, and set the helmet of salvation on his head. And he was wrapped in the garment of vengeance, and in a cloak, as one repaying vengeance, reproach to his adversaries. […]

59:17.t: Then he put on the breastplate of righteousness, and the helmet of salvation, and the garments of vengeance, and was wrapped in the cloak of zeal; and thus armed he went forth to war, to render vengeance to his enemies, doubtless meaning the Jews who persevered in their blasphemies, and recompense to his foes, when the Roman army surrounded them; and in their victory the Lord is shown to have fought. Paul used this testimony when writing to the Ephesians, wishing us to put on the armor of Christ, by which we may resist the fiery darts of the devil (Eph 6). And what is not found in the Seventy Translators, He will repay recompense to the islands, signifies the cities of Judea, which the Roman army laid waste. For above too (Isa 20) the Lord speaks through the Prophet to the inhabitants of the island, that is, of Jerusalem.

59:19.t: And those from the West shall fear the name of the Lord, and those from the rising of the sun his glory, when he comes like a violent river which the spirit of the Lord drives on; and the redeemer shall come to Zion, and to those who return from iniquity in Jacob, says the Lord. This is my covenant with them, says the Lord: My spirit which is in you, and my words which I have put in your mouth, shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of the seed of your seed, says the Lord, from now and for ever. LXX: And those from the West shall fear the name of the Lord, and those from the rising of the sun the glorious name. For the wrath of the Lord shall come like a violent river, ÷ it shall come with fury ⁚ and he who delivers shall come from Zion. And he shall turn away impieties from Jacob, and this shall be my testament to them, says the Lord. […]

59:20.t: It follows: The redeemer of Zion shall come, and of those who return from iniquity in Jacob, says the Lord. For this the Seventy translated: He who delivers shall come from Zion, and shall turn away impieties from Jacob. If, then, he who turns away the impieties from Jacob will come from Zion, we understand this: that a man was born in Zion, and the Most High founded her, he who turns away the crimes of Jacob. But if the redeemer shall come to Zion, and to those who return from iniquity in Jacob, says the Lord, this is the sense: Christ will come, who will redeem Zion with his blood; or, according to the Hebrew idiom, he who is the kinsman of Zion and was begotten of the stock of Israel; for this is what GOEL (גואל), that is, ἀγχιστεὺς, means. […]

Paul, explaining this place carefully, writes to the Romans that there is no distinction of Jew and Greek, but the same Lord of all, rich toward all who call upon him (Rom 10); and that the nations did not believe in such a way that Israel was wholly driven out. For I too, he says, am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God has not cast off his people whom he foreknew (Rom 11:1, 2). And a little after, when he had set down the example of Elijah, complaining to the Lord that he alone was left, and hearing from him that the Lord had left for himself seven thousand men who had not bent the knee before Baal (1 Kgs 19), he added: So then at this present time also a remnant has been saved according to the election of grace. And if by grace, it is no longer of works; otherwise grace is no longer grace. What then? What Israel was seeking, this it has obtained; but the election has obtained it, and the rest have been blinded. And they, if they do not remain in unbelief, will be grafted in. […]

59:21.t: Theirs, then, is the redemption in Zion, and theirs the kinsman, who from Jacob have received him; and to them he promises, saying: This is my covenant with them, or pact, as all the others translated, or testament, as the Seventy put it. What the covenant, pact and testament is, the following verse shows: My spirit, he says, which is in you, and my words which I have put in your mouth, shall not depart from your mouth, nor from the mouth of your seed, from now and for ever. This is said either to Isaiah, as it seems to me, or to the Lord, as very many think. With reference to Isaiah, then, the order is connected thus: This is the everlasting pact of the Gospel: that my spirit which is in you, and my words which I have put in your mouth, by which you foretell things to come, shall not depart from your mouth, nor from that of your sons and grandsons and your seed, so that every generation in succession is indicated: namely, that the grace of the Prophets comes upon the Apostles, and through those of Israel who are to […]

60:1.t: And the Logos, exhorting us to come to this light, says, in the prophecies of Isaiah, "Enlighten yourself, enlighten yourself, O Jerusalem, for your light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen on you." Observe now the difference between the fine phrases of Plato respecting the chief good and the declarations of our prophets regarding the light of the blessed; and notice that the truth as it is contained in Plato concerning this subject did not at all help his readers to attain to a pure worship of God, or even himself, who could philosophize so grandly about the chief good, whereas the simple language of the Scriptures led to their honest readers being filled with a divine spirit; and this light is nourished within them by the oil, which as a certain parable is said to have preserved the light of the torches of the five wise virgins.

Hail, thou heaven upon earth, Sion, the city that is for ever faithful unto the Lord. Hail, and shine thou Jerusalem, for thy light is come, the Light Eternal, the Light for ever enduring, the Light Supreme, the Light Immaterial, the Light of one substance with God and the Father, the Light which is in the Spirit, and in which is the Father; the Light which illumines the ages; the Light which gives light to mundane and supramundane things, Christ our very God. Hail, city sacred and elect of the Lord. Joyfully keep thy festal days, for they will not multiply so as to wax old and pass away.

Arise, be enlightened; for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you. For behold, darkness will cover the earth, and thick gloom the peoples; but upon you the Lord will rise, and his glory will be seen in you. And the nations will walk in your light, and kings in the brightness of your rising. LXX: Be enlightened, be enlightened, ÷ Jerusalem ⁚ for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you. Behold, darkness will cover the earth, and thick gloom upon the nations. But upon you the Lord will appear, and his glory will be seen in you. And the nations will walk in your light, and kings in your brightness. What we thought about the restoration of Zion and Jerusalem, and about everything that is promised to her by the prophetic oracle, we said more fully at the end of the preceding book, where we explained what that little verse meant: The redeemer will come to Zion, and to those who return from iniquity in Jacob. […]

Further, the name Jerusalem and of the nations, which the Seventy set down here, is not found in the Hebrew, and must be marked beforehand with an obelus, against those who assert that everything said here is said to Jerusalem.

He also cries out to Jerusalem in another place: Be enlightened, be enlightened, O Jerusalem; for your light has come upon you, and the glory of your God has risen upon you. For behold, darkness and gloom shall cover the earth over the nations, but over you the Lord shall appear, and the glory of your God has risen upon you. And kings shall walk in your light, and the nations in your splendor. If gloom and darkness shall cover the earth over the nations, how in turn shall the nations walk in the splendor of the Lord? But those nations will be in darkness which the cold and frost have gripped; and those will walk in the light of the Lord which have followed the kings, the apostles and prophets, of whom it is written: The heart of the king is in the hand of the Lord.

60:2.t: For behold, darkness will cover the earth, that is, those who savor earthly things; and thick gloom the peoples, or, as we read in the Hebrew, the tribes: which refers properly to the Jews, of whom it is written in another psalm: For there the tribes went up, the tribes of the Lord, the testimony of Israel (Ps 121 [122]:4). But upon you the Lord will rise, the sun of righteousness, and his glory will be seen in you, of which it is written: And we saw his glory, the glory as of the only-begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth (John 1:14).

60:3.t: And the nations will walk in your light. We all shall walk in the light of the Apostles, which shines in the world, and the darkness did not comprehend it. And kings, he says, in the brightness of your rising, when you were first born in Christ. This is fulfilled both spiritually and carnally: so that kings whose heart is in the hand of the Lord, and in whose mortal body sin does not reign (Prov 21), may walk in the brightness of the newborn Church, or in him who has risen in the Church, and may bow their necks to the faith of Christ, the true king (Rom 6). And we see this fulfilled daily, when the Roman princes, the error of idolatry and the fury of persecution being removed, pass over to the faith and tranquillity of Christ. There are some who await in a time to come all these things which we relate as partly fulfilled and wholly to be fulfilled from the first coming of the Savior until the consummation of the world, when, as the fullness of the nations comes in, all Israel is to be saved (Rom 11). […]

60:4.t: Lift up your eyes round about and see: all these have gathered and come to you. Your sons will come from afar, and your daughters will suck at your side. LXX: Lift up your eyes round about, and see all your sons gathered. All your sons have come from afar, and your daughters will be carried upon the shoulders. It is said to the Church, Zion, which was first gathered through the Apostles; of whom we also read in the Acts of the Apostles that devout men from the whole world were in Jerusalem, who received the word of God, and in the tongues of their own and of foreign nations either heard others speaking or themselves spoke to the rest (Acts 2). And they are commanded to lift up their eyes round about, which the Lord too commanded the Apostles, saying: Lift up your eyes and see, for the crops are already white for the harvest (John 4:35). For out of Zion, and by no means out of Mount Sinai, the law will go forth, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem. […]

60:5.t: Then you will see and overflow, and your heart will marvel and be enlarged, when the multitude of the sea has been turned to you, and the strength of the nations has come to you. LXX: Then you will see, and you will fear, and you will be astonished in heart: because the riches of the sea, and of the nations, and of the peoples will be transferred to you. When you have lifted up your eyes and beheld your sons and daughters either coming swiftly by themselves or carried on the shoulders of the saints, then you will rejoice, and like rivers you will overflow with sudden waters, and your heart will marvel and be astonished, nay rather will be enlarged, as it hears the Apostle: My mouth is open to you, O Corinthians. And again: Be enlarged, and we too (2 Cor 6:11); lest through narrowness of heart you should be unable to have as your guest Christ, who says in the Gospel: I and the Father will come and will make our dwelling with him (John 14:23). […]
"Then you shall be radiant at what you see, your heart shall throb and overflow": in contemplation, there is admiration, expansion, a transference and restoration of one's self.

When the soul is lifted up, it must not be idle, but should look around. "Then you shall be radiant at what you see, your heart shall throb and overflow." Then, indeed, the soul must be fixed, and standing, and expecting. Then follows divine induction. When a worthy admission has come about together with a holy perception, then the soul is rapt in God, that is, in the beloved.

60:6.t: And again I say to you: It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of heaven. By this saying it is shown that it is not difficult but impossible. For if, as a camel cannot enter through the eye of a needle, so a rich man cannot enter the kingdom of heaven, none of the rich will be saved. But if we read in Isaiah how the camels of Midian and Ephah come to Jerusalem with gifts and offerings, and how those who were formerly bent and twisted by the perversity of vices enter the gates of Jerusalem, we shall see how these camels too, to which the rich are compared, when they have laid down the heavy burden of sins and the crookedness of the whole body, can enter by the narrow and strait way that leads to life.

A flood of camels will cover you, the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah. All from Sheba will come, bringing gold and incense, and proclaiming praise to the Lord. All the flock of Kedar will be gathered to you; the rams of Nebaioth will minister to you; they will be offered upon my altar of propitiation, and I will glorify the house of my majesty. LXX: And herds of camels will come to you, and the camels of Midian and Gephar will cover you: all from Sheba will come, bringing gold and incense, and they will proclaim the salvation of the Lord. All the sheep of Kedar will be gathered to you, the rams of Nabaeoth will come, and they will be offered as propitiatory upon my altar; and the house of my prayer will be glorified. After the riches of the sea and the strength of the nations, herds of camels too, and the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah, are promised to Jerusalem, all of which will come from Sheba carrying gold and incense, and, what is greater than these, proclaiming the salvation of the Lord. […]

60:8.t: In that place they shall forget this world. There they have no want; and they shall love one another with an abundant love. In their bodies there shall be no heaviness, and lightly shall they fly as doves to their windows.
60:8.s: Demonstration 22 (Of Death and the Latter Times), Section 12

60:8.t: Thus, typically, under the leadership of the Law (for Moses was a type of the Law that was coming) Israel passes unwetted over that sea, while the Egyptian who crosses in her track is overwhelmed. Each fares according to the disposition which he carries with him; one walks lightly enough, the other is dragged into the deep water. For virtue is a light and buoyant thing, and all who live in her way "fly like clouds," as Isaiah says, "and as doves with their young ones"; but sin is a heavy affair, "sitting," as another of the prophets says, "upon a talent of lead." If, however, this reading of the history appears to any forced and inapplicable, and the miracle at the Red Sea does not present itself to him as written for our profit, let him listen to the Apostle: "Now all these things happened unto them for types, and they are written for our admonition."

For the soul has flights, as has been said, "Who are these that fly like clouds and like doves with their young?" You see, the soul has spiritual flights that, in a brief moment, circle the whole globe. For the thoughts of wise people are free and, insofar as they rise up from lower to higher shadows, so much and more they fly without the hindrance of any earthly weight, and they are the more carried along by the beating of spiritual wings onto that ethereal and rarefied place; [the soul] despises all worldly things. It soars above the world in its regard for eternal virtues; for justice is above the world, goodness is above the world, wisdom is above the world, even when it is found in the world, it is above the world nevertheless.

Who are these who fly like clouds, and like doves to their windows? For the islands wait for me, and the ships of the sea in the beginning, that I may bring your sons from afar, their silver and their gold with them, to the name of the Lord your God, and to the Holy One of Israel, because he has glorified you. LXX: Who are these who fly like clouds, and like doves with their young to me? The islands have waited for me, and the ships of Tarshish among the first, to bring your sons from afar, and their silver and gold with them, for the sake of the holy name of the Lord, and because the Holy One of Israel has been glorified. […]

For death indeed climbs in through the windows and enters houses, in that through the body's sense lust comes and enters the dwelling of the mind. Quite to the contrary is this which we have often cited from Isaiah concerning the righteous: "Who are they who fly like clouds and like doves come to their windows?" The righteous are said to be like clouds since they are raised above earthly contagions, just as doves go to their own windows, since each one does not pay much attention to their exterior senses, and fleshly lust does not catch them when they are far from home.… For the holy person who receiving the senses of his body like servants to help him is in control of them; and the fairest judge sees sins before they come and closes the windows to the plundering death of the body, saying, "I have made a covenant with my eyes, that I should not gaze at a young woman."
60:8.s: Morals on the Book of Job, Book 21

60:8.t: But this sacrifice of good will is never fully paid unless desire for this world is perfectly abandoned. For whatever we covet in it, we without doubt envy our neighbors. For it seems that what another obtains is lacking to us. And because envy always conflicts with good will, as soon as the former seizes the mind, the latter departs. Therefore the holy preachers, that they might perfectly love their neighbors, strove to love nothing in this age, never to desire anything, to possess nothing even without desire. Looking upon them well, Isaiah says: "Who are these that fly as clouds, and as doves to their windows?" For he saw them despise earthly things, draw near to heavenly things in mind, rain down words, flash forth miracles. And those whom holy preaching and sublime life had lifted up from earthly contagions, he calls both flying and clouds. Moreover our windows are our eyes, because through them the soul looks upon what it desires outwardly. But the dove is a simple animal, and free from the malice of gall. […]

60:10.t: And the sons of strangers will build your walls, and their kings will minister to you. For in my indignation I struck you, and in my reconciliation I have had mercy on you. And your gates will be open continually; they will not be shut by day or by night, so that the strength of the nations may be brought to you, and their kings be led in. For the nation and the kingdom that will not serve you will perish, and the nations will be laid waste with desolation. LXX: And foreigners will build your walls, and their kings will stand by you. For because of my wrath I struck you, and because of mercy I have loved you. And your gates will be open always; they will not be shut by day or by night, so that they may bring in to you the strength of the nations, and their kings who are to be led in. For the nations and the kings that will not serve you will perish; the nations will be made desolate with desolation. […]

Or certainly this must be said: that she who was once afflicted and handed over to captivity in the people of the Jews he reconciles to himself in the calling of the nations, so that her gates are always open, and are shut neither by day nor by night, and stand continually open to those who desire to be saved; that is, that entrance to her is not denied to those who wish to believe, whether in joy or in tribulation. And let the strength, or the riches, of the nations be brought in to her, and let their kings minister to her, or be led to her as captives. This you will understand when you see the most eloquent men led to the faith of Christ, and the wisdom of the wise made foolish, and the prudence of the prudent rejected (1 Cor 1), so that the foolishness of God is wiser than men.

60:12.t: But the nation and their kings who refuse to render the Church a good and profitable service, so as to pass over into apostolic dignity, will perish with the perdition that is prepared for the ungodly; and whatever was in them who refused to have God as their guest will be reduced to desolation.

60:13.t: The glory of Lebanon will come to you, the fir and the box and the pine together, to adorn the place of my sanctification; and I will glorify the place of my feet. And the sons of those who humbled you will come to you bowed down, and all who disparaged you will worship the footprints of your feet, and they will call you the city of the Lord, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel. LXX: The glory of Lebanon will come to you, in cypress and pine and cedar together, so that my holy place may be glorified, ÷|÷ and I will glorify the place of my feet ⁚ And the sons of those who humbled you will go to you in fear, ÷ and provoked you ⁚ and all who provoked you will worship the footprints of your feet; and you will be called the city of the Lord, Zion, of the Holy One of Israel. Much is lacking in the Seventy, which I have set down from the Hebrew under asterisks, and what they added I have marked beforehand with an obelus. […]

60:14.t: And what follows, And the sons of those who humbled you will come to you bowed down, or returning, and all who had disparaged you will worship the footprints of your feet, we ought to understand of those who are Christians not by will but by necessity, and who bow with fearful minds through dread of offending those who reign. Or certainly that those who were formerly persecutors afterwards believed: such as was the apostle Paul too, who persecuted the Church of God and was afterwards called a vessel of election (Acts 9). When these things have been so fulfilled that the fullness of the nations enters in, then all Israel will be saved. And she will truly be called the city of the Lord, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel, who stands upon the watchtower and has been gathered from both peoples.

60:15.t: Because you were forsaken and hated, and there was none who passed through I will make you the pride of the ages, a joy from generation to generation; and you will suck the milk of the nations, and you will be suckled at the breast of kings. And you will know that I am the Lord who saves you, and your redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob. LXX: Because you were forsaken and hated, and there was none who helped, I will make you an everlasting exultation, a joy of generations unto generations. And you will suck the milk of the nations, and you will eat the riches of kings. And you will know that I am the Lord who has saved you, and who has rescued you, the God of Jacob. […]

60:16.t: You will suck too the milk of the nations, and you will be suckled at the breast of kings. What sense this passage has we explained more fully above, when discussing the little verse, Your sons will come from afar, and your daughters will suck at your side. Or, according to the Seventy, you will eat the riches of kings. These riches, according to the Hebrew truth, are the breasts of kings and teachers, by which the infancy of those born in Christ is instructed and nourished. When you have sucked these and have come to solid food, so that you also eat the riches of such kings, then you will know that I am your Savior, who redeemed you with my blood, or the mighty God of Jacob.

60:17.t: For bronze I will bring gold, for iron I will bring silver, and for wood bronze, and for stones iron; and I will make your visitation peace, and your overseers righteousness. Iniquity will no more be heard in your land, devastation and destruction in your borders; and salvation will occupy your walls, and praise your gates. LXX: For bronze I will bring you gold, and for iron I will give you silver, and for wood I will grant you bronze, and for stones iron. And I will give your princes in peace, and your bishops in righteousness; and iniquity will no more be heard in your land, nor destruction and misery in your borders; but your walls will be called salvation, and your gates carving. The same thing, according to the nature of its position, is a genus to one, a species to another. And so as not to seem to say anything about the arts of rhetoric and dialectic, I shall give common examples which can instruct the simple reader. […]

I will make, he says, your princes in peace, and your bishops in righteousness. For which it is written in the Hebrew: I will make your visitation peace, and your overseers righteousness. Here is the admirable majesty of holy Scripture, that it named the future princes of the Church bishops, all of whose visitation is in peace, and the title of whose dignity is in righteousness: so that they do not respect persons in judgment, and nothing unjust is heard in the land of the Church, nor destruction and unhappiness in her borders. For wherever there is iniquity, and righteousness is not kept, and peace is lost, all these things follow.

60:18.t: But instead of all these, he says, salvation will occupy your walls, or the Savior, which in the Hebrew reads JESUS, which properly sounds as the name of the Lord. For he himself is the strength of the walls of the Church, which has her gates in the praise of the Lord, so that those who enter her may first learn to praise the Lord and to confess his name. But as for the Seventy having translated γλύμμα, that is, carving, instead of praise, we can say this: that the gates of the Church, through which we enter her, ought to be engraved with all the virtues.

60:19.t: We must keep in mind, however, that the Word promises to the righteous through the mouth of Isaiah that days will come when not the sun but the Lord will be to them an everlasting light, and God will be their glory. And it is from misunderstanding, I think, some pestilent heresy that gave an interpretation to the words "let there be light," as if they were the expression of a wish merely on the part of the Creator, that Celsus made the remark, "The Creator did not borrow light from above, like those persons who kindle lamps at those of their neighbors."

You will no longer have the sun to give light by day, nor will the brightness of the moon illumine you; but the Lord will be to you an everlasting light, and your God will be your glory. Your sun will no more go down, and your moon will not wane, for the Lord will be an everlasting light, and the days of your mourning will be ended. LXX: And you will no longer have the sun for the light of day, nor will the rising of the moon give you light by night; but the Lord will be to you an eternal light, and God your glory. For the sun will not go down for you, and the moon will not fail you. And the Lord will be an everlasting light, and the days of your mourning will be ended. From this passage we are compelled to refer everything that has been said and is still to be said to the last time, when, as heaven and earth pass away, the office of the sun and the moon will cease, and the Lord himself will be a perpetual light; […]

It is lifted up, so that it may see Jerusalem in a threefold way: as standing in heaven, coming down from heaven, and going up to heaven. In no other way can the soul be contemplative. Isaias speaks of the first: "Rise up in splendor, Jerusalem. No longer shall the sun be your light by day, nor the brightness of the moon shine upon you at night; the Lord shall be your light forever."

60:21.t: And your people will all be righteous; they will inherit the land for ever, the shoot of my planting, the work of my hand, for glorifying. The least will become a thousand, and the little one a very mighty nation. I the Lord will do this suddenly in its time. LXX: Your people, all righteous, will possess the land for ever, keeping the planting, the works of their hands, for glory. He who is small will become thousands, and he who is least a great nation. I the Lord will gather them in time. When the days of mourning are finished and completed, when sorrow will be turned into joy, the people of Zion will be all righteous, not for a short time but for ever; and because it is righteous, it will possess the land of the gentle. […]

60:22.t: Then he who was a little one will become thousands, hearing from the Lord: Have authority over five or ten cities (Luke 19:17, 19), so that he is called a χιλίαρχος. And he who had said with the Apostle, To me, the least of all the saints, this grace was given (Eph 3:8), will be prince of a great nation in the heavens, when at the appointed time the Lord sends his angels, and they gather to him all the saints from the height of heaven to its summit (Matt 24): not only from Israel but also from the people of the nations, signifying whom he said: And I have other sheep which are not of this fold, and them also I must gather, that there may be one flock and one shepherd (John 10:16). And he will do this suddenly, so that when everything has been despaired of, then they may be gathered into a very mighty nation. And although we see these things being fulfilled in part daily in the Church, yet they will be more fully fulfilled at the consummation of the world and at the second coming of the Savior.

61:1.t: For Christ did not at that time descend upon Jesus, neither was Christ one and Jesus another: but the Word of God-who is the Saviour of all, and the ruler of heaven and earth, who is Jesus, as I have already pointed out, who did also take upon Him flesh, and was anointed by the Spirit from the Father-was made Jesus Christ, as Esaias also says, "There shall come forth a rod from the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise from his root; and the Spirit of God shall rest upon Him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and piety, and the spirit of the fear of God, shall fill Him. He shall not judge according to glory, nor reprove after the manner of speech; but He shall dispense judgment to the humble man, and reprove the haughty ones of the earth." […]

...the Son of God having been made the Son of man, as the very name itself doth declare. For in the name of Christ is implied, He that anoints, He that is anointed, and the unction itself with which He is anointed. And it is the Father who anoints, but the Son who is anointed by the Spirit, who is the unction, as the Word declares by Isaiah, "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because He hath anointed me," -pointing out both the anointing Father, the anointed Son, and the unction, which is the Spirit.

Let us therefore contemplate what those things are which he spoke in the prophet and afterward sounds forth about himself in the synagogue. "He sent me", it says, "to evangelize the poor". The "poor" signifies the nations; for these were "poor", possessing nothing at all, not God, not the law, not the prophets, not justice and the remaining virtues. For which cause God sent him to announce to the poor: "to preach release to the captives". Captives we were, whom for so many years Satan had bound, holding us captive and subject to himself. Jesus came "to preach release to the captives and to the blind, that they might see"; for indeed by the word and preaching of his teaching the blind see. Let the preaching therefore be understood ἀπὸ κοινοῦ (in common), not only over the captives, but also over the blind. "To send forth the broken into liberty". What was ever so broken and crushed as man, who was released and healed by Jesus? "To preach the acceptable year of the Lord". […]
61:1.s: HOMILIES ON THE GOSPEL OF LUKE 32

61:1.t:
MY witness of this shall be from the words of Isaiah, who cries in the Person of Christ:

"The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has sent me to preach good news to the poor, to proclaim deliverance to the captives, and recovery of sight to the blind."

Our Saviour, after reading this prophecy through in the Synagogue one day to a multitude of Jews, shut the book and said: "This day is this Scripture fulfilled in your ears." And beginning His own teaching from that point He began to preach the Gospel to the poor, putting in the forefront of His blessings: "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven." Yea, and to those who were hampered by evil spirits, and bound for a long time like slaves by daemons, He proclaimed forgiveness, inviting all to be free and to escape from the bonds of sin, when He said: "Come unto me, all ye that labour, and are heavy laden, and I will refresh you." […]
61:1.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 3, Chapter 1

61:1.t:
Now listen to Isaiah prophesying in the clearest words thus about Christ, as one to be sent by God to men as their Redeemer and Saviour, and coming to preach forgiveness to those in bondage of spirit, and recovery of sight to the blind. For here again the prophet teaches that the Christ has been anointed not with a prepared unguent, but with the spiritual and divine anointing of His Father's Divinity, conferred not by man but by the Father. He says then in the person of Christ:

"The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me. He has sent me to preach glad tidings to the poor, to proclaim liberty to the captives, to heal the broken in heart, and recovery of sight to the blind."

Let this point then be regarded as certain, that Isaiah, equally with David, prophesies that He that should come to mankind to preach liberty to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind would not be anointed with a prepared unguent, but with an anointing of the power of His Father Unbegotten and Perfect. […]
61:1.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 4, Chapter 15

61:1.t:
And we should here again remember Isaiah, who said:

"The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, for whose sake he hath anointed me. He has sent me to preach the gospel to the poor, to heal the broken-hearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and sight to the blind."

And we have already shewn that the priests from among men, who in long distant times were consecrated to the service of God, were anointed with a prepared unguent. But he that is spoken of in the prophecy is said to have been anointed with the Divine Spirit. And this passage in its entirety was referred to Jesus the only true Christ of God, Who one day took the prophecy in the Jewish synagogue, and after reading the selected portion, said that what He had read was fulfilled in Himself. For it is written, that having read it:

"And closing the book, and giving it to the minister, he sat down. And the eyes of all them that were in the synagogue were fastened upon him, 21. And he began to say unto them, This day is this Scripture fulfilled in your ears."
61:1.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 4, Chapter 16

61:1.t:
[Passage quoted, Isa. lxi. 1.]

Now this prediction our Lord Himself claims to be fulfilled in Himself, when He came to Nazareth, where He was brought up:

"He entered, as his custom was on the Sabbath day, into the synagogue, and stood up to read. And there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Esaias. And when he had opened the book he found the place where it was written, The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me, to preach the gospel to the poor: he hath sent me to proclaim deliverance to the captives, and giving of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord. And he closed the book, and he gave it again to the minister, and sat down. And the eyes of all them that were in the synagogue were fastened upon him. And he began to say unto them, This day is this Scripture fulfilled in your ears." […]
61:1.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 9, Chapter 10

61:1.t:
And he was not anointed with oil prepared from material substances, but, as befits divinity, with the divine Spirit himself, by participation in the unbegotten deity of the Father. And this is taught also again by Isaiah, who exclaims, as if in the person of Christ himself, "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me; therefore hath he anointed me. He hath sent me to preach the Gospel to the poor, to proclaim deliverance to captives, and recovery of sight to the blind."

And not only Isaiah, but also David addresses him, saying, "Thy throne, O God, is forever and ever. A scepter of equity is the scepter of thy kingdom. Thou hast loved righteousness and hast hated iniquity. Therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows." Here the Scripture calls him God in the first verse, in the second it honors him with a royal scepter. […]

What is there to wonder at, what to disbelieve, if the Lord who gives the Spirit, is here said himself to be anointed with the Spirit, at a time when, necessity requiring it, he did not refuse in respect of his manhood to call himself inferior to the Spirit?

Let no one be misled by the fact of the apostle's frequently omitting the name of the Father and of the Holy Spirit when making mention of baptism, or on this account imagine that the invocation of the names is not observed. "As many of you," he says, "as were baptized into Christ have put on Christ;" and again, "As many of you as were baptized into Christ were baptized into his death." For the naming of Christ is the confession of the whole, shewing forth as it does the God who gave, the Son who received, and the Spirit who is, the unction. So we have learned from Peter, in the Acts, of "Jesus of Nazareth whom God anointed with the Holy Ghost;" and in Isaiah, "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because the Lord hath anointed me;" and the Psalmist, "Therefore God, even thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows." Scripture, however, in the case of baptism, sometimes plainly mentions the Spirit alone.

"For into one Spirit," it says, "we were all baptized in one body." […]

We have shown by the clear evidence of the Scripture that the apostles and prophets were appointed, the latter to prophesy, the former to preach the gospel, by the Holy Spirit in the same way as by the Father and the Son. Now we add what all will rightly wonder at and not be able to doubt, that the Spirit was on Christ; and that as he sent the Spirit, so the Spirit sent the Son of God. For the Son of God says, "The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has appointed me, he has sent me to preach the gospel." And having read this from the book of Isaiah, he says in the Gospel, "Today has this Scripture been fulfilled in your ears," that he might point out that it was said of himself.

Here is the one who says, "My teaching is not mine but his who sent me. If anyone wants to do his will, let him know about the teaching, whether it is from God or I am speaking by my own authority." For one is teaching from God, the other is human teaching. Thus, the Jews, when they asked whether his teaching was taken from people, saying, "How has he known these writings without learning them?" Jesus replied, "My teaching is not mine."

He is anointed with spiritual oil and heavenly power, that he might water the poverty of the human condition with the eternal treasure of the resurrection, turn away the captivity of the mind, enlighten the blindness of minds, proclaim the year of the Lord, spread over endless times, a year which knows no return into a round of toil, and which grants men a continuance of fruit and of rest.

The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the meek, to heal the broken in heart, and to preach indulgence to the captives, and opening to those who are shut in; and to proclaim a year of favor to the Lord, and a day of vengeance to our God; to comfort all who mourn; to appoint for those who mourn in Zion, and to give them a crown instead of ashes, the oil of joy instead of mourning, a mantle of praise instead of a spirit of sorrow. LXX: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me; he has sent me to preach the gospel to the poor, to heal the broken in heart, to preach remission to the captives and sight to the blind, to call an acceptable year to the Lord, and a day of retribution, to comfort all who mourn, to give to those who mourn in Zion, to give them glory instead of ashes, the anointing of gladness to those who mourn, a garment of glory instead of a spirit of sorrow. […]

He who said in the preceding words concerning those who would be called in faith: "I the Lord will gather them at the proper times," as the time was already present, in which he promised to gather them, and as one who had already become man, and had undergone the likeness to us, and had lowered himself to emptiness, "The Spirit of the Lord," he says, "is upon me," although being by nature God the Only-begotten is the Holy of holies, and he himself sanctifies all creation, since indeed he is begotten of a holy Father, and pours forth the Spirit from himself, and sends it into the powers above as his own, and moreover to those who have recognized his epiphany. How then was he sanctified? For being at once God and the same one man, he gives the Spirit divinely to creation, but he receives it from God the Father according to his humanity. This we say is the use. And he makes clear the cause of the incarnation. For having said that it was from the Father, he necessarily added, "Because of which he has anointed me; […]

The Spirit of the Lord is upon Me; therefore He hath anointed Me: He hath sent Me to preach the Gospel to the poor.

He plainly shews by these words that He took upon Him the humiliation and submission to the emptying (of His glory), and both the very name of Christ and the reality for our sakes: for the Spirit, He says, which by nature is in Me by the sameness of Our substance and deity, also descended upon Me from without. And so also in the Jordan It came upon Me in the form of a dove, not because It was not in Me, but for the reason for which He anointed Me. And what was the reason for which He chose to be anointed? It was our being destitute of the Spirit by that denunciation of old, "My Spirit shall not abide in these men, because they are flesh." […]
61:1.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

61:1.t: And what means the sending away the broken in freedom? It is the letting those go free whom Satan had broken by the rod of spiritual violence. And what means the preaching the acceptable year of the Lord? It signifies the joyful tidings of His own advent, that the time of the Lord, even the Son, had arrived. For that was the acceptable year in which Christ was crucified in our behalf, because we then were made acceptable unto God the Father, as the fruit borne by Him. Wherefore He said, "When I am lifted up from the earth, I shall draw all men unto Myself." And verily He returned to life the third day, having trampled upon the power of death: after which He said to His disciples, "All power has been given Me, &c." That too is in every respect an acceptable year in which, being received into His family, we were admitted unto Him, having washed away sin by holy baptism, and been made partakers of His divine nature by the communion of the Holy Ghost. […]
61:1.s: Commentary on the Gospel of Luke

61:1.t: The spirit of the Lord is upon me—a passage which the Lord having read in the synagogue on the Sabbath said: Verily I say unto you, to-day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.

61:2.t: WHY HAVE THE DEEDS AND SAYINGS OF THE LORD BEEN ARRANGED IN WRITING IN FOUR BOOKS BY FOUR AUTHORS? — It was fitting that the acceptable year of the Lord, as the prophet says (Isa. 61:2), should be contained in four books as if in four seasons. For just as the year unfolds in four seasons, in such a way that they need one another, so too the deeds and sayings of the Lord have been set forth in four books, in such a way that each one needs the others; yet together they form perfect fullness. And as to why they were ordered by four writers, this was the reason: because the names of the seasons are different, so also the titles of the Gospels should be different. And if anything in their wording seems contrary, yet in meaning they do not differ, thanks to an interpretation suitably adapted to the matter: just as the seasons, although they clearly differ in name, in climate, and in the course of the stars, yet do not differ in the effects of the things they bring forth.
61:2.s: QUESTIONS ON THE OLD AND NEW TESTAMENTS, QUESTION 1: ON WHY THERE ARE FOUR GOSPELS

61:2.t: By the acceptable year and the day of retribution understand the whole time of his preaching, during which he lived in the flesh. This the apostle Paul too interprets of the first coming of the Savior, saying: Behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation (2 Cor 6:2). Of this we spoke more fully above (cf. Isa 60). But if retribution is taken not in the rewards of the good but in the punishments of sinners, in accordance with its being called the day of vengeance, it must be understood of the Jewish people, upon whom, after his passion, the wrath of God came at once.

And he comforted all who mourn, saying: Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted (Matt 5:5), so that he might appoint for those who mourn in Zion, and give them glory and a crown instead of ashes. Among these was the apostle Paul too, who mourned for Zion and said: For I have sorrow and continual grief (Rom 9:2); and again: I could wish that I myself were anathema from Christ for my brethren and kinsmen according to the flesh, who are Israelites (ibid., 3). And therefore those who mourned and lamented received the oil of joy instead of ashes, seeing that very many of the Jews had believed and were receiving a most pure robe instead of the garment of mourning.

61:3.t: And in her they will be called the mighty ones of righteousness, the planting of the Lord for glorifying. And they will build the places deserted from of old, and raise up the ancient ruins, and restore the cities deserted and scattered from generation to generation. And strangers will stand and feed your flocks, and the sons of foreigners will be your farmers and vinedressers. LXX: And they will be called generations of righteousness, the planting of the Lord for glory. And they will build the everlasting desert places; those that had formerly been made desolate will be raised up, and they will renew the deserted cities, desolate for generations; and foreigners will come and feed your sheep, and ploughmen and vinedressers of other nations. After both the Apostles and apostolic men have received, instead of ashes and a spirit of sorrow, the oil of joy and the mantle, or, according to the Seventy, the robe of glory and praise, then they will be called generations of righteousness, the glorious planting of the Lord; […]

61:5.t: They will have not only the skill of building and restoring cities, but they will also be the best of shepherds, so that, the old shepherds being driven away, to whom God had said through Ezekiel, O shepherds of Israel, do shepherds feed themselves, and not rather the sheep (Ezek 34:2)?, they may hear with the apostle Peter: Feed my sheep (John 21:17). And in a wonderful manner they will pass from masons and shepherds to farmers, that is, to ploughmen and vinedressers, so that they may say with the Apostle: We are God's building, God's husbandry (1 Cor 3:9). Thus the Savior asks the scribes and Pharisees, the vinedressers and farmers of the Jews, what he will do to the wicked vinedressers and farmers; and when they answered, He will destroy the wicked wickedly, and give the vineyard to other farmers (Matt 21:41), he went on: The kingdom of God will be taken from you and given to a nation producing its fruits (ibid., 43). The matter needs no interpretation. […]

61:6.t: But you will be called the priests of the Lord; it will be said to you, ministers of our God. You will eat the strength of the nations, and you will pride yourselves in their glory. Instead of your double confusion and shame they will praise their portion; therefore in their land they will possess double things; everlasting gladness will be theirs; for I am the Lord who loves judgment, and hates robbery in burnt offering. LXX: But you will be called the priests of the Lord, ministers of our God. You will eat the strength of the nations, and in their riches you will be admirable. Thus they will possess the land a second time, and everlasting joy will be upon their head. For I am the Lord who love righteousness and hate robberies from iniquity. […]

61:7.t: And what follows, Instead of double confusion and instead of shame they will praise their portion, which is not found in the Seventy, I think should be explained thus: Because you had a double confusion, both over the people of the Jews, which had departed from God, and over the nations, which served idols, you will see them, converted to the fear of God, praising their portion: without doubt the Lord, of whom the holy man also spoke: My portion is the Lord (Ps 72 [73]:26). No one can say this except one who has no other portion. Because, then, you had over them a double confusion and the shame of their sin, over which they themselves did not blush, therefore in their land, that is, in the land of the gentle and of the living, they will possess double things, since they will have believed both in the things present and in the things to come. And they will have everlasting gladness. For which we read in the Seventy, thus they will possess the land a second time. […]

About this twin glory it is written, "they will possess double in their own land." This is written concerning the souls of the saints, for single white cloaks are given to them, and it is said that they might have rest a short time until the number of their colleagues and brothers is filled up. So they take now single cloaks, but they will have double cloaks on the day of judgment; for the first is in the way of souls only, but later they will rejoice in the glory of souls and bodies together.

61:8.t: This the Lord has granted, who loves the truth of judgment and hates robbery in burnt offering. For which the Seventy translated robbery from iniquity, as though there were some robbery that did not consist of iniquity. What he says, then, is this: God loves the poverty of the righteous more than the gifts of the rich, which come from robberies and iniquity.

And I will give their work in truth, and I will strike an everlasting covenant with them. And their seed will be known among the nations, and their offspring in the midst of the peoples. All who see them will recognize them, that these are the seed which the Lord has blessed. LXX: And I will give their labor to the righteous, and I will set an eternal testament with them. And their seed will be known among the nations, and their descendants in the midst of the peoples. Everyone who sees them will recognize them, that these are the seed blessed by God. God, who loves righteousness and judgment and detests violent burnt offerings (for whatever comes from robbery he reckons as the hire of a harlot and the price of a dog), will himself give the labor of those who will possess the land a second time, and whom he will have crowned with a double gladness, to the righteous, or, as is better in the Hebrew, in truth: so that it is no longer, as in the Law, the shadow of the truth, but the truth itself. […]

For those offerings of fasts, which we thoughtlessly extort by violently tearing our bowels, and fancy that we rightly offer to the Lord, these He execrates who "loves mercy and judgment" saying: "I the Lord love judgment, but I hate robbery in a burnt offering."
61:8.s: The First Conference of Abbot Theonas, Chapter 22

61:8.t: But it is one thing to show mercy for sins, another to sin for the sake of showing mercy, which cannot really be called mercy since it does not issue in sweet fruit, since it is embittered through the influence of a diseased root. For here the Lord rebukes such sacrifices through the prophet, saying, "I, the Lord, love justice and hate robbery with whole burnt offerings." … Such people also often withdraw from the poor what they give to God. But the Lord shows how strongly he disowns and censures such conduct.
61:8.s: The Book of Pastoral Rule, Part 3, Chapter 21

61:9.t: And then the apostolic seed will be known among the nations, and all future generations will receive the sowing of God's doctrine; by no means saying that in which the people of the circumcision formerly erred, saying: For what else does God seek but seed? Everyone who sees them will recognize at first sight that they are the seed which the Lord has blessed. For who would not recognize the people of God from their manner of life, their gentleness, continence, hospitality and all their virtues? And who, on the contrary, would not detest the bloody hands of Israel, against whom the Prophet prays, saying: Fill their faces with shame, O Lord (Ps 82 [83]:17)?

61:10.t:
But for the present, she that was formerly widowed and desolate is clothed by the grace of God with these flowers, and is become truly like a lily, as the prophecy says, and having received the bridal garment and the crown of beauty, she is taught by Isaiah to dance, and to present her thank-offerings unto God the King in reverent words.

Let us hear her saying, 'My soul shall rejoice in the Lord; for he hath clothed me with a garment of salvation and with a robe of gladness; he hath bedecked me like a bridegroom with a garland, and he hath adorned me like a bride with jewels; and like the earth which bringeth forth her bud, and like a garden which causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth, thus the Lord God hath caused righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations.'

In these words she exults. And in similar words the heavenly bridegroom, the Word Jesus Christ himself, answers her. […]

Rejoicing I will rejoice in the Lord, and there has exulted my soul in my God: for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, and with the vesture of righteousness he has encompassed me, as a bridegroom adorned with a crown, and as a bride decked with her jewels. For as the earth brings forth its shoot, and as a garden makes its seed spring up, so the Lord God will make righteousness and praise spring up before all the nations. LXX: With joy they will be glad in the Lord; let my soul exult in the Lord. For he has clothed me with the garment of salvation, and has put about me the tunic of gladness. As a bridegroom with a mitre, and as a bride he has adorned me with a woman's finery, and as the earth putting forth its flower, and as a garden makes its seeds spring up, so the Lord God brings forth righteousness and praise in the sight of all the nations. The beginning of the passage according to the Seventy, who said, With joy they will be glad in the Lord, is joined to the end of the preceding passage. […]

But whether Head speaketh or whether members speak, Christ speaketh: He speaketh in the person of the Head, He speaketh in the person of the Body. But what hath been said?
