There shall be two in one flesh. “This is a great Sacrament:” “I,” he saith, “speak in Christ and in the Church.” And He Himself in the Gospel, “Therefore no longer two, but one flesh.” For in order that ye may know these in a manner to be two persons, and again one by the bond of marriage, as one He speaketh in Isaiah, and saith, “As upon a Bridegroom he hath bound upon me a mitre, and as a Bride he hath clothed me with an ornament.” A Bridegroom He hath called Himself in the Head, a Bride in the Body. He is speaking therefore as One, let us hear Him, and in Him let us also speak.

61:11.t: And she sets forth examples of another comparison, of which the first refers to the bridegroom, the next to the bride. As the earth brings forth its shoot and is watered by the rains of heaven, and as a garden makes its seed spring up, which longs for the waters of springs and rivers, so, he says, the Lord will make righteousness and gladness spring up before all the nations: by no means before Israel, so as to strike down the haughtiness of the Jews, but before all the nations, which are gathered in the Church.

Therefore, those who had been scattered returned, preaching the word of God. Instead of "the dispersed," the Greek text has "disseminated," that is, scattered like seed, for they were those about whom Isaiah said, "their offspring in the midst of the peoples" and about whom the Lord in the parable of the Gospel said, "the good seed is those sons of the kingdom." For this seed was disseminated throughout many regions, so that the harvest of faith that started in Jerusalem filled first Judea and Samaria and then the whole world. About these same ones, dispersed or rather disseminated through the next generations, it is said that they spoke the word not only to Jews but also to Greeks, and the noblest foundations of the new church in Antioch were planted through these.

62:1.t: For Zion's sake I will not be silent, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, until her righteous one goes forth as brightness, and her savior is kindled as a lamp. And the nations will see your righteous one, and all kings your renowned one, and a new name will be called for you, which the mouth of the Lord has named. And you will be a crown of glory in the hand of the Lord, and a diadem of the kingdom in the hand of your God. LXX: For Zion's sake I will not be silent, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not leave off, until her righteousness goes forth as light, and her salvation burns as a lamp. And the nations will see your righteousness, and all kings your glory, and he will call you by a new name, which the mouth of the Lord will name. And you will be a crown of beauty in the hand of the Lord, and a diadem of the kingdom in the hand of your God. […]

62:2.t: And all kings will see your renowned one, O Jerusalem and Zion: he who was begotten of your stock, who, lifted up in you on the gibbet, drew all men to himself; so that the nations see his righteousness, by which the Creator of all has had mercy on the nations, and kings his glory, by which he was glorified on the cross and subjected all kingdoms to his rule. Indeed she will no longer be called Jerusalem and Zion, but she will receive a new name, which the Lord will have given her, saying to the apostle Peter: You are Peter, and upon this rock I will build my Church, and the gates of hell will not prevail against it (Matt 16:18). This title he derived from the name of the Lord, so that she is called the Lord's. And her people will no longer be called by the old name, Israel, but by a new one, that is, Christian.

62:3.t: And she will be as a crown of beauty in the hand of the Lord, and as a diadem of the kingdom in the hand of her God, when the throng of believers has crowned her, and the diadem of empire, which the Martyrs have adorned with the variety of their gems, is in the hand of God, that he may crown his Son with their victories. Hence the apostle Paul too said to the saints: My joy and my crown.

"You will be a crown of beauty in the hand of the Lord, and a royal diadem in the hand of your God." For each holy soul, and the Church as a whole, that is, the communities of the saints, must be compared to a crown composed of many flowers, or to a royal diadem, shining with Indian stones, and having manifold excellence: for the heroic deeds of the saints are very many, and the manner of their boasts is not one, but many and various. And indeed the divine David introduces the Church of Christ clothed in gold-fringed garments, variegated, but the phrase "In the hand of the Lord," he says, that is, under the shadow of my hand I will cover you: and Christ himself somewhere concerning his own flock, that is, of the flock of those who have believed in him, says, that "No one will snatch them out of my Father's hand."

62:4.t: You will no longer be called Forsaken, and your land will no more be called Desolate; but you will be called My-will-is-in-her, and your land Inhabited, for the Lord has been well pleased in you, and your land will be inhabited. LXX: And you will no longer be called Forsaken, and your land will not be called Deserted any more. For you will be called My will, and your land Inhabited. Instead of Zion and Jerusalem you will be called the Church and the Lord's; instead of Jews they will be called Christians. Nor will you be content with this end of names; but you who before were called forsaken, which in Hebrew is AZUBA (עזובה), will be called EPESI-BA (חפצי־בה), which means my will is in her; and your land, which before was called SEMEMA (שממה), desolate or deserted, will afterwards be called BULA (בעולה), which Aquila translated ἐσχημένη, Symmachus and Theodotion συνωκισμένη, the Seventy οἰκουμένη, all of which signify inhabited and possessed. […]

62:5.t: For the young man will dwell with the virgin, and your sons will dwell in you. And the bridegroom will rejoice over the bride; your God will rejoice over you. LXX: And as a young man dwelling with a virgin, so will your sons dwell. And it will be that as a bridegroom is glad over a bride, so the Lord will be glad over you. The Apostle too says: Husbands, love your wives, as Christ also loved the Church (Eph 5:25). And when in another place he had set down the example, For this reason a man will leave his father and mother, and will cleave to his wife, and the two will be in one flesh, he added: This is a great mystery; but I speak in Christ and in the Church (Eph 5:31, 32). If, then, because of the shortness of the time, which is straitened, husbands ought so to have their wives as though they had them not, how much more holy will the union between the bridegroom and the bride be? This is the bridegroom of whom it is sung in the eighteenth psalm: And he as a bridegroom coming forth from his chamber (Ps 18 [19]:6). […]

62:6.t: But they who are babes in understanding say:—“If no one has received his reward, why did the Apostle say, When we shall depart from the body, we shall be present with the Lord?” But recollect, my beloved, that I instructed thee concerning this matter in the Demonstration concerning Solitaries, that the spirit which the righteous receive, according to its heavenly nature, goes to our Lord until the time of the Resurrection, when it shall come to put on the body in which it dwelt. And at every time it has the memory of this in the presence of God, and looks eagerly for the Resurrection of that body in which it dwelt, as the Prophet Isaiah said about the Church of the Gentiles:—They that make mention of thee shall be faithful and stand before the Lord, and thou shalt not give them rest. But as to the wicked, they have none to make mention of them before the Lord, because the Holy Spirit is far removed from them, because they are animal, and are buried after the manner of animals.
62:6.s: Demonstration 8 (Of the Resurrection of the Dead), Section 23

62:6.t: Upon your walls, Jerusalem, I have set watchmen; all the day and all the night they will never be silent. You who remember the Lord, do not be silent, and give him no silence, until he establishes, and until he makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth. LXX: And upon your walls, Jerusalem, I have set watchmen, all the day and all the night, who will never be silent, remembering the Lord: for there is none like you if he corrects, and he will make Jerusalem a joy upon the earth. The Prophet had said, For Zion's sake I will not be silent, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest, and the rest, up to the place where the passage has now ended: The bridegroom will rejoice over the bride; your God will rejoice over you. And he had promised that he would pray by day and by night that the Savior and Righteous One who had been promised might come and, like a lamp, light up the whole world. […]

62:7.t: Give him no silence, understand: the Lord; but be always troublesome, in season, out of season, and imitate the woman who importuned the hard judge. For if he laid aside the fierceness of his mind because of constant entreaty, how much more will the heavenly Father give good things to those who ask him? And you ought to ask for as long as it takes until Jerusalem, which fell in the Jews and is become an example and a curse, is turned into the praise of the whole world. And I wonder what the Seventy meant, instead of what is in the Hebrew, give him no silence, until he establishes and makes Jerusalem a praise in the earth, by saying what does not cohere in sense with what precedes: For there is none like you, if he corrects, and makes Jerusalem a joy upon the earth. Unless perhaps we fit it together with artful speech, so that it is said to the watchmen of the Church that there will be none like those who by their preaching have brought it about that Jerusalem is corrected and becomes the joy of the whole earth.

62:8.t: The Lord has sworn by his right hand and by the arm of his strength: If I give your wheat any more as food to your enemies, and if the sons of strangers drink your wine, for which you have labored! For those who gather it will eat it and praise the Lord, and those who bring it in will drink it in my holy courts. LXX: The Lord has sworn by his right hand and by the strength of his arm: If I give my wheat any more to be food for your enemies, and if the sons of strangers drink any more your wine for which you have labored! But those who have gathered will eat it and praise the Lord, and those who have gathered will drink it in my holy courts. Almighty God, who had said to the Church, Upon your walls I have set watchmen, who will never be silent, and whom I bid never to cease praying until they obtain what they pray for, now swears by his right hand and the arm of his strength. Of this we have often said that it is our Lord and Savior, who according to the Apostle is the power of God and the wisdom of God (1 Cor 1). […]

62:10.t: This I seemed to hear Him say, and to see Him do, and besides, to hear Him shouting to His people, which once were few and scattered and miserable, and have now become many, and compact enough and enviable, Go through My gates and be ye enlarged. Must you always be in trouble and dwell in tents, while those who vex you rejoice exceedingly? And to the presiding Angels, for I believe, as John teaches me in his Revelation, that each Church has its guardian, Prepare ye the way of My people, and cast away the stones from the way, that there may be no stumblingblock or hindrance for the people in the divine road and entrance, now, to the temples made with hands, but soon after, to Jerusalem above, and the Holy of holies there, which will, I know, be the end of suffering and struggle to those who here bravely travel on the way.

Pass through, pass through the gates, prepare the way for the people, make the road level, and pick out the stones; lift up a signal to the peoples. Behold, the Lord has made it heard at the ends of the earth: say to the daughter of Zion, Behold, your Savior comes; behold, his reward is with him, and his work before him. And they will call them a holy people, redeemed by the Lord. But you will be called a city sought out, and not forsaken. LXX: Go through my gates, and make a way for my people, and throw the stones off the way. Lift up a signal to the nations; for behold, the Lord has made it heard to the end of the earth. Say to the daughter of Zion: Behold, your Savior comes, having his reward with him, and his work before his face; and he will call it a holy people, redeemed by the Lord. But you will be called a city sought after, and not forsaken. […]

Although before we had thorns and thistles, although stones, it is said to us in Isaiah: "And cast the stones out of the way." And He says this for the reason, that when He wishes to walk about in our way, He may not stub His foot. The stones which are in the way, and are commanded to be cast out, are our sins. Christ does not walk in our heart, if there be any sin: at once He stumbles against the stones.

And lest the Jews should think this was said of themselves, there is joined to it: Lift up a signal to the nations, and to the peoples of the Gentiles, so that it is not the narrow confines of the one land of Judea that are called to salvation, but the message is made heard at the ends of the earth, so that the whole world may hear of the passion of the Creator of all.

62:11.t: Say, he says, to the daughter of Zion. She is called the daughter of Zion either because she first arose from the Jews, she of whom it says in the Song of Songs, The sons of my mother have fought against me (Song 1:5); or certainly she is called daughter because she received from God the name of adoption. For as many as received him, to them he gave power to become sons of God (John 1). And what is it that the masters and teachers are bidden to announce to the daughter of Zion? Behold, your Savior comes, who in the Hebrew is called Jesus. Hence Gabriel too, to Joseph: And you will call, he says, his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins (Matt 1:21). This Savior is the judge of all believers, to render to each according to his works: to the righteous rewards, to sinners everlasting punishments (Matt 16).

62:12.t: And he will call, he says, them, the Lord and Savior himself. Or, according to the Hebrew, they will call them, the Apostles and apostolic men, a holy people, and redeemed by the Lord, who have been redeemed by the blood of Christ. The city itself too will by no means be called forsaken, as she had been called before, whether among the Jews because of their trafficking, or among the nations because of their idolatry, but sought after, as it is said in Hebrew DRUSA (דרושת); so that, according to the growth and variety of their virtues, they may always receive new names.

63:1.t: He likewise, when mentioning the cup and making the New Testament to be sealed "in his blood," affirms the reality of Christ's body. For no blood can belong to a body that is not a body of flesh. If any sort of body were presented to our view, which is not one of flesh, not being fleshly, it would not possess blood. In order, however, that you might discover how anciently wine is used as a figure for blood, turn to Isaiah, who asks, "Who is this that comes from Edom, from Bosor with garments dyed in red, so glorious in his apparel, in the greatness of his might? Why are your garments red, and your clothing as his who comes from the treading of the full winepress?" The prophetic Spirit contemplates the Lord as if he were already on his way to his passion, clad in his fleshly nature; […]

Blessed is that soul which, by the gore of blood poured out in martyrdom, casts down the airy throngs of demons that meet it. Blessed is he of whom, as he goes to heaven, the angels speak that prophetic word: "Who is this that comes up from Bozrah?"—that is, who ascends from the flesh to heaven. "Who is this that comes up from Bozrah, the redness of his garments?"—by the "redness of his garments" signifying the gore of blood. Blessed, then, are the souls that so follow Christ as Christ went before them. And therefore, because they so follow, they arrive even at the very altar of God, where the Lord Jesus Christ Himself is, the "high priest of the good things to come," "to whom is glory and power unto the ages of ages. Amen!"

And if He ascend up into Heaven, ascend with Him. Be one of those angels who escort Him, or one of those who receive Him. Bid the gates be lifted up, or be made higher, that they may receive Him, exalted after His Passion. Answer to those who are in doubt because He bears up with Him His body and the tokens of His Passion, which He had not when He came down, and who therefore inquire, "Who is this King of Glory?" that it is the Lord strong and mighty, as in all things that He hath done from time to time and does, so now in His battle and triumph for the sake of Mankind. And give to the doubting of the question the twofold answer. And if they marvel and say as in Isaiah's drama Who is this that cometh from Edom and from the things of earth? Or How are the garments red of Him that is without blood or body, as of one that treads in the full wine-press? […]

The angels, too, were in doubt when Christ arose; the powers of heaven were in doubt when they saw that flesh was ascending into heaven. Then they said, "Who is this King of glory?" And yet some said, "Lift up your heads, O gates! And be lifted up, O ancient doors! That the King of glory may come in." In Isaiah, too, we find that the powers of heaven doubted.

Who is this who comes from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah? This one, beautiful in his robe, marching in the greatness of his strength. LXX: Who is this who comes from Edom, with tawny garments from Bosor? So beautiful in his robe, violence with strength. This whole passage, from the place where according to the Seventy it is said, Be enlightened, be enlightened, Jerusalem, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you (Isa 60:1), up to the present passage, where it is said, Who is this who comes from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah?, many of our people refer to the end of the world, in which they contend these things are to be fulfilled, whether carnally or spiritually (for the opinion of most is divided). But we, since we read above in this same section too, The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me; […]

The cross of Christ, therefore, has profited not only us, but also the angels and all the virtues in heaven, and has opened a mystery which they did not know before. Accordingly they marvel at God returning to heaven with his body, and say: Who is this who comes up from Edom, his garments tawny from Bozrah, so beautiful in a white robe (Isa. 63:1). And in another place: Who is this king of glory? The Lord of virtues, he is the king of glory (Ps. 23:10).

Furthermore, because Idumea means both earthly and, on account of the color red, can also be understood as bloody, for this reason the Savior, carrying back to the Father the victory over the world, when the angels were crying out: Open your gates, O princes, and the king of glory shall enter in. And in Isaiah, astonished, they were asking: Who is this who comes up from Edom, with garments tawny from Bozrah, so beautiful in a white robe? And one spoke to him face to face: Why is your clothing red, and your garments like those of men who tread in the winepress? He himself speaks in triumph, displaying the palms of his cross: I have trodden the winepress alone, and of the nations there is no man with me.

That your foot may be dipped in blood. Because his own foot was dipped in his own blood. "I have trodden the winepress alone, and of the nations there was no man with me." And again: "Who is this who ascends from Edom? his garments red from Bosor." Edom is interpreted "blood," Bosor "flesh": it signifies our Lord himself crucified.

Isaiah asks: "Who is this that comes from Edom, in crimson garments, from Bosra? 'It is I who announce vindication, I who am mighty to save.'" For that reason, He is called Strong, and from Him come strong defenses. And so all the wars of Scripture refer to the victory of Christ.

63:2.t: Why then is your clothing red, and your garments like those of men treading the winepress? LXX: Why are your garments red, and your clothing like that of men treading the winepress, full and trodden down? Where it now says red, the Hebrew reads EDOM (אדום). So above too, where Edom is written, it is not the name of a place but a word for blood. And again the angels ask and say: We have learned that you are he who speaks righteousness, and that the salvation of all has been placed in your judgment. Now we wish to know why your garments are as if dyed with new wine; or what cause there was for you to stain with blood the tunic that was woven from the top and cannot be torn, and that had from the virgin's womb such whiteness as no fuller on earth could make? For mercy befits you more than cruelty, whiteness more than gore. To them the Lord answered, not with one little verse as before, but with many words, so as to teach everything to those who did not know, lest they be compelled to ask again.

63:3.t: And does not also the Holy Spirit, speaking in Isaiah, testify the same thing concerning the passion of the Lord, saying, "Why are your vestments red and your garments as from treading the wine press full and well-trodden?" For can water make vestments red, or is it water that is trodden by the feet in the winepress or forced out by the press? The mention of wine is placed there, indeed, that in the wine the blood of the Lord may be known and that which was afterward manifested in the chalice of the Lord might be foretold by the prophets who announced it. The treading and pressing of the winepress are also spoken of, since wine cannot be prepared for drinking in any other way unless the cluster of grapes is first trodden and pressed. Thus, we could not drink the blood of Christ unless Christ had first been trodden on and pressed, and unless he had first drunk the chalice of which he should also give believers to drink.
Who is that who for shame is clothed in scarlet? For Bosra among the Hebrews has such a meaning.

I have trodden the winepress alone, and of the nations there is no man with me. I have trodden them in my fury, and trampled them in my wrath; and their blood has been sprinkled upon my garments, and I have polluted all my clothing For the day of vengeance is in my heart; the year of my redemption has come. I looked round, and there was no helper; I sought, and there was none to give aid. And my own arm saved for me, and my indignation itself helped me. And I trampled the peoples in my fury, and made them drunk in my indignation, and brought down their strength to the earth. The Seventy, instead of what we have said, I have trodden the winepress alone, translated full and trodden down, which is rather to be read with the preceding passage than taken as the beginning of the following one. The rest they translated thus: And of the nations there is no man with me; and I trampled them in my fury, and broke them like earth, and brought down their blood to the earth, and I have defiled all my garments. […]

Out of the whole world he chose twelve apostles: out of the twelve one departed, eleven remained. The cross came, ten fled: one Peter remained, one with the One. And that one fled, and would that he had fled: and he denies. Therefore let us say, the whole human race perished. Since it had perished, therefore the Lord, being crucified, said: I have trodden the winepress alone, and of the nations there was not a man with me. At that time the psalm was fulfilled: Save me, O Lord, for the holy one has failed. There is none who does good, there is none, even to one. He who had promised, saying If it be necessary for me to die, or to go into prison, I will not deny you, denied.

Isaiah, when he was speaking of the passion of the Lord, introduced the Lord saying: I have trodden the winepress alone, and of the nations there is no man with me (Isa. 63:3). But there, by the winepress the cross of the Lord is understood; here, however, not the cross, but the place of punishments into which the wicked are to be thrust is signified.

63:4.t: For the day of vengeance, he says, is in my heart; the year of my redemption has come. Of this we read above too (cf. Isa 61), in a good sense, to preach the acceptable year of the Lord and the day of retribution to our God; and now it is taken both in a bad and in a good sense. In a bad sense: For the day of vengeance is in my heart. In a good sense: The year of my redemption has come; so that at the time when the adversaries are punished, the people of God might be set free, nay rather redeemed by the precious blood of the Lamb, who in the Apocalypse of John is said to have been slain. Of this day of retribution Moses too prophesied by the Holy Spirit: And he will render vengeance to his enemies, and will repay those who hate him. I looked round, and there was no helper; I sought, and there was none to give aid (Deut 32:41).

63:5.t: He had also said in the psalm: And I looked for one who would grieve with me, and there was none, and for one who would comfort me, and I found none (Ps 68 [69]:21). For he, though he was in the form of God, did not count it robbery to be equal with God, but emptied himself (Phil 2), taking the form of a servant, and became obedient to the Father unto death, even the death of the cross; and therefore he gave him a name above every name, so that he might save for himself by his right hand those who believe in him, and his indignation, which was against the adversaries, might set the people of God free. Or he rescued the believers by his arm, and no longer put off his fury; and he brought down their blood to the earth, either that of the demons, τροπικῶς, or certainly the blood of the Jews; for which the other translators rendered contention; who strove with all zeal that they might let the bound people go.

63:7.t: I will remember the mercies of the Lord, the praise of the Lord for all that the Lord has rendered to us, and for the multitude of good things to the house of Israel, which he has bestowed on them according to his indulgence and according to the multitude of his mercies. LXX: I have remembered the mercy of the Lord; I will remember the mighty works of the Lord in all that he has rendered to us: the Lord, a good judge to the house of Israel, will repay us according to his mercy and according to the multitude of his righteousness. Now that the passage on the coming of the Savior has been completed, the first coming, as we judge, the second, as most suppose, in which is understood the voice of one judging, nay rather fighting and slaughtering the adversaries of himself and of his people, and in which he is described as bloodied and victorious, another περικοπή begins, in which the Prophet speaks in the person of the people, recounting God's benefits toward it and the hardness of its own heart, on account of which […]

63:8.t: And he said: Surely they are my people, sons who do not deny; and he became their Savior. In all their tribulation he was not troubled, and the Angel of his face saved them; in his love and in his indulgence he himself redeemed them, and he bore them and lifted them up all the days of the age. But they provoked him to anger and afflicted the spirit of his Holy One and he was turned to be their enemy, and he himself fought them down. LXX: And he said: Is it not my people? Sons will by no means reject. And he became their salvation out of all their tribulation; not an envoy nor an angel, but he himself saved them, because he loved them and spared them; he himself redeemed them, and took them up, and exalted them all the days of the age. But they did not believe, and they embittered his Holy Spirit; he was turned to be their enemy, he himself fought against them. […]

63:10.t: But if the prudent reader should answer in silent thought, Why have many not been saved, if he himself saved them, and loved and spared his sons, and redeemed them with his blood, and took them up and exalted them once assumed?, a clear reason is given: But they did not believe, and they embittered his Holy Spirit, or the Spirit of his Holy One, which in Hebrew is CADESO (קדש). God, then, willed to save those who desired it, and he called them to salvation, so that their will might have its reward; but they would not believe. Otherwise it is written of John too: There was a man sent from God, whose name was John; he came to bear witness to the light, that all might believe through him (John 1:6). Nor is he at once at fault if many would not believe; but the will of the one who came was this, that all should believe and be saved. […]

63:11.t: And he remembered the days of the age, of Moses, of his people. Where is he who brought them up out of the sea with the shepherds of his flock? Where is he who put in its midst the Spirit of his Holy One? Who led Moses by the right hand with the arm of his majesty; who divided the waters before them, to make for himself an everlasting name; who led them through the depths like a horse in the desert that does not stumble. Like a beast going down into the plain, the Spirit of the Lord was its leader; so you led your people, to make for yourself a name of glory. LXX: And he remembered the ancient days, he who brought up from the land the shepherd of the sheep. Where is he who put the Holy Spirit in them? Who led Moses by the right hand, the arm of his glory. So he led his people through the mighty water in his sight, to make for himself an everlasting name. He led them through the deep like a horse through the wilderness, and they did not labor. […]

63:13.t: For he led his people through the boundless depths of the waters like a horse through the wilderness, and like cattle over the plain, and the Spirit of the Lord was its leader, that is, of the Lord's flock (Exod 14). By Spirit here we ought to understand the angel who was the leader of the people of Israel, according to what is written: Who makes his angels spirits, and his ministers a burning fire (Ps 103 [104]:4). And in the Epistle to the Hebrews: These are ministering spirits, sent forth to serve for the sake of those who are to possess salvation (Heb 1:14). Let us consider whether what is written in the Acts of the Apostles, The Spirit of the Lord caught away Philip, and the eunuch saw him no more (Acts 8:39), ought to be taken of an angel. There are some who maintain that the angel did these things in the Holy Spirit. We run through what is plain so as to dwell on what is more obscure.

63:14.t: And Isaiah, "The Lord God and His Spirit hath sent me," and "the Spirit came down from the Lord and guided them." And pray do not again understand by this guidance some humble service, for the Word witnesses that it was the work of God;—"Thou leddest thy people," it is said "like a flock," and "Thou that leadest Joseph like a flock," and "He led them on safely, so that they feared not." Thus when you hear that when the Comforter is come, He will put you in remembrance, and "guide you into all truth." do not misrepresent the meaning.

63:15.t: Look down from heaven, and see from your holy dwelling and that of your glory. Where is your zeal and your strength? The multitude of your bowels and of your mercies toward me have held themselves back. For you are our father; and Abraham has not known us, and Israel has been ignorant of us. You, O Lord, are our father, our redeemer from of old is your name. LXX: Turn from heaven, and see from your holy house and that of your glory: where is your zeal and your strength? Where is the multitude of your mercies and of your compassions, with which you bore with us? For you are our father, because Abraham has not known us, and Israel has not known us. But you, O Lord our father, deliver us: from the beginning your name is upon us. You who granted such great things to the people as the preceding discourse has related, so that you even deemed us worthy of the fellowship of your Spirit, now too look down from heaven and see our works, if indeed they are worthy of you. Why do you turn away your face from us? […]

63:16.t: For Thou art our Father, though Abraham be ignorant of us, and Sarah travailed not with us, need we inquire further on this point? And if the Psalmist says, Let them be troubled from His countenance, the Father of the fatherless, and Judge of the widows, is it not manifest to all, that when God is called the Father of orphans who have lately lost their own fathers, He is so named not as begetting them of Himself, but as caring for them and shielding them. But whereas God, as we have said, is in an improper sense the Father of men, of Christ alone He is the Father by nature, not by adoption: and the Father of men in time, but of Christ before all time, as He saith, And now, O Father, glorify Thou Me with Thine own self, with the glory which I had with Thee before the world was.

For you, he says, are our father, you who are the creator of all. Abraham does not know us, and Israel is ignorant of us, because we have offended you, nor do they recognize as sons those whom they perceive not to be loved by their God. A sudden question arises: why did he set down Abraham and Israel, that is, Jacob, and leave the name of Isaac unspoken (Gen 32)? To this we shall answer that, when the beginning and the end are set down, the middle too is named. Or thus: Abraham was called to faith from the nations, and according to the character of his former and his subsequent condition received a change of name. Jacob too reached it only by much toil, to be called Israel. Hence too Abraham had three wives, and Jacob four; but Isaac kept his ancient name from beginning to end, and, signifying the chastity of the Church, was content with one wife. Those, then, who pray for a change from sinners to a better state take on the likeness of those to whom joy succeeded after sorrow. […]

63:17.t: Why have you made us stray, O Lord, from your ways? You have hardened our heart, so that we did not fear you. Return for the sake of your servants, the tribes of your inheritance. As if for nothing they have possessed your holy people; our enemies have trodden down your sanctification. We have become as in the beginning, when you did not rule over us, nor was your name called upon us. LXX: Why have you led us astray, O Lord, from your holy way? You have hardened our hearts, so that we did not fear you. Return for the sake of your servants, for the sake of the tribes of your inheritance, that we may possess a little of your holy mountain; our adversaries have trodden down your sanctuary; we have become as from the beginning, when you did not rule over us, nor was your name called upon us. […]

As for what is set down above, Why have you made us stray (Isa 63:17)?, in what sense it is to be taken Jeremiah teaches most fully: You have led me astray, O Lord, and I was led astray; you took hold of me, and you prevailed (Jer 20:7). For while you promise me mercy, and like a merciful father you conceal your severity, and like a skilful physician you hide the sharpest knife so as not to frighten the sick man before you heal him, you have made me careless. For this reason God says of Jerusalem too: Behold, I will lead her astray, and I will make her like a desert, and set her like a land without water, and I will speak to her heart; and I will give her possessions from there, and the valley of Achor to open understanding (Hos 2:14, 15). Let us consider the order of each thing: he leads her astray, and makes her deserted and without water, so that she may suffer thirst for the virtues. […]

Return, he says, O Lord, or turn us back, for the sake of your servants, Abraham and Israel, who have not known us, or whom we believe to be among the people. For as if for nothing, and without any toil, our adversaries have possessed your holy people. Or, turn us back so that, according to the Seventy, we may possess a little of your holy mountain, since we cannot possess the whole of your mountain; so that when we have had a part we may come to its fullness and contemplate the glory of the Only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth (John 1); of which it is said in this same prophet: In the last days the mountain of the Lord will be manifest (Isa 2:2).

63:18.t: Our enemies, he says, have trodden down your sanctuary. There is no doubt that he means the Temple, which the victorious Romans trod down.

63:19.t: And we have become as in the beginning, before we were called in Abraham, and while we were in Egypt, having no God, nor kings, nor princes, nor Prophets, nor the Law of the commandments of God (Hos 3); all of which was fulfilled after the passion of the Lord, and is being fulfilled today. For since they said, His blood be upon us and upon our children (Matt 27:25), an everlasting curse remains, and God does not rule over them, nor is his name called upon them, since they are by no means called the people of God.

64:1.t: O that you would rend the heavens and come down! At your presence the mountains would flow down. As the burning of fire they would melt away; the waters would burn with fire, so that your name might be made known to your enemies; at your presence the nations would be troubled. When you do wonders, we shall not endure them; you came down, and at your presence the mountains flowed down. LXX: If you open heaven, trembling will seize the mountains because of you; and they will melt as wax melts before the fire, and fire will burn up the adversaries; and your name will be manifest among the adversaries; at your presence the nations will be troubled. When you do glorious things, trembling will seize the mountains because of you. Since our enemies have trodden down your sanctuary, and we have become as in the beginning, when your name was not called upon us, therefore we entreat and say: O that you would rend the heavens and come down, and that you who are always promised would at some time fulfill your promises. […]

64:4.t: But it may be argued that the Apostle was not inspired by the Spirit of prophecy when he borrowed these prophetic words; that he was only interpreting at random the words of another man, and though, no doubt, everything the Apostle says of himself comes to him by revelation from Christ, yet his knowledge of the words of Isaiah is only derived from the book. I answer that in the beginning of that utterance in which it is said that the servants of the true God shall bless Him and swear by Him, we read this adoration by the prophet: "From everlasting we have not heard, nor have our eyes seen God, except Thee, and Thy works which Thou wilt do for them that await Thy mercy." Isaiah says that he has seen no God but Him. For he did actually see the glory of God, the mystery of Whose taking flesh from the Virgin he foretold. […]

From of old they have not heard, nor perceived with their ears; the eye has not seen, O God, besides you, what you have prepared for those who wait for you. You have met him who rejoices and does righteousness in your ways; they will remember you. LXX: From of old we have not heard, nor have our eyes seen a God besides you, and your works, which you will do for those who wait for mercy; for he meets those who do righteousness, and they will remember your ways. A paraphrase of this testimony the apostle Paul, as a Hebrew of the Hebrews, takes from the authentic books in the Epistle which he writes to the Corinthians, not rendering word for word, which he altogether disdains to do, but expressing the truth of the sense, which he uses to support what he wished (1 Cor 2). Let the ravings of the apocrypha, then, fall silent, which on the pretext of this testimony are thrust upon the churches of Christ. Of them it can truly be said that the devil sits in ambush with the rich in the apocrypha, to kill the innocent. […]

Do not thou then, O thou who hast denied the things which are seen, ask what kind of riches thou wilt receive in exchange for thy poverty, but be thou in earnest only to forsake thy poverty, and to hasten to possess them. Now what these riches are, and unto what they are like, Paul explaineth not unto thee, nor of what kind they are, for there is nothing which can be compared with them, nor how much they are, because they cannot be measured. "That which eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, and what hath not gone up in the heart of man, is what God hath prepared for them that love Him"; and the greatness of the reward is made manifest by these and such like words.
64:4.s: 13 Ascetic Discourses, Discourse 9 -- Second Discourse on Poverty

64:5.t: Thou art angry, and we have sinned, says one of old, making confession; and it is now time for me to say the opposite, "We have sinned, and Thou art angry:" therefore have we become a reproach to our neighbours.

Behold, you are angry, and we have sinned; in them we have always been, and we shall be saved. And we have become as one unclean all of us, all our righteousnesses as the cloth of a menstruous woman. And we have all fallen like a leaf, and our iniquities, like the wind, have carried us away. LXX: Behold, you are angry, and we have all sinned; therefore we have gone astray, and we have all become as unclean, all our righteousness as the cloth of a woman who sits apart; and we have fallen away like leaves because of our iniquities; as the wind will carry us away. The order is inverted. It is not because you are angry that we have sinned, but because we have sinned that you are angry. And because we have sinned, you are angry with us, O Lord; therefore we have gone astray and left the right way. Or, according to the Hebrew: we who have always been in sins shall be saved only by your mercy, we who of ourselves are unclean; […]

64:6.t: Finally as our goodness turns to badness in the eyes of the Highest so also our righteousness when set against the Divine righteousness is considered like a menstruous cloth, as Isaiah the prophet says: "All your righteousness is like a menstruous cloth."
64:6.s: The Third Conference of Abbot Theonas, Chapter 4

64:6.t: It is hence that Isaiah laments bitterly, saying, And we all do fade as a leaf; and our iniquities like the wind have taken us away. And there is none that calleth upon Thy Name, that stirreth up himself to take hold of Thee. Now any of the righteous may sometimes be able to resist the visitations of a present judgment, by the merits of a derived innocency, but they have no power by their own goodness to rid mankind of the woes of the death to come. Therefore let the holy man bethink himself whereunto the human race has run out, let him cast his eye on the woes of eternal death, which it is plain that human righteousness can never withstand, let him see how frowardly man has offended, let him see how severely the wrath of the Creator is directed against man, and let him call for the Mediator between God and man, God and Man in one, forasmuch as he beholds Him destined to come long after. ... […]
64:6.s: Morals on the Book of Job, Book 9.38

64:7.t: There is none who calls upon your name, who rises up and takes hold of you. You have hidden your face from us, and have dashed us down in the hand of our iniquity. LXX: And there is none who calls upon your name, and who, remembering, lays hold of you. For you have turned away your face from us, and have handed us over because of our iniquities. Because we have fallen away like leaves from the trees, which the wind scatters when they are dried up, therefore no one has been found who would call upon your name, and, rising from the ruin of his iniquities, would lay hold of you or take hold of you, and say with the bride: I have found him whom my soul sought; I will hold him and will not let him go (Song 3:4). The wind is put in the Scriptures in three ways: either for the greatness of temptations, or for perversity of doctrine, or simply for the wind by which the clouds are gathered and the air is driven together into clouds. […]

64:8.t: And now, O Lord, you are our father, and we are clay; and you are our fashioner, and we are all the works of your hands. Do not be angry, O Lord, exceedingly, and do not remember iniquity any longer. Behold, look: we are all your people. The city of your Holy One has become a desert; Zion has become a desert, Jerusalem desolate. The house of our sanctification and of our glory, where our fathers praised you, has been made a burning of fire, and all our desirable things have been turned into ruin. Will you hold yourself back over these things, O Lord, will you be silent, and afflict us exceedingly? LXX: And now, O Lord, you are our father; but we are clay, we are all the works of your hands. Do not be angry with us, O Lord, too much, and do not remember our sins in time. And now look, for we are all your people; the city of your Holy One has become a desert, Zion; Jerusalem as a wilderness, for a curse; […]

64:10.t: We can refer these things to the Church, or to the soul of a holy man, which can rightly be called a watchtower and vision of peace when the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit have dwelt in it. But if, through our fault or that of the people, such a Zion has been forsaken by the Lord, it will at once lie open to the burning of the fiery arrows of the devil; for all who commit adultery, their hearts are like an oven. And when the coolness of chastity has been driven out, the flame of lust will rage in the temple of God, so that whatever in us was formerly glorious and renowned may collapse, be destroyed and perish. And then is fulfilled what is said in the Psalms: They have burned your sanctuary with fire; they have profaned on the earth the tabernacle of your name. This he alone can quench out of whose belly flow rivers of living water.

And have mercy on the city of your sanctuary, in which your name has been called upon. This city is called Zion and Jerusalem, which the rush of the river makes glad, and in which there was once the watchtower of the virtues and the vision of peace (Ps 43 [44]). Your house too, that is, the Temple of our sanctification and glory, in which our fathers praised you, has fallen into ruins and ashes, and has been destroyed by devastating fire; so that no victims are offered in it, no Passover is celebrated, nothing is done of the ceremonies which you commanded to be done; but all our desirable things have been turned into ruins. Since, then, this is how things stand, will you, O Lord, hold back your mercy over these things, and be silent toward the adversaries who blaspheme, and afflict and humble us, not in the usual manner but exceedingly? All this the Jews think was fulfilled in the times of the Assyrians and the Babylonians. […]

65:1.t: And after that Righteous One was put to death, we flourished as another people, and shot forth as new and prosperous corn; as the prophets said, "And many nations shall betake themselves to the Lord in that day for a people: and they shall dwell in the midst of all the earth." But we are not only a people, but also a holy people, as we have shown already. "And they shall call them the holy people, redeemed by the Lord." Therefore we are not a people to be despised, nor a barbarous race, nor such as the Carian and Phrygian nations; but God has even chosen us and He has become manifest to those who asked not after Him. "Behold, I am God," He says, "to the nation which called not on My name." For this is that nation which God of old promised to Abraham, when He declared that He would make him a father of many nations; not meaning, however, the Arabians, or Egyptians, or Idumaeans, since Ishmael became the father of a mighty nation, and so did Esau; and there is now a great multitude of Ammonites. […]

Who then, one might say to the Jews, is he that was made manifest? For if it is the prophet, let them say just when he was hid, afterward to appear again. And what manner of prophet is this, who was not only openly made manifest from obscurity but also stretched out his hands on the cross? None surely of the righteous, save the Word of God only, who, incorporeal by nature, appeared for our sakes in the body and suffered for all.
65:1.s: On the Incarnation of the Word 38:2

65:1.t: They sought me who before did not ask for me: they found, who did not seek me. I said: Behold me, behold me, to a nation that did not call upon my name. LXX: I appeared to those not seeking me: I was found by those who did not ask for me. I said: Behold me, in a nation that did not call upon my name. To the prayer of the people mingled with complaints, in which it had said: Why have you made us err, O Lord, from your way: you have hardened our hearts, so that we did not fear you (Isa 63:17)? there answers, as the Jews would have it, God the Father; as we hold, the Lord and Savior: So far am I from being harsh and cruel, I who prefer the repentance of the sinner to his death, and do not repel repentant sons, provided they have kept the dignity of their name, that I wish to save even strangers (Ezek 33). For those who did not seek me, and could not say: We have found him of whom Moses wrote in the Law, and the prophets, Jesus (John 1:45), to these very ones I appeared; […]

65:2.t: I have spread out my hands all the day to an unbelieving people, who walk in a way not good, after their own thoughts. LXX: I have spread out my hands all the day to an unbelieving and contradicting people, who have not walked in the good way, but after their sins. This which was said above: I appeared to those who did not ask for me: I was found by those who did not seek me, the apostle Paul, writing to the Romans, when he had expounded it of the person of the nations, added: But to Israel he says: I have spread out my hands to an unbelieving and contradicting people (Rom 10:21); a people which, when it was overcome by the benefits of the Lord and saw signs beyond what a man can do, said: This man does not cast out demons except by Beelzebub, the prince of the demons (Luke 11:15). And again: You are a Samaritan and have a demon (John 8:48). And again: though you are a man, you make yourself God (John 10:33). And elsewhere: This man is not from God, for he does not keep the sabbath (John 9:16). […]

The tree of life which was planted by God in Paradise pre-figured this precious Cross. For since death was by a tree, it was fitting that life and resurrection should be bestowed by a tree. Jacob, when He worshipped the top of Joseph’s staff, was the first to image the Cross, and when he blessed his sons with crossed hands he made most clearly the sign of the cross. Likewise also did Moses’ rod, when it smote the sea in the figure of the cross and saved Israel, while it overwhelmed Pharaoh in the depths; likewise also the hands stretched out crosswise and routing Amalek; and the bitter water made sweet by a tree, and the rock rent and pouring forth streams of water, and the rod that meant for Aaron the dignity of the high priesthood: and the serpent lifted in triumph on a tree as though it were dead, the tree bringing salvation to those who in faith saw their enemy dead, just as Christ was nailed to the tree in the flesh of sin which yet knew no sin. LXX: This people that embitters me in my sight: they always sacrifice in gardens, and burn incense upon brick ÷ to demons that are not. ⁚ Though the Lord says: You shall not make for yourself an idol, nor a likeness of anything that is in heaven, and that is upon the earth. And though through Moses he rebukes those who do so: They provoked me with strange gods, and with their abominations they provoked me to bitterness. They sacrificed to demons, and not to God (Deut 32:16, 17); they, out of a zeal for sinning, as if to irritate and provoke God, not only did what was not lawful, but did it continually and always, sinning in the sight of the Lord, to whose eyes all things lie open, or in his Temple, sacrificing victims to idols. 65:4.t: Who dwell in tombs, and sleep in the shrines of idols: who eat swine's flesh, and profane broth is in their vessels: who say, Depart from me, do not come near me, for you are unclean. LXX: In tombs and in caves they sleep for the sake of dreams: who eat swine's flesh and the broth of victims; all their vessels are profane: who say, Go far from me, do not come near me, for I am clean. There was no sacrilege that the people of Israel left out: not only sacrificing in gardens and kindling frankincense upon bricks, but also sitting, or dwelling, in tombs, and sleeping in the shrines of idols, where they used to lie upon the spread-out skins of victims, so as to learn the future from dreams. This the error of the heathen celebrates to this day in the temple of Aesculapius and in many others, which are nothing else but the tombs of the dead. […]

65:5.t: These shall be a smoke in my fury, a fire burning all the day. Behold, it is written before me: I will not be silent, but I will render and repay into their bosom your iniquities, and the iniquities of your fathers together, says the Lord, who sacrificed upon the mountains and upon the hills, reproached me; and I will measure back their former work into their bosom. LXX: This is the smoke of my fury: a fire burns in it all the days. Behold, it is written in my sight: I will not be silent until I render and repay into their bosom their sins, and those of their fathers, says the Lord: who burned incense upon the mountains and upon the hills, reproached me; I will render their works into their bosom. Because of your works, and the incredible arrogance of your mind, in that, being unclean, you thought the clean unclean, you shall be smoke, a burning fire, which is kindled from my fury. […]

65:6.t: Behold, he says, it is written before me. For all our sins lie open to the eyes of God, and are written in those books of which we read in Daniel: Thrones were set, and the books were opened (Dan 7:10). Of which it is said in another place: Let them be written upon the earth (Jer 17:13). And he will by no means keep silent any longer, he who had said before: I have kept silent: shall I always keep silent? says the Lord (Isa 42:14). But he will render to each what he has worked, into his bosom, that is, into the secret place of the heart, so that their own conscience may torment them. Of this the prophet Hosea too prophesies: Their princes shall fall by the sword because of the unruliness of their tongue (Hos 7:16). This is their own detraction in their bosom, which proceeds from the heart of each. Something similar is written in Proverbs: In their own bosom all things are rendered to the wicked (Prov 5:22). […]

65:7.t: For we ought not to take as fathers, whose iniquities and sins are now repaid to us, those from whose seed our bodies were born. Otherwise Moses himself, who had said that the sins of the fathers are to be repaid to the sons to the third and fourth generation of those who hate God (Exod 20), interprets his own sentence, saying: The sons shall not die for the sins of the fathers: but each shall die in his own sin (Deut 24:16). Ezekiel approves the same sentence, that that parable is by no means to be spoken: The fathers have eaten a sour grape, and the teeth of the sons are set on edge (Ezek 18:2), but that only his teeth are set on edge who has eaten, and that the sinning soul perishes, and does not pay for another's sins. From this we understand that those are to be taken as fathers, whether in the good sense or in the contrary, to whom each is added when he has departed from this life. Now Israel sacrificed upon the mountains and hills when it set up the golden calves in Bethel and Dan. […]

65:8.t:
"8. Thus saith the Lord, as a grape-stone shall be found in the cluster, and they shall say, Destroy it not, for a blessing is in it: so will I for the sake of him that serves me, for his sake I will not destroy all. 9. And I will lead out the seed of Jacob and Juda, and they shall inherit my holy mountain : and my chosen and my servants shall inherit it and dwell there. 10. And there shall be in the forest a fold of sheep, and the valley of Achor shall be a resting-place for the herds of my people, who have sought me.

"11. But ye are they that have left me, and forget my holy mountain and prepare a table for chance, 12. and fill up the drink-offering to the Demon. I will deliver you up to the sword, ye shall all fall by slaughter, because I called you and ye did not hear, and did evil before me, and chose that which I willed not."

In this passage the Scripture distinguishes, and says that but a small seed from Jacob will attain the promises, and that the elect are those that dwell in the wood. […]

65:8.t: Thus says the Lord: As if a grain is found in a cluster, and it is said: Do not destroy it, for it is a blessing; so will I do for the sake of my servants, that I may not destroy the whole. LXX: Thus says the Lord: As if a grape is found in a cluster, and it is said: Do not touch it, for there is a blessing in it: so will I do for the sake of my servant, that I may not destroy all. The Lord had said that Israel would perish, and that all its sins lay open to his sight, and that he would repay the works of each into their bosom. After this he brings in a likeness and an example by comparison, to teach that each perishes by his own sin, and that, even if the multitude of sinners be very great, one righteous man does not perish through the vice of all. 65:9.t: And I will bring forth a seed out of Jacob, and out of Judah one possessing my mountains: and my elect shall inherit it, and my servants shall dwell there, and the plains shall be folds for flocks, and the valley of Achor a resting place for herds, for my people who have sought me. LXX: And I will bring forth a seed out of Jacob, and out of Judah, and it shall inherit my holy mountain, and my elect shall inherit, and my servants shall dwell there, and in the woodland there shall be sheepfolds for flocks, and the valley of Achor for the rest of herds, for my people who have sought me out. Him whom above he called the grain of the cluster, or the grape, or (as many would have it) the bunch, he now calls the seed of Jacob and Judah, who is to possess the mountains, or his mountain. Most understand the seed of Jacob and Judah as Christ, of whom it is said in Genesis: Judah, your brothers shall praise you (Gen 49:8), and the rest. For no one doubts that the Savior was born of the stock of Judah. […]

65:10.t: And there shall be, he says, plains, or woodlands, as folds for flocks. For plains, SARON (שרון) is put in the Hebrew. The whole region around Lydda, Joppa and Jamnia is suited to pasturing flocks. Of it it is also written in the Acts of the Apostles: But the woodlands shall be turned into sheepfolds (Acts 9), according to what is sung in the psalm: The voice of the Lord perfecting the stags, and he will lay bare the woodlands (Ps 28 [29]:9), or the thickets of the forests, so that robbers may cease to lurk there, and beasts and venomous animals, and places once of ambush and blood may pass into churches of the Lord, and flocks may be pastured there by him who laid down his life for his sheep. Of whom it is written: He will shepherd us forever (Ps 47 [48]:15). This voice of the Lord, perfecting the stags and laying bare the thickets of the forests, cries out through John in the desert: Already the axe is laid to the root of the trees. […]

65:11.t: And you who have forsaken the Lord, and have forgotten my holy mountain; who set a table for fortune, and pour libations upon it: I will number you for the sword, and you shall all fall in the slaughter. LXX: But you who have forsaken me, and have forgotten my holy mountain, and prepare a table for fortune, and fill a drink for the demon: I will hand you over to the sword: you shall all fall slain. In places once wooded and full of trouble, in the places of the Gentiles, there will be folds for the sheep, that is, the Churches of believers from the whole world. But you, O people of Israel, who have forsaken the Lord and provoked the Holy One of Israel to anger, who have forgotten his holy mountain, of which we have often spoken, whether the Lord Savior, who is the mountain of mountains and the holy one of all the holy, or Mount Zion and the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem: you who do this and that, I will hand over to the sword, so that you may all fall slain together. 65:12.t: Because I called, and you did not answer; I spoke, and you did not hear: but you did evil in my eyes, and what I did not will, you chose. LXX: Because I called you, and you did not hear: I spoke, and you despised, and you did evil in my sight, and what I did not will you chose. You have been handed over to the sword, he says, because you have not only forsaken me and forgotten me and mixed a cup for fortune, but when I was Emmanuel, that is, God with us, of whom John too writes: The Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us (John 1:14), I called you, present among you: Return to me, returning sons (Jer 3:14). And: Come to me, all you who labor and are burdened (Matt 11:28); and you would not answer. I spoke in parables, and did all that I ought to do, and you did not hear me, nay, you even despised me. For I am he who said above as well: I came, and there was no man: I called, and there was none to obey (Isa 50:2). Nor was this impiety enough for you, to despise me when I was present, and to kill the heir sent to you; […]

65:13.t: Therefore thus says the Lord God: Behold, my servants shall eat, and you shall be hungry. Behold, my servants shall drink, and you shall be thirsty. Behold, my servants shall rejoice, and you shall be put to shame. Behold, my servants shall give praise for exultation of heart, and you shall cry out for sorrow of heart, and for contrition of spirit you shall howl. LXX: Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, my servants shall eat, but you shall be hungry. Behold, my servants shall drink, but you shall be thirsty. Not only shall you fall by the sword, you who have forsaken the Lord and done evil in his sight and would not hear him when he was present, but you shall see a great difference between yourselves and the multitude of the nations. 65:14.t: And the contrition of spirit for sorrow of heart is to be understood of the conscience of sins, according to what is written: Those who err in spirit shall know understanding (Isa 29:24). And: A contrite and humbled heart, O God, you will not despise (Ps 50 [51]:19). The spirit is crushed when it has been lifted up; as is written of a king hostile to Israel: The Lord hardened his spirit (2 Kgs 17:14). And of the prince of the Babylonians, when his heart was lifted up and his spirit hardened, so that he said in his pride: This is Babylon, and I have made it (Dan 4:27).

65:15.t:
On them Scripture now proceeds to prophesy that a new name shall be conferred, saying to the wicked :

"For your name shall be left, as a loathing for my chosen, and the Lord shall destroy you : but my servants shall be called by a new name."

And this new name, which was not known to them of old time, what could it be but the name of "Christians," blessed through all the world, formed from the name of our Saviour Jesus Christ?
65:15.s: The Proof of the Gospel, Book 2, Chapter 3

65:15.t:
It is admitted that when in recent times the appearance of our Saviour Jesus Christ had become known to all men there immediately made its appearance a new nation; a nation confessedly not small, and not dwelling in some corner of the earth, but the most numerous and pious of all nations, indestructible and unconquerable, because it always receives assistance from God. This nation, thus suddenly appearing at the time appointed by the inscrutable counsel of God, is the one which has been honored by all with the name of Christ.

One of the prophets, when he saw beforehand with the eye of the Divine Spirit that which was to be, was so astonished at it that he cried out, "Who hath heard of such things, and who hath spoken thus? Hath the earth brought forth in one day, and hath a nation been born at once?" And the same prophet gives a hint also of the name by which the nation was to be called, when he says, "Those that serve me shall be called by a new name, which shall be blessed upon the earth."

With the ungrudging generosity of his godhead, Christ has granted to all of us to bear his name. For whereas as human sovereigns have some special title of sovereignty that they keep exclusively from use by other people, Jesus Christ, being Son of God, has deigned to bestow on us the title of Christians.… But some will say, "The name of 'Christians' is new and was not previously in use": and new-fashioned phrases are often objected to on the score of strangeness. The prophet made this point safe beforehand, saying, "But on my servants shall a new name be called, which shall be blessed upon the earth."

And you shall leave your name for an oath to my elect, and the Lord God shall slay you, and he shall call his servants by another name, in which he who is blessed upon the earth shall be blessed in God, amen: and he who swears in the earth shall swear in God, amen. LXX: For you shall leave your name for satiety to my elect. But you the Lord shall slay: and to those who serve me a new name shall be called, which shall be blessed upon the earth: for they shall bless the true God, and those who swear upon the earth shall swear by the true God. For satiety, which in Hebrew is called SABAA (שבועה), the others translated oath; this word has many meanings and varies with the difference of accents. For it is understood as oath, and fullness, and satiety, and many, and seven. Of this we spoke in the book on Genesis, and in this volume (cf. Isa 4), where seven women took hold of one man. Again, where the Seventy translated true, and in the Hebrew it is said AMEN (אמן), Aquila rendered πεπιστωμένως, that is, faithfully. […]

65:16.t: For the former distresses have been given over to oblivion, and because they are hidden from my eyes. For behold, I create new heavens and a new earth, and the former things shall not be in memory: and it shall not come up upon the heart: but you shall rejoice and exult forever in the things that I create. LXX: For they shall forget the former tribulation, and it shall not come up upon their heart. For there shall be a new heaven and a new earth: and they shall not remember the former things, and they shall not come upon their heart; but they shall find joy and exultation in it. The cause of the gladness and of the confession of the true God is that an eternal oblivion of the former distresses will follow, so that they will by no means remember the idols and their ancient error, but will pass from darkness to light, so as to enjoy eternal blessedness.
